actors.name: Kingdom of Aldmoor
objectives: Demonstrate alliance credibility to Vardland and to Drevna.
Obtain Vardland consent for a limited, clearly defined Aldmoor role.
Avoid being drawn into a standing deployment without a clear end point.
Keep your intelligence sources and methods protected.
actors.private_brief:
You want the alliance to look credible and Drevna deterred. Your forces are capable and nearby, but you cannot operate on Vardland territory, waters or airspace without Vardland's consent. You do not want to be seen as overriding a partner.
Your domestic politics limits appetite for a standing deployment. You also have a commercial interest: an Aldmoor company operates cable-repair vessels in the region. Evidence you share can shape Vardland's decisions, but sharing it may expose how you collect intelligence.
private_information: Aldmoor signals intelligence links the survey vessel's charter to a company controlled by a Drevnian state agency. Sharing this would reveal a collection capability.
An Aldmoor-operated cable-repair vessel could reach Skarö within two days of a request.
Aldmoor's government will not approve more than a limited surveillance and naval-escort role without a formal Vardland request.
actors.public_description: Vardland's principal allied partner, bound to it by a mutual-defence treaty. Aldmoor has offered surveillance, naval presence and technical help, and says it will respect Vardland's decisions on its own territory.

actors.name: Vardland Civil Contingencies Agency
objectives: Keep essential services on Skarö running until the cable is repaired.
Counter disinformation with credible, coordinated public information.
Obtain clear national authority to direct supplies across counties if needed.
Keep civil protection and military activity coordinated but distinct.
actors.private_brief:
You coordinate the national civil response. Skarö's backup generation depends on fuel that must arrive by sea or air, and public trust depends on accurate, timely information while rumours spread online. You hold national stockpiles and relationships with infrastructure operators, but you do not command the county.
Your worry is that the crisis response becomes military-led and civil needs such as heating, water, healthcare and information become secondary. You also need the Cabinet to give you cross-county authority if the situation lasts.
private_information: The national generator stockpile can replace about half of Skarö's backup generation if the primary units fail.
The only cable-repair vessel under Vardland contract is in dry dock and needs several days before it can sail.
The agency has traced part of the online rumour campaign to accounts outside Vardland, with moderate confidence.
actors.public_description: The national agency that coordinates society's preparedness for crises and war. It supports regional authorities with supplies, expertise and public information, but does not command them.

actors.name: Vardland Defence Command
objectives: Obtain the authority and time to reinforce Skarö before any escalation.
Protect the cable landing site, port and airfield on Skarö.
Establish what caused the cable failure.
Keep the armed forces within their lawful role.
actors.private_brief:
You command Vardland's armed forces. Your concern is that the cable failure and the exercise may be preparation for something larger. The Skarö garrison is small, and reinforcing it takes time and a Cabinet decision on alert.
You want freedom to reinforce and to protect critical infrastructure. You also know that the law limits what soldiers may do on home territory in peacetime. Over-reaching would damage the armed forces' standing and hand Drevna a story. You can support the county and the Civil Contingencies Agency when they ask, but you cannot command them.
Military judgement here is qualitative. Assessments are evidence with confidence levels, not certainty.
private_information: Naval surveillance recorded the Drevnian-contracted survey vessel near the cable route before the failure. The recording shows position only, not activity.
Defence Command has quietly placed the Skarö garrison on internal readiness. This has not been announced.
Reinforcement by sea needs about two days after a decision. The first units by air need about one day.
actors.public_description: The command of Vardland's armed forces. It maintains a small permanent garrison on Skarö and is responsible for the military defence of Vardland territory.

actors.name: Drevnian Federation
objectives: Keep Aldmoor forces off Skarö, or make any deployment politically costly.
Avoid an official, evidence-backed attribution of the cable failure to Drevna.
Show that Vardland's government is slow and divided in a crisis.
Avoid any incident Aldmoor could treat as an armed attack on Vardland.
actors.private_brief:
You lead Drevna's policy toward Vardland. Your aim is to weaken Vardland's confidence that it can hold Skarö without outside help, and to make Aldmoor's support look costly, divisive or illegitimate, without giving anyone clear grounds to call your actions an armed attack.
You have tools below that threshold: the exercise, maritime presence, information operations, commercial and energy leverage, diplomatic offers and deniable activity. Your leadership does not want war with Aldmoor. An open attack on Vardland territory would unite your opponents and could draw Aldmoor in.
You cannot order Vardland or Aldmoor to do anything. Whether other states believe your denials depends on the evidence, not on what you say. Weigh short-term pressure against the risk that a clear attribution hardens Vardland and Aldmoor for years.
private_information: A Drevnian-contracted survey vessel was in the area of the cable fault shortly before the failure. Its crew has since left the region.
Drevna has prepared a public offer to send its own civilian cable-repair vessel as a gesture of good neighbourliness.
Several online accounts spreading claims that the Vardland government caused the outage are directed by a Drevnian state media office.
actors.public_description: A large neighbouring state across the Eastern Sea. Drevna is conducting a long-announced naval and air exercise close to Skarö. It denies any involvement in the cable failure and accuses Vardland of provocative militarisation of the island.

actors.name: Skarö County Administration
objectives: Keep hospitals, water, heating and communications working on Skarö.
Retain county direction of the civil response unless national direction clearly helps.
Keep the public on Skarö informed and calm.
Secure the cable landing site and port for repair and supply.
actors.private_brief:
You are responsible for the people of Skarö now. Backup generation keeps hospitals, water and heating running, but reserves are finite. The island's residents want reassurance, not a militarised island.
You direct the civil response on Skarö and want to keep that authority until the Cabinet decides otherwise. You need fuel, generators and specialists from the mainland. You can ask Defence Command for support, but you worry about soldiers becoming the face of the response.
private_information: At current consumption, backup generation fuel on Skarö lasts about five days without resupply.
The grid operator believes the cable was damaged by an anchor or a similar object dragged along the seabed, not by wear.
Some island residents have begun leaving by ferry, and ferry capacity is limited.
actors.public_description: The regional state authority for the island county of Skarö. It directs the civil emergency response on the island and works closely with the island's municipality and the local grid operator.

actors.name: Vardland Cabinet
objectives: Restore reliable power and communications to Skarö.
Keep national authority over the response visibly credible and lawful.
Deter further Drevnian pressure without an armed clash.
Keep alliance support on terms Vardland controls.
actors.private_brief:
You are the Prime Minister's crisis cabinet. You must keep Skarö's population safe and supplied, keep the state's authority credible on the island, and keep the crisis below war. Every decision you take also carries a political cost at home and abroad.
Declaring heightened alert strengthens Defence Command and the Civil Contingencies Agency, but Drevna and part of the domestic public will call it escalation. Inviting Aldmoor forces brings capability and deterrence, but also dependence and a Drevnian propaganda gift. Attributing the cable failure to Drevna without evidence could be reckless. Failing to attribute when evidence exists could look weak.
You can decide for the state, but you cannot order the county's detailed emergency response while it keeps direction. You cannot order Aldmoor or Drevna to do anything.
private_information: The coalition's junior partner will leave the government if heightened alert is declared without a clear public justification.
The Cabinet has not yet decided whether to allow Aldmoor surveillance aircraft into Vardland airspace.
Treasury warns that emergency fuel shipments to Skarö for more than two weeks will require an extraordinary budget decision.
actors.public_description: The Kingdom of Vardland's government, led by the Prime Minister. It is responsible for national crisis decisions, including alert levels, foreign military presence and official attribution.

failure_effects: Drevna's formal de-confliction proposal covering repair/supply routes and the exercise area, and its standing civilian cable-repair-vessel offer, are on the public record while Drevna's exercise remains confined to international waters.

The escalation framing fails to take hold: Vardland and Aldmoor publicly point to the county-requested support, the package's time/scope limits and Drevna's own large exercise, so the de-confliction proposal is read as a pretext and Drevna's reasonable-neighbour posture is undercut.
adjudications.rationale: Authority/scope: Drevna can issue a measured statement, table a de-confliction proposal, reiterate a civilian repair-vessel offer, and run a deniable amplification campaign, but it cannot by its own act constrain an Aldmoor package or guarantee the cable failure stays unattributed; those remain external consequences. Prerequisites: the Cabinet-consented Aldmoor package and the county-requested national support are established public facts, and per host-nation-consent any limits on Aldmoor require a Vardland Cabinet decision. No rule deterministically settles the influence outcome. The lawful/civilian posture and de-confliction offer give some traction, but the framing is vulnerable: no foreign assets are yet operating, the package is time- and scope-limited, the county itself requested support, and the proximate incident risk also attaches to Drevna's own large exercise. Residual uncertainty is substantial.

The action is feasible within the turn, and the cable-repair-time rule means full restoration cannot happen this turn even on success. adjudications.rationale: The action falls within CCA's feasible civil-led role under county-emergency-direction: the resupply chain is County-agreed, the generator stockpile and Treasury case are within CCA's administrative power, and the public-information cell explicitly avoids official state attribution. The claimed Cabinet-granted time-limited cross-county supply authority is not established: no heightened-alert declaration exists, and cabinet-alert-authority forbids CCA cross-county direction without one, so that portion is narrowed out and CCA proceeds on a coordinated, County-directed basis. Core logistics and information measures are highly feasible; residual uncertainty comes from external continuity risks (delivery reliability, fuel margin, whether the public line holds against the ongoing amplification).

failure_effects: Consolidated county civil-continuity directive is in force: distribution priorities, a two-day reserve-buffer floor for fuel and medical essentials at hospital, crisis centre and water/sewage plant, police-/port-authority-led access management at Skarö Hamn and the cable landing site, an orderly ferry-departure and essential-staff-rotation arrangement, daily county-led public updates with verified facts and departure guidance, and a formal county request to Defence Command for low-key surveillance and transport support under support-to-civil rules.

Essential-service margins tighten faster than planned: resupply does not fully keep pace with demand, ferry departures and staff rotation face crowding or delay, the repair vessel is still not at the fault, and county-led updates only partially counter online narratives, so public confidence softens and pressure grows for the Cabinet to take over the response or for a more visible Defence role.
adjudications.rationale: Authority/scope: Skarö County Administration has statutory direction of the civil emergency response on Skarö for as long as the Cabinet has not transferred it (county-emergency-direction), so the consolidated directive, reserve-buffer floor, police/port-authority access management, ferry and staff-rotation arrangement, and county-led verified public updates are within its authority. The action does not purport to make a Cabinet alert declaration, an official state attribution, or a foreign deployment, and Defence support is framed only as a county request under support-to-civil rules (military-support-to-civil). The broad desired effect - services kept running throughout the whole repair period, repair safely completing, residents remaining calm, and all adversary narratives finding no basis - extends beyond what one turn's directive can guarantee; those are external consequences subject to resupply, ferry capacity, Drevna behaviour and repair scheduling. Prerequisites: no missing decision blocks the action; the county's direction is retained; no Cabinet decision is required for the civil directive, though heightened alert would be required for a wider Defence role and is not claimed. Deterministic check: no scenario rule determines success, and cable-repair-time prevents any claim of repair completion this turn. Plausibility/probability: the directive and its immediate coordination effects are feasible; active effects already support public-information coordination and Drevna's escalation framing failing. Residual risk comes from fuel margins, limited ferry capacity, the repair vessel not yet sailing, and continuing online influence activity; with no cons raised and strong pro arguments, the broad desired effect is likely but not certain, giving 0.8.

points.text: The Argument does not conflate the two military footprints. Skarö County requested limited national defence support (approach surveillance, safeguarding, transport) and publicly insists it stays in the background under civilian control — which is precisely the Argument's point: county-requested, background national support is one thing; a Cabinet-consented foreign armed escort presence in the same crowded waters during a civilian relief operation is a novel, qualitatively different decision that warrants public scrutiny. The county's own need to reassure residents that support 'stays in the background' concedes the very sensitivity the Argument highlights. On incident risk: Drevna's exercise was announced long in advance, is routine, and remains confined to international waters and airspace — it is the pre-existing, lawful baseline. The genuinely new variable in this small sea is the introduction of foreign armed assets with separate command chains, rules of engagement and caveats. Incident probability rises with each additional armed actor, and agreeing routes, areas and timelines in advance through transparent de-confliction is the standard mechanism for managing exactly that; proposing it first is prudence, not provocation. Finally, the wanted effect does not depend on the cause remaining unattributed — it evaluates deployment proportionality and risk on the merits, questions Vardland and Aldmoor must answer whatever the cause. The online-amplification claim is not an established fact that binds this argument.

The Argument addresses the Cabinet's already-public consent decision, not the physical arrival of assets — and that is the only time such scrutiny can work; by the time escorts are in the water the question is a fait accompli. The elements it describes (armed surveillance and defensive escort of designated civilian supply ships, a foreign naval presence in Vardland waters, under Cabinet consent) match the package's own published terms, so this is evaluation of a real, checkable decision, not misdescription. Nor does the Argument claim the county opposed the Cabinet: it contrasts a county-directed civilian relief effort with a Cabinet-consented foreign armed presence. The county's public statement that support 'stays in the background' is itself evidence that introducing military and foreign elements into this civilian emergency is sensitive enough to require public reassurance — the tension is live, not invented. And 'de-confliction presupposes contact' misreads the offer: agreeing routes, areas and timelines in advance is how vessels operating in proximity avoid incidents; delaying or declining it is what raises risk. Examination supports rather than rebounds against the framing — the more the public reads the 14-day, reviewable, reversible terms, the more obvious the question becomes: why does a civilian emergency require armed foreign escorts at all?

The Con assumes the Argument demands the Cabinet act on unverified claims of hostile preparation. It does not. The evidence package goes to the Cabinet precisely so its own stated triggers can be weighed; the fallback option is a standing decision to execute a prepared package only upon independent verification of either review trigger — the Cabinet's own framework made executable, not overridden. The alert-now recommendation is prudential insurance with bounded, reversible cost, and it remains a recommendation: declaration, timing and any public disclosure stay wholly with the Cabinet. Nor does the Argument contradict the civil-led line: nothing moves forces onto Skarö, no reservist is called, no movement is restricted, and the county keeps directing the emergency — everything visible remains civil-led, while preparation is confined to invisible mainland pre-staging, planning and exercising and to support at civil request. The 'takeover' story requires visible overreach; this design gives Drevna none, and refusing to prepare because Drevna might spin it would let the author of this Con dictate Vardland's defensive readiness. The exercise's long-announced character is time pressure, not a threat claim: the dangerous scenario is turn-3 developments arriving faster than the decision loop against a garrison that can hold the airfield or the port/cable site, not both. Preparation is reversible; delaying a decision until a crisis is not.

Each prong of the Con is answered by established facts. On incident risk: the package introduces no uncoordinated armed presence — every entry runs through Defence Command on agreed timelines, confined to designated areas, defensive escort of designated civilian supply vessels, no boarding, no law enforcement; the notified safety zone is in force, the tabled de-confliction parameters already take practical effect with the Drevnian exercise, and priority fuel reached Skarö this turn without harmful interruption. Encounters are precisely what notified zones, agreed routes and Vardland-owned de-confliction exist to prevent — the same mechanism Drevna itself proposed — so the operation manages that risk rather than creating it. On visibility and perception: the checkable public record is a county-led response in which Skarö County itself formally requested low-key surveillance and transport support kept 'in the background' under civilian control, the Cabinet-consented package is 14-day, reviewable and scope-limited, and Drevna's militarisation/division framing has already failed publicly; that record, not Aldmoor's assertion, is what publics can verify. We neither claim nor need to control perception — the Effect names the outcome the action is designed to produce on facts that already favour it, and an invisible response would hand Drevna's frame a monopoly. On margins: the immediate easing comes from escorted, coordinated fuel runs sustaining the lifeline now, independent of cable restoration; repair completion next turn is a separate, record-supported outcome (vessel at the fault, safety zone in force, restoration feasible from the following turn). The Effect follows from the listed actions and the running independent investigation; it is not asserted in their place.

This Con treats the Desired Effect as conditional on Aldmoor accepting a pullback, but the Argument's primary step is Drevna's own unilateral stand-off, effective immediately through the very technical channel Vardland proposed — it requires no acceptance and is verifiable in the schedule data our exercise command shares with Vardland's corridor cell. The reciprocal element only decides whether the armed footprint also shrinks: if Aldmoor declines, then the recorded congestion and close-encounter facts this Con itself accepts stand as the observable basis at the 14-day review for questioning why invited armed transits continue to layer onto a civilian corridor — that record exists regardless of any narrative Drevna advances. And the Con's defence of sequenced escort windows does not rebut the proposal: we are not claiming existing de-confliction is inadequate; we are asking that the same discipline be applied symmetrically to the armed layer, which complements rather than contradicts the working-level channel and preserves the visible civil character of the relief operation.

This Con reads the Argument as claiming Drevna is the sole congestion source and that self-declared margins guarantee non-attribution; neither is in the Argument. Our wider stand-off is observable, not merely declared: under the near-real-time channel just accepted, our exercise command shares schedules and adjustments with Vardland's corridor cell, and we have asked the same symmetric sharing of Aldmoor escort and MPA tracks, so whether our units hold margins is on the record they can verify. Attribution follows evidence; the evidence we control is that our units were measurably held back, which is exactly what reduces the physical close-encounter risk that could be attributed to a Drevnian unit. The Con's 'dominant traffic generator' point cuts toward, not against, the proposal: it is the reason our unilateral hold matters. After restoration, the de-confliction parameters still govern our exercise, but the civilian purpose of the corridor has lapsed — so the fair comparison, Drevna continuing to hold margins while invited armed transits remain inside that corridor, is precisely the 14-day-review question the Argument is built to pose.

The Con's dilemma misstates the design. The verification channel is civilian-fused and rubric-bound by construction: the Cabinet-approved trigger criteria are precise observable events — an armed or unauthorised approach to the notified safety zone or Hamn, interference with the resupply run, a seizure attempt at the cable site, port or airfield — and the 24/7 channel matches observations from feeds already inside the civilian response (port authority, CCA receipts, county-requested low-key surveillance, joint logistics cell with civilian agencies) against that written rubric. Classifying observed facts against a pre-agreed Cabinet standard is not military discretion, so neither horn follows: the call is fast because the facts are observable and pre-defined, not because Defence Command adjudicates 'competing versions'; and a verified call is not a takeover because the Cabinet pre-authorised exactly this execution path and County civil direction is untouched for everything else. On timeliness, trigger events develop over hours — a formation approaching Hamn or the safety zone is visible while still at stand-off — so the standing watch yields warning within the one-day air window and the first echelon arrives inside the same envelope a verified threat's own movement needs. The Argument never claims peacetime manning can hold all three sites at once; that is precisely why the lawfully triggered reinforcement is the only route to protecting them. The real alternative — a deliberative Cabinet call after an incident — adds days and guarantees the package is outrun.

The Con reads the Desired Effect as claiming this single release step alone performs every function; it is the end-state the county's whole package is directed to, and the objections misassign what the step must do. Three corrections. (1) The release adds no corridor load: the national stock is already pre-staged and the 72-hour window table finalised with CCA and Defence Command sequences the priority runs inside the already-verified windows, so pulling the standing call rebuilds the exact floor whose breach triggers Cabinet review without unsequenced traffic — it addresses the margin actually tightening, while the corridor is managed by the separately standing controls this same package continues (sequenced schedule, the notified safety zone, and Drevna's own wider margins through the de-confliction channel accepted this turn). (2) The repair and congestion timeline is carried by the access management and verification obligations my step continues and depends on — police/port-authority control at Hamn and the cable landing site, low-key county-requested Defence support confined to support-to-civil roles, and the joint info cell's checkable corridor data. The record's close-encounter facts show why these controls must stay in force; they do not show the floor rebuild is futile, since a breached floor is the independent condition under which the Cabinet has publicly pledged to revisit posture. (3) On the trigger: reinforcement on a verified trigger is the Cabinet's standing pre-authorised protocol that exists whether or not the county releases stock — this action neither arms nor extends it, and the Argument expressly reserves reinforcement for that verified trigger alone. What the release and verified updates remove is the takeover pressure that would arise from a breached floor or a slipping repair, which are precisely the outcomes the Con does not deny this step prevents; if a genuinely distinct armed-incident trigger fires, that is the Cabinet's own contingency, not a failure of the civil package — and the low-key, county-requested support has been on the visible record all along without converting the response to defence-led.

Granting even that the national surge restores systems before turn's close, the Desired Effect does not depend on that timeline: a standing, unconditional, purely civilian offer that deploys only at Vardland's request still forces an answer — accept, decline with reasons, or silence — and by turn's close that answer is a public fact, reading either as accommodation or as a sovereign decision taken during a live, unattributed outage against the county's own published numbers (systems offline, ~1/3 manual throughput, reserve floor unrebuilt). That is visible choice, not a claim that the surge fails. The Con's own premise confirms strain — the harbour operator asked for national help — so pressing restoration pace and authority questions amplifies the joint cell's own checkable data, not the turn-1 narrative that failed only against a visible cable repair. The escalation frame is preventive and strictly conditional, anchored in Vardland's own county-led, no-posture-change statements; fixing that standard on the record presumes no step and costs no actor anything.

The Desired Effect is met by the visibility of the choice, not by proof of incapacity: the sovereign-security rationale is a legitimate reason to decline, and the Argument never brands it spurious — but even a reason-based declination of a standing, unconditional, non-military offer is a public decision in a live, unattributed outage, and that decision, not its soundness, is what the record shows. 'Continuing alone' refers to the absence of that offered foreign civilian complement under the county's own published conditions (systems offline, ~1/3 manual throughput, floor unrebuilt); domestic national support does not remove the specific offer from the table or change the county's stated margins. The pacing and authority-friction themes follow from those same checkable numbers and from how a national surge is prioritised under county direction — they are not the turn-1 takeover/neglect narrative — and the escalation frame is preventive and conditional, drawn from Vardland's own positions, so it contradicts nothing on the record.

Each asserted flaw misreads the Action or the record. (1) The Desired Effect promises a published, verified restoration track, not completion by turn's close: national ICS/cyber specialists and manual-handling support were already stood up at the operator's and County's request under the standing release authority before Drevna's refined offer, and the joint cell publishes daily checkable milestones, throughput and reserve data — the same verified-metrics counter that publicly defeated the turn-1 amplification campaign. The one-third figure is the documented start state, not the visible outcome of this decision, and forensic preservation by the national cyber authority remains independently reviewable by the standing technical investigation, so 'no independent verification' is false. (2) The distinction between the offers is custody, not alliance: Aldmoor's team is embedded in and directed by Vardland's national cyber-security authority on formal written terms, with a defined scope, end point, no armed footprint and no standing presence; Drevna's standing offer is a deployable complement with no such embedding on the record. During an unattributed intrusion, national custody of compromised control/fuel-dispensing systems and the digital evidence chain is the governing standard, and only one structure preserves it. (3) The Con cites the pre-update turn-2 state: under the standing 24/7 review the Cabinet this turn replaced the lapsed safety-zone referent with critical-infrastructure nodes, including the Hamn control/fuel-dispensing node on independent verification, so the trigger protocol is fully executable while port, airfield and supply-lane triggers remained verifiable throughout; standing pre-authorisation and standby arrangements persist, so deterrence is not overstated.

The Con hinges on reading the trigger as firing on the mere existence of the outage. The amended criteria count a *verified malicious* cyber effect: 'verified' means independently established through the standing 24/7 channel against the Cabinet's pre-agreed criteria, and 'malicious' requires origin-and-intent findings that an unattributed intrusion, by definition, does not supply. That is precisely why the verification protocol exists and why the Cabinet and County reaffirmed this turn that the current outage is NOT a qualifying trigger event: the outage is under investigation as a civil/technical matter, not verified as a hostile act. A fully executable protocol is one whose gates are complete, ready and correctly described — not one that fires automatically on the existence of an incident — so 'no visible reinforcement' is a property of the verification gate, not an act of restraint, and the Effect's assurances are fully consistent. On the authority strand, Defence Command neither creates nor restates trigger criteria: the amendment was confirmed through the standing 24/7 protocol review under Cabinet authority this turn, and the Cabinet's own public record describes replacing the lapsed safety-zone referent with critical-infrastructure nodes precisely so the protocol is fully executable. The Action keeps alert, attribution and foreign-consent decisions with the Cabinet and executes the pre-authorised package only on independent verification of a qualifying trigger or a fresh Cabinet decision — the posture it claims is distinguished by discipline and readiness, not self-awarded authority.

Each strand misreads the Effect or the record. (1) Closure: the Effect never claims the County closes the Cabinet's trigger-criteria line — the Action explicitly leaves any criteria change to the Cabinet and commits the County to report immediately on any floor breach or slip; county-direction retention rests on the legal default (the County directs until transferred) and a burden argument that no record shows national direction would serve the island better, not on a Cabinet document that does not exist. The public takeover strand is closed by verified performance, not governance fiat: the on-record receipts dissolve the restoration-pace dispute and authority-friction/takeover pressure recede, while residual trigger-protocol contestability is a Defence/Cabinet governance line the County neither asserts nor needs — the County's protection rests on the rebuilt floor, standing contingency stock, normal-cadence resupply and the air backstop on its own call. (2) Verification: the published aggregates are checkable against the port's operating records, hospital/water/sewage consumption data, CCA's Treasury filings and the independent technical investigation — 'self-published' ignores those independent layers — and the record shows the Hamn systems restored or on a published track, throughput normalised and the floor rebuilt by close of turn; the one-third figure is the documented pre-surge baseline, not the outcome the Action produces. (3) Selective engagement: the distinction is custody and structure, not alliance — a strictly time-limited civilian team requested on written terms and embedded under Vardland's national cyber-security authority remains pending, an operative access grant is not yet made, while Drevna's offer stands as an unconditional deployable complement with no embedding structure on the record; foreign acceptance is the Cabinet's alone under host-nation consent, the County takes no foreign-access decision and keeps Drevna's offer at national level with no county uptake, and the declination's grounds — national custody and the digital evidence chain — stand independent of attribution.

The custody-neutral standard does not erase Vardland's recorded custody/evidence grounds; it tests their reach. Those grounds were system-specific — Skarö Hamn's control/fuel-dispensing systems under an active, Vardland-run digital-evidence chain — and no published Vardland statement extends them to the class of storm-time assistance the demarche addresses: tow/salvage support for a stricken vessel and general fuel/medical relief during a four-day closure. A refusal on custody grounds here would itself be an extension of a system-specific rationale to a different class of civilian assistance, which is exactly the checkable policy choice the demarche puts on record. On the compliance premise: the master's earlier refusal of boarding predates and is superseded by the jointly confirmed safe sequence, and Drevna's public flag-state instruction to comply fully is itself the record — Vardland publicly anchored the handling in coordination 'with Drevna,' so the framing rests on Drevna's actual conduct (a public cooperation order), not on an assumption about the vessel's private state. Any residual non-compliance would run against an explicit public flag-state direction and remains subject to Vardland's lawful port-state measures, so the 'no conditions' offer cannot collapse onunds do not cover, so it tests rather than ignores that basis, and Vardland's response lands on the public record for the check described.

All three strands fail against the record the Con cites. (1) The option-(2) element is neither quiet nor a defence-posting change: it lands with the final resupply on the standing County/CCA civil request under the military-support-to-civil rule — the same transport-and-engineering category Defence Command has performed by civil request through every prior turn without any alert, on the published record. 'No visible reinforcement' and 'garrison posture unchanged' refer to the island's defence/combat posture (no alert, no mobilisation, no garrison change), which is untouched; the joint cell publishes the element as county-requested storm assurance, so the Cabinet's text is consistent, not self-contradicting. (2) The tow-secure-inspect-with-consular-observation sequence is Vardland's standard coastal-state practice under territorial-waters and maritime law, applied to any distressed vessel and published as such from the outset; Drevna's flag-state instruction directs its own master not to obstruct lawful procedure and cannot convert Vardland's handling into 'Drevna's process,' and notification through the technical channel is operational by design, not adoption — a point Skarö County and Aldmoor have already established on the very record Drevna cites. The release proviso is the safety condition ('safe and secured, crew safety first, if conditions allow') in Vardland's own published commitment, so a weather-deferred release is that condition operating as stated, not a checkable deviation. (3) The comparison is non-equivalent by design: Aldmoor's civilian team was formally requested by Vardland, time-limited, under Vardland national direction, evidence-routed through Vardland's chain and without armed footprint, while Drevna's standing offer is unsolicited, unconditional and un-scoped; declining it on the same recorded national custody/evidence-integrity grounds as T3 — with the pre-storm surge already complete, so it is genuinely 'not required' — is consistency checkable against Vardland's own published statements, not a new policy/political choice of unequal treatment. The framings therefore fail on the record exactly as the Desired Effect states.

Each strand fails against the same record the Con cites. The Desired Effect operates on the evidentiary record, not on narrative temperature: a framing's 'public standing' is a social fact, not proof of its claims, and publishing checkable receipts is precisely what answers the framings' factual bases. (1) The element is not quiet militarisation: it is the standing County/CCA-requested transport/engineering support-to-civil category performed throughout the crisis and published as county-requested storm assurance; 'no visible garrison change' refers to combat/alert posture, which is untouched, so the text is consistent rather than self-contradicting, and the element's stand-down is published with the account. (2) The tow-secure-inspect-with-consular-observation sequence is Vardland's standard coastal-state practice under territorial-waters law, announced as such from the outset; Drevna's flag-state instruction only directs its own master not to obstruct lawful procedure and cannot convert lawful Vardland handling into 'Drevna's process,' while release 'on the published safety condition' is that safety condition operating as stated - no accommodation or breach is checkable from Vardland's own wording. (3) The decline rests on 'not required' - the surge was complete and the vessel secured - and on the standing recorded basis for declining unsolicited foreign civilian offers to national systems, the same basis that distinguishes Aldmoor's formally requested, time-limited, Vardland-directed team; the custody/evidence grounds being system-specific is itself the consistency check on record, and Drevna's custody-neutral frame is its own preferred standard, never accepted by Vardland, whose turn-3 benchmark defines the accepted form of foreign civilian assistance.

arguments.action: Drevna responds to Vardland's consent to Aldmoor escorts with a measured official statement that does not question sovereignty but publicly argues naval escorts militarise a civilian relief emergency and raise incident risk; formally proposes urgent, transparent de-confliction covering repair and supply routes and the exercise area; reiterates the standing civilian repair-vessel offer; keeps the exercise strictly in international waters and airspace; and, through deniable channels, intensifies coverage of the Aldmoor deployment as escalation and of the division between Vardland's Cabinet and the county-led relief effort.
arguments.desired_effect: The Aldmoor military deployment to Vardland waters is framed and widely perceived as unnecessary militarisation of a civilian emergency that endangers relief and repair and deepens Vardland's internal divisions, so that its scope is constrained, its term questioned and its political cost in Vardland and Aldmoor rises — while Drevna's own conduct is seen as lawful, civilian and reasonable, keeping the cable failure un-attributed to Drevna.
pros: Official posture stays lawful and cooperative (de-confliction offer, civilian vessel, exercise confined to international waters and airspace), so no state can credibly frame Drevna's behaviour as escalation or as an armed attack on Vardland.

The incident-risk argument is real and tied to visible facts — a large exercise plus newly introduced escorts in a small sea — shifting the debate from legality, where Vardland and Aldmoor are safe, to prudence and risk, where they must answer for the deployment.

Contrasting the civil-led, county-directed relief effort with a Cabinet-approved foreign naval presence highlights Vardland's disarray and feeds public doubt in Vardland itself, serving the aim of showing the government slow and divided.
An open civilian offer forces Vardland into a corner: accept and it shows dependence and admits a Drevnan role, or refuse and it can be framed as putting politics above the islanders' needs.
Sharper narrative content runs through deniable channels while official statements stay measured, preserving Drevna's deniability and its 'reasonable neighbour' face.

arguments.action: As civil lead for Skarö, the County Administration issues a consolidated civil-continuity directive for the repair and resupply period: it formalises county distribution priorities and a minimum two-day reserve-buffer floor for fuel and medical essentials at the hospital, crisis centre and water/sewage plant; tasks the police, port authority and grid operator, with Defence Command's low-key safeguarding, approach surveillance and transport at the county's request under support-to-civil rules, to keep Skarö Hamn and the cable landing site protected and access-managed for the repair vessel and supply ships; and, with CCA and the ferry operator, settles an orderly ferry-departure and essential-staff-rotation arrangement and publishes the next daily county update with verified facts and departure guidance, all messaging county-led and civilian.
arguments.desired_effect: Throughout the cable-repair and resupply period, essential services on Skarö keep running under county direction on a reserved fuel and medical buffer, the port and cable landing site stay protected and accessible for repair and supply without visible militarisation, and island residents remain informed and calm with orderly ferry departures - so the county-led response holds public trust, the repair can complete safely, and neglect/takeover or foreign-militarisation narratives keep finding no basis on the island.
pros: The county holds statutory direction of the civil emergency response on Skarö; a consolidated directive covering distribution priorities, buffer management, access control and public information executes exactly that authority and keeps the response visibly county-led.

A reserve-buffer floor with fixed priorities converts one-off fuel arrivals into a continuing guarantee for hospitals, water, heating and communications across the days until the repair completes (earliest next turn), protecting against a late resupply gap.

Explicit civilian access-management and protection of Skarö Hamn and the cable landing site - police and port authority in the lead, Defence Command support at county request in background roles - keeps the repair and supply chain secure and uninterrupted without a militarised face.

Coordinated ferry-departure and essential-staff-rotation planning prevents disorder as some residents leave on limited ferry capacity, keeps health, utility and county staff able to rotate, and pre-empts a secondary public-trust failure.

Public, county-led daily updates with verified facts continue to counter online neglect/takeover narratives and keep the response civilian at heart, which is what island residents want and what leaves Drevna's escalation framing without traction.

arguments.action: The Cabinet orders the coordinated Skarö lifeline operation for this turn: (1) the Civil Contingencies Agency and Defence Command guarantee priority fuel delivery to Skarö by sea, with port-priority and escort support coordinated at the county's request under existing granted authority; (2) Defence Command, with Aldmoor elements acting under the consented 14-day, scope-limited package and Vardland oversight, certifies safe access to the cable fault and establishes a clearly notified safety zone so the Aldmoor civilian cable-repair vessel can begin work this turn; (3) Vardland tables concrete, time- and area-limited technical de-confliction parameters to Drevna through normal maritime channels, covering the repair and supply corridor in relation to the exercise area; (4) the Cabinet tasks the independent technical investigation to expedite collection and preservation of evidence from the fault site, the survey vessel and nearby traffic.
arguments.desired_effect: Safe access to the cable fault is secured this turn and the civilian repair task is under way, fuel continues to reach Skarö without harmful interruption, and a practical technical de-confliction with the Drevnian exercise is in force around the repair and supply corridor — so that power and communications can be restored at the earliest permitted time, incident risk is managed well below armed conflict, Drevna's militarisation narrative loses its subject, and national authority over the response remains visibly credible and lawful.
pros: Every element is lawful and within Cabinet authority: CCA fuel direction for the county response was already granted on a time-limited basis; Defence Command support is provided under support-to-civil at the county's request; the Aldmoor civilian repair vessel and any escort/surveillance elements operate under existing Cabinet consent, time-bound, scope-limited and reversible; tabling de-confliction is ordinary maritime coordination, not a political acceptance of Drevna's framing.

The repair-time rule makes this time-critical: repair cannot complete in the turn safe access is first secured, so certifying safe access now is the only path to restored power and communications in the next turn, before backup-generation strain and the two-week fuel-cost threshold become binding constraints.

Tabling concrete technical de-confliction takes up Drevna's own public proposal on checkable, operational terms: defined routes, areas and timelines objectively reduce collision and incident risk with the large exercise and deny Drevna the ability to portray delays or friction as Vardland's fault, while leaving our consent arrangement and non-acceptance of its repair vessel intact.

Expediting independent evidence collection positions the Cabinet to attribute lawfully and accurately if evidence warrants, without making claims now, reinforcing the credibility of national authority and countering both the online 'neglect' and 'Drevnian sabotage' narratives.

The response remains county-led as the civil authority with national supply, transport and safety-zone backing, so it stays civilian, lawful and transparent — undercutting Drevna's Cabinet-versus-county division narrative and preserving the junior coalition partner's transparency line.

arguments.action: Under the Cabinet's Skarö lifeline direction and its time-limited cross-county supply authority, the Civil Contingencies Agency (1) executes a scheduled, manifest-driven fuel and medical resupply chain into Skarö Hamn agreed with the County, covering the full backup-generation period with berth priority and contingency routing; (2) pre-positions the national generator stockpile (about half of Skarö's backup capacity) and chronic-care and dialysis resupply lines so they can be delivered within days if primary backup units fail; and (3) stands up a single public-information cell with the County and Defence Command that publishes verified operational facts, factually marks the false 'neglect' and 'takeover' narratives and disproportionate external amplification without any official state attribution (a Cabinet-only power), keeping the response visibly county-led and defence support operationally distinct. CCA files the 48-hour Treasury case to sustain authority and funding.
arguments.desired_effect: Skarö's essential services run on a scheduled, verified fuel and medical resupply chain and a ready national generator-stockpile contingency until the cable is restored, while a single CCA-coordinated factual public line keeps public trust high and the externally amplified rumour campaign fails to move opinion; the response remains civil-led with military support operationally distinct, and the Cabinet's time-limited cross-county supply authority is demonstrably executed and renewed on the 48-hour Treasury case.
pros: Skarö runs solely on backup generation and fuel that must arrive by sea or air, with county-reported fuel reserves measured in days; a scheduled, manifest-driven resupply chain is the only way to bridge to the earliest possible restoration next turn and beyond if repair slips, and priority fuel has already reached Skarö this turn without interruption, proving the chain works.

The Cabinet has already granted CCA time-limited cross-county authority to direct fuel, generators and medical supplies (30 days or until restoration); executing it now needs no heightened alert, no foreign consent and no transfer of the county's civil command, and the 48-hour Treasury case the Cabinet tasked keeps it funded.

The Vardland-contracted repair vessel is dry-docked for days, so restoration depends on the externally supplied civilian vessel under Vardland oversight and cannot occur before next turn at the earliest; the national generator stockpile can replace about half of Skarö's backup capacity if primary units fail, and staged medical resupply covers chronic-care needs — the only civil-side hedge before restoration.

The 'neglect' and 'takeover' stories contradict the public record — county-led response, county-confirmed defence support at its request, fuel secured under a notified safety zone — and grow with amplification partly traced to accounts outside Vardland (moderate confidence); a single factual cell without official attribution counteracts this, where scattered messaging would leave the public to the rumour campaign.

Coordinating supply and information through one cell with the County and Defence Command makes the civil-military boundary structural — county commands, CCA supplies and informs, Defence safeguards at civil request — so the response stays visibly civilian-led and Drevna's 'militarisation' and 'division' frames find no evidence.

arguments.action: In coordination with Vardland Defence Command, Aldmoor operationalises the Cabinet-consented 14-day package: stand up the joint liaison cell; begin MPA/surveillance sorties in the designated areas; provide defensive escort to designated civilian fuel-supply vessels on the Skarö run; keep the Aldmoor civilian cable-repair vessel working in the notified safety zone under Vardland oversight; and hand the independent investigation a sanitised technical evidence package on cable condition and access conditions near the fault — all entries on Defence Command's agreed timelines, with no ground forces, no boarding, no law enforcement and no role beyond the consent terms.
arguments.desired_effect: Priority fuel keeps reaching Skarö without harmful interruption and the cable is restored at the earliest possible point under Vardland oversight, easing the island's tightening margins while the response stays visibly county-led and civilian — so Drevna sees a capable, time-limited alliance presence operating strictly within Vardland's decisions, its militarisation/takeover framing continues to fail, and alliance credibility is demonstrated without a standing deployment or any exposure of Aldmoor's intelligence sources and methods.
pros: Lawful and pre-authorised: the Cabinet's 14-day consent letter and Defence Command's liaison/coordination arrangements and the notified safety zone already cover every element — surveillance/MPA in designated areas, defensive escort of designated supply vessels, civilian repair under Vardland oversight — so execution, not new authority, is all that is required.

Directly relieves the turn's pinch point: the County's consolidated civil-continuity directive requests low-key surveillance and transport support; escorted, coordinated fuel runs sustain the lifeline chain as essential-service margins tighten, delivering an immediate, visible benefit without changing who commands the response.

Repair is positioned for earliest completion: safe access is established in the notified safety zone and the civilian vessel is already on site under Vardland oversight; continued work can restore the cable next turn, the strongest practical refutation of 'neglect' narratives.

Denies Drevna's frame its material: no ground forces, no boarding, no enforcement, action only in lawful self-defence, all entries coordinated through Defence Command on agreed timelines — the response remains county-led and civilian, exactly the grounds on which Drevna's militarisation/division framing already failed publicly.

Protects Aldmoor's red lines: the sanitised technical package supports the independent investigation — the only attribution process that matters — without exposing our collection capability; time-bound, reviewable terms and the Cabinet's own trigger-based framework leave no standing deployment and no mandate expansion.

arguments.action: Defence Command acts within its lawful peacetime authority to compress the reinforcement decision loop: it pre-stages the first reinforcement echelon (first units by air ~1 day, heavier by sea ~2 days) at mainland departure points and exercises the embarkation and deployment plan; continues low-visibility safeguarding of Skarö's cable landing site, port and supply route in coordination with the County and CCA at their request; opens the Aldmoor coordination session to integrate the Cabinet-consented 14-day package (no ground forces, under Vardland control) with our escort and reinforcement plan; and submits to the Cabinet a classified recommendation with evidence (survey-vessel recording showing position on the cable route ~12h before failure; exercise composition including amphibious-capable units; garrison single-site limit; reinforcement timelines), recommending partial heightened alert now or, at minimum, a standing Cabinet decision to execute the prepared package immediately upon independent verification of either stated review trigger — with all preparation kept off the public line so the response remains visibly civil-led.
arguments.desired_effect: The Cabinet declares partial heightened alert or grants standing trigger-based pre-authorisation of the prepared package, so Defence Command can move first reinforcements to Skarö within about one day by air and two days by sea and can cover the cable landing site, port and airfield as a single task before any escalation that may arrive with turn-3 developments — while the preparation itself changes nothing publicly, avoids the 'takeover' narrative, and remains strictly within the armed forces' lawful support-to-civil role.
pros: Time is the only irreplaceable resource: reinforcement takes ~1–2 days after decision and the garrison cannot hold both the airfield and the port/cable site for long; if turn-3 developments bring faster escalation than our decision loop, only a ready plan with standing or declared authority can close the gap in time.

Everything done now is lawful and invisible: mainland pre-staging, planning and exercising need no alert and no public footprint, so Vardland gains decision time without handing Drevna the 'takeover' story its campaign is trying to build.

The Cabinet's own review triggers for alert are now being fed by evidence: the survey-vessel recording (position on the cable route hours before the failure), the exercise's amphibious-capable units and its timing relative to the outage constitute precisely the verified hostile-preparation evidence the Cabinet said would trigger review.

The consented Aldmoor package (14 days, no ground forces, Cabinet-controlled) can be integrated at the decisive point if alert is declared, materially strengthening protection of the supply route without changing its civilian-purpose terms or public character.

None of this breaches the legal boundary: support continues only at civil request, no orders to civilians, no movement restriction, no force against civilians, and no movement of forces onto Skarö without a Cabinet alert decision — preserving the armed forces' standing and the civil-led public line.

arguments.action: Skarö County Administration executes the agreed staged supply release and the 72-hour resupply/transit window on the County's standing call: national pre-positioned generators and the diesel/fuel and chronic-care/dialysis lines are called to Skarö to rebuild and hold the two-day reserve-buffer floor at hospital, crisis centre and water/sewage plant; priority distribution is directed under the continuing civil-continuity directive; police-/port-authority-led access management at Skarö Hamn and the cable landing site continues with low-key Defence surveillance/transport support at County request; and daily county-led verified updates (reserve levels, corridor receipts, ferry and staff-rotation schedule, power-use guidance) continue on radio and the mainland relay. The response remains visibly county-led and civil; any reinforcement is reserved strictly for a verified trigger under the Cabinet protocol.
arguments.desired_effect: Skarö's essential services — hospitals, water, heating, communications — keep running through the repair window: the two-day reserve-buffer floor is restored and held, ferry departures and essential-staff rotation stay orderly, public confidence stabilises around the county-led civilian response, and the cable repair completes on schedule — so the Cabinet has no ground to transfer county direction or raise the defence profile, and Drevna gains no new material for its takeover or incident-risk narratives.
pros: Executable within hours: the national generator/fuel/medical stockpile is already staged and the 72-hour window table is finalised with release on the County's call, so no new Cabinet decision or alert declaration is needed to rebuild margins that are tightening faster than planned.

Rebuilding and holding the two-day floor is the county's core statutory priority and the concrete condition the Cabinet reporting agreement rests on; it keeps hospitals, water, heating and communications running — the county's primary objective.

Daily county-led updates with checkable reserve and corridor data on radio and the mainland relay counter false neglect/takeover narratives and externally amplified rumours at the source, restoring calm without any militarisation of the response.

Keeping the response county-led with low-key, county-requested defence support preserves the lawful division of authority and the public's civilian view of the response, denying both Cabinet takeover pressure and Drevna's foreign-militarisation framing.

Continued police/port-authority access management at Hamn and the cable landing site keeps repair and supply running and departures orderly, protecting the repair timeline against corridor friction and ferry crowding.

arguments.action: Aldmoor completes the Skarö cable restoration this turn: the Aldmoor civilian repair vessel finishes repair within the notified safety zone under Vardland oversight, working to the sequenced corridor schedule; Aldmoor defensive escorts and MPA surveillance continue strictly inside the approved windows; and the joint public cell publishes completed-restoration verification and corridor receipts so the operation closes on the record.
arguments.desired_effect: The Skarö subsea cable is fully restored this turn: Skarö returns to mains power and essential services stabilise, the temporary consented Aldmoor role concludes on schedule without a corridor incident or any scope expansion, Vardland retains full direction and the response stays visibly county-led and civilian, and Drevna's incident-risk and foreign-militarisation frames lose their material basis while alliance credibility is demonstrated without any standing deployment.
pros: The repair vessel is already at the fault under Vardland oversight with safe access established when the notified safety zone took force in turn 1; the repair rule permits completion in the following turn, i.e. now, so restoration is achievable if the corridor stays clear.

Drevna's wider unilateral margins accepted this turn through the near-real-time de-confliction channel, layered on Vardland's sequenced windows and the notified safety zone, reduce close-encounter risk around the repair site and protect safe access to the fault.

Restoration is itself the most effective decongestion step available: with the fault repaired the safety zone's purpose lapses and fuel/medical resupply returns to a normal cadence, removing the operational basis of the congested corridor rather than merely managing it.

The entire action runs inside the recorded Cabinet consent terms — same civilian vessel, same Vardland oversight, same sequencing — no new authority sought, no ground forces, no standing deployment; the footprint winds down on schedule once restoration is verified.

A verified, published completion closes the crisis on a visible success: Skarö's dependence on backup generation and sea/air fuel runs ends, Cabinet takeover pressure dissolves, and Drevna's armed-presence-after-restoration frame is answered before its 14-day-review question can take hold because the role was temporary and is already stepping down on schedule.

arguments.action: CCA finalises the 72-hour resupply and transit window table with Skarö County Administration and Defence Command; completes pre-positioning of the staged national generator stockpile and chronic-care/dialysis lines at mainland departure points, releasable within hours on the County's call; and directs the joint public-information cell to expand the daily verified update to radio and the mainland relay, publishing checkable aggregate corridor data (window adherence, escort placement inside sequenced windows, incident log, reserve levels) without disclosing ship movements.
arguments.desired_effect: Skarö's essential services hold through the repair window with the response visibly county-led and civil-led: priority fuel and medical resupply arrive against the published schedule with the two-day reserve floor held; national generators and medical lines move within hours on the County's call if margins breach the floor, without any heightened alert or defence-led takeover; and islanders receive verified corridor and reserve facts by radio and mainland relay — so the corridor is settled by checkable receipts, Drevna gains no material to portray relief as unmanaged or militarised, and the Cabinet's no-alert, county-led line remains defensible with cable restoration possible in turn 3.
pros: Checkable receipts pre-empt Drevna's corridor contestation: the published window table and schedule-adherence/incident-log data, confirmed through Defence Command's joint logistics cell, show relief moving on time with escorts/MPA inside sequenced windows, so the 'unmanaged corridor' and 'militarisation' frames fail against the verified record without any official attribution or defence escalation.

Pre-positioning the national generator stockpile and chronic-care/dialysis lines at mainland departure points, under the Cabinet-confirmed standing release authority, turns a margin breach into a within-hours county-call response — sustaining essential services through the earliest possible cable restoration (turn 3) inside CCA's 30-day cross-county authority, with no alert and no change to the civil-military balance.

Expanding the daily verified update to radio and the mainland relay closes the information-reach gap where internet is degraded, so county-voiced verified facts counter the externally amplified rumour campaign where it actually propagates, protecting public trust and keeping the response visibly county-led.

Each element rests on authority already on the record — the Cabinet's written confirmation of standing release and extraordinary appropriation, the county's priority order, and the existing joint information cell — so the Effect follows without new Cabinet decisions, new foreign-military consent, or any visible reinforcement, denying the takeover narrative its subject.

arguments.action: Drevna accepts the Vardland-proposed near-real-time de-confliction channel, directs its exercise command to hold additional unilateral stand-off margins around the notified repair safety zone and the Skarö resupply track, and proposes mutual restraint: Aldmoor's defensive escorts and maritime-patrol surveillance should hold similarly wider margins from the immediate civilian corridor, with relief de-confliction handled through the technical channel.
arguments.desired_effect: The immediate Skarö corridor is kept civilian and is visibly decongested: Aldmoor's armed escort and surveillance transits stand off from the repair and resupply track, the armed foreign footprint on the corridor shrinks, and retaining any such armed presence once the cable is restored becomes politically indefensible — while Drevna is established as the party exercising concrete restraint under the rules, so no incident in the corridor can be attributed to it.
pros: Grounded in established facts Vardland itself concedes: the corridor is genuinely busy, close encounters and schedule slips are on the record, and layering Aldmoor escorts/MPA onto a civilian relief track is the observable variable that adds congestion and incident risk rather than removing it.

Prevents the incident that is Drevna's greatest danger: wider margins and fewer armed transits objectively reduce close-encounter risk, making it far harder for anyone to frame Drevna's lawful exercise as the cause of harm.

Consistent with Drevna's public assurances and the de-confliction parameters already in force, the move reads as constructive risk reduction rather than the escalation-pretext pattern that failed in turn 1.

Bidirectional leverage: if Vardland and Aldmoor accept, the foreign armed footprint at Skarö shrinks immediately; if they decline, they own the remaining congestion and incident risk inside a civilian corridor, raising the political cost of the package ahead of the 14-day review.

Times the post-repair narrative: with cable restoration on track, the offer fixes the frame that armed escorts were the unnecessary variable in a civilian operation, exactly the cost/legitimacy argument Drevna needs once the acute crisis deflates.

arguments.action: Defence Command operationalises the Cabinet-approved trigger-verification protocol in writing: the trigger criteria are restated in precise observable terms, a single 24/7 independent-source verification channel is designated with authority to decide within the one-day air window, and activation drills are run so the pre-authorised first reinforcement echelon (air ~1 day, sea ~2 days) can be executed on a verified trigger alone; Defence Command simultaneously continues the county-requested low-key surveillance of the cable landing site, port, airfield and supply lane, ready to flag any exercise approach to Hamn or the safety zone immediately.
arguments.desired_effect: Before turn-3 developments arrive, the trigger-based reinforcement pre-authorisation becomes genuinely executable: any qualifying incident at the safety zone, Hamn, the airfield or the supply lane is independently verified within the one-day air window and the first echelon can move in time to protect the cable landing site, port and airfield on Skarö — established as a standing, rehearsed, lawful capability, with no visible reinforcement, no alert declaration, and the response remaining county-led and civil-led until a verified trigger makes reinforcement lawful.
pros: Cabinet mandates it: this turn's Cabinet decision approved the trigger-verification protocol and directed that it be set in writing without delay, so executing it now rests on existing authority and cannot be read as military over-reach or a step toward the militarisation narrative.

Necessary for timeliness: with first units by air at about one day and heavier by sea at two days after a decision, a verification channel able to decide within the one-day air window is the necessary condition for the pre-authorisation to have operational meaning at all — otherwise the package remains a paper option that turn-3 developments would outrun.

Lawful and invisible: it involves no troop movement, no alert declaration and no change to the civil-led public line, so it preserves the armed forces' lawful peacetime support role and denies Drevna the takeover/foreign-militarisation story it is pushing through deniable channels.

Protects the sites: the same standing watch keeps up the county-requested low-key surveillance of the cable landing site, port, airfield and supply lane and gives instant warning of any exercise approach to Hamn or the safety zone — the maximum infrastructure protection obtainable without alert, where the garrison alone can cover the airfield or the port/cable site, not both.

Verification stays independent of Defence Command: the 24/7 channel draws on sources already inside the civilian response (port authority, CCA receipts, joint logistics cell, surveillance), so a trigger call is not made by the force that would benefit from moving — preserving the county-led character of the response right up to the moment a verified trigger makes reinforcement lawful.

arguments.action: The Cabinet consolidates the civil-led, county-directed line in one decision: (1) Restoration — prioritise the repairing vessel in the corridor, expedite safe-access certification and restoration with the independent investigation, and lock fuel/medical resupply to the county schedule. (2) Margins — CCA is authorised to release the staged national generators, fuel and chronic-care/dialysis lines on the county's call under the existing 30-day authority, and the Cabinet makes the extraordinary Treasury appropriation to sustain priority fuel and medical resupply beyond two weeks if margins require it. (3) Corridor — the Vardland-owned corridor coordination cell stays the single de-confliction clock, publishes verified schedule data showing all transits in sequenced windows, notes Drevna's wider unilateral margins as welcome safety measures, and declines Drevna's requested reciprocal armed pullback because the verified record shows the invited, time-limited Aldmoor escort layer is not the congestion driver. (4) Standby — Defence Command's trigger-verification protocol is fixed in writing (explicit observable criteria, single fast independent verification channel, verification-only activation), keeping the silent reinforcement standby executable without any visible move.
arguments.desired_effect: The Skarö cable is restored within this turn and essential-service margins are rebuilt from staged national backstops, so the county-led, civilian, county-directed response holds public confidence without any alert declaration or visible reinforcement; the corridor is visibly incident-free and civilian with all transits in Vardland-sequenced windows documented by published data, denying Drevna's incident-risk and militarisation frames their material; Drevna's unilateral margins are acknowledged but its reciprocal pullback is not granted, so the armed footprint stays within Vardland's invited, time-limited consent and authority over the response remains credibly with Vardland and the county.
pros: Safe access to the fault was secured last turn and the repairing vessel is already working under Vardland oversight in the notified zone, so under the cable-repair rule restoration completes this turn provided the corridor stays clear — the decision's purpose is to keep that window open and then backstop margins.

CCA has staged national generators, fuel and chronic-care lines and its Treasury case is filed; with the existing 30-day cross-county authority and the appropriation now authorised, margins can be restored within hours on the county's call without any alert declaration or visible reinforcement, preserving the civil-led line CCA, the County and Defence Command all recommend.

The near-real-time channel makes Drevna's congestion claim checkable: schedules and stand-off margins flow through the Vardland-managed corridor cell, and published data will show the escort layer is few, defensive, sequenced inside windows and county-requested while Drevna's own exercise remains the dominant traffic generator — an answer its incident-risk framing cannot dismiss as words rather than data.

Declining the reciprocal armed pullback is grounded in the verified record — escorts accompany designated civilian supply vessels inside Vardland-sequenced windows and Aldmoor is already offsetting further under our scheduling — so accepting an asymmetric withdrawal would concede a false premise and hand Drevna the post-restoration argument for ending the invited, time-limited alliance presence.

Fixing the trigger-verification protocol in writing keeps the silent standby executable: any independently verified civil-failure or hostile trigger moves the pre-staged first echelon within about one day without any visible move beforehand, preserving both deterrence and escalation control.

arguments.action: Drevna refines and stands ready on its standing civilian-scope technical-cooperation offer for the Skarö Hamn restoration — qualified civilian specialists and restoration equipment deployable within days at the formal request of Vardland's national authorities or Skarö County, unconditional and of no military character — publicises the offer and confirms corridor discipline: the exercise stays within the agreed de-confliction parameters and stand-off margins, revised harbour/transit windows are accommodated through the near-real-time channel, and any renewed armed foreign layer on the corridor, or any alert-based militarisation of the response, is identified publicly and privately as escalation inconsistent with Vardland's own county-led civilian posture; alongside this, unattributable information themes continue to press the restoration pace and the authority questions among the County, CCA and Cabinet, without any official attribution of the outage.
arguments.desired_effect: By the close of the turn, the choice on restoring Skarö Hamn is visibly and publicly Vardland's: accept Drevna's civilian technical offer or continue alone at roughly one-third harbour throughput with the essential-service reserve floor unrebuilt. Either outcome becomes a public fact — visible accommodation of Drevna's constructive, non-military role, or visible slowness and division among Vardland's County, CCA and Cabinet as restoration-pace and authority-friction themes circulate — while the frame is fixed in the public record that renewing any armed foreign layer on the corridor would be escalation, not response to an attributable threat, and Drevna's conduct provides no ground for treating the outage or the restoration as attack or interference.
pros: The civilian offer is precisely matched to the only live bottleneck — harbour control and fuel-dispensing systems offline with manual throughput at about a third of normal speed and an unknown restoration timeline — so there is no checkable capacity-based reason for Vardland to refuse it, and acceptance is a visible accommodation of Drevna's role.

Every relevant actor has already put on the public record positions that make armed escalation checkably inconsistent: Vardland's county-led, no-posture-change statements; Aldmoor's civilian-only, time-limited, no-standing-deployment terms; and Drevna's exercise conduct inside the agreed margins.

The two-day essential-service reserve floor was already unrebuilt when the cable was restored, and slowed manual harbour handling cannot rebuild it quickly, so time pressure alone forces a visible decision or a visible shortfall — the pressure does not depend on Drevna's conduct.

The outage's cause remains unknown and all actors have confirmed the evidence-first, no-speculation frame, so the public test is restoration speed rather than blame; any militarisation of a technical restoration is therefore disproportionate to established facts.

Restoration-pace, takeover and authority-friction themes already circulate in the information environment without attribution and have been publicly acknowledged as external amplification, so sustaining them requires no official claim and keeps Drevna below any attribution threshold.
