cons.reason: The Desired Effect rests on a false binary — accept Drevna's civilian offer or appear slow and divided — and neither branch is checkable by turn's close. (1) Vardland is not continuing 'alone': national ICS/cyber-security specialists and manual-handling procedure support were surged to Skarö Hamn under the Cabinet's standing release authority at the County's request and under county direction before Drevna's refined offer, so restoration is visibly proceeding by national means regardless of any Drevna involvement. (2) Declining foreign access to harbour control and fuel-dispensing systems has a checkable sovereign-security basis wholly independent of attribution — preserving the integrity of the digital evidence chain during an unknown-origin intrusion and protecting critical infrastructure from further supply-chain risk — so a refusal reads as prudent custody, not slowness, and cannot be demonstrated as 'division.' (3) The authority-friction and takeover themes the Argument plans to press contradict the established public record — Cabinet's written reconfirmation of county direction, CCA's coordinated supply-and-restore role, and the joint verified public-information cell publishing daily checkable harbour data — while equivalent external-amplification themes were already publicly documented as failing, giving the 'visible division' branch nothing demonstrable to take hold of.

The Desired Effect claims the storm account closes Drevna's framings, but an active turn-4 public effect on this very record states the opposite: Drevna's accommodation, selective-sovereignty, unequal-treatment and authorities-contradiction framings 'keep public standing through the storm' and 'the public contest stays open,' with the element deployment and offer decline themselves recorded as checkable as an authorities contradiction and unequal treatment on Vardland's own record. Publishing verified receipts proves the response ran; it cannot close framings whose bases are the account's own published contents. (1) CCA's facts confirm a Defence Command logistic/engineering element was on Skarö through the storm and now stands down as links reopen — a checkable armed-forces footprint and stand-down that a 'no visible garrison change' characterisation cannot erase, whatever label is applied, so the quiet-militarisation/authorities-contradiction question is answered from the text, not closed by it. (2) The same account confirms the Drevnian vessel was secured, inspected with consular observation and released only 'on the published safety condition' — precisely the tow-secure-inspect sequence and conditional release Drevna proposed and publicly instructed its master to accept; whether that is accommodation or standard practice remains a live, checkable question each reader answers from Vardland's own wording, which the turn-4 record already shows read as accommodation. (3) The asserted identity of grounds — declining Drevna's offers 'on the same recorded national custody/evidence-integrity grounds' as hosting Aldmoor's civilian team — is asserted, not established: the recorded grounds address Skarö Hamn's control/fuel-dispensing systems under an active evidence chain, a different class from the storm-time tow/salvage and general relief assistance at issue, and Drevna's unconditional civilian offer was never scoped or tested under the custody-neutral, time-limited, Vardland-directed terms it explicitly invited. Each strand therefore remains checkable on the published record exactly as the Desired Effect concedes it is published, so the framing-failure claim fails against the same turn's facts.

The forced choice can be collapsed by facts already on the record. The national ICS/cyber-restoration surge is under way under the Cabinet's standing release authority at the County's and harbour operator's request (as the County published on 24 Sep), with milestones and daily verified throughput data from the joint public-information cell; if the harbour systems are restored and handling normalised within the turn, the 'continue alone at roughly one-third throughput' horn dissolves, and declining an unnecessary offer becomes a routine sovereign decision rather than visible slowness or County/CCA/Cabinet division. The unattributable restoration-pace and authority-friction themes have already failed once this crisis: the external-amplification campaign moved no opinion and was publicly acknowledged as interference, and the same verified-metrics counter is live again, so sustained unattributed pressure will harden rather than divide the government's line. The accompanying claim that any renewed armed layer would be escalation presupposes a step no Vardland actor has taken or proposed and reads as the same checkable overreach that already undercut Drevna's turn-1 de-confliction bid, so the frame fixes nothing and can be rebutted on the record.

The claimed 'accommodation of Drevna's process' and the paired 'breach / unequal-treatment' framings fail on the face of the published record. The tow-then-secure-then-inspect sequence with consular observation is standard coastal-state practice under international maritime law that Vardland applies to any distressed vessel in its territorial waters; Vardland's own statements (Cabinet and the joint public-information cell) frame the handling as coast-guard action 'under maritime law' and 'territorial-waters law', not as a sequence proposed by Drevna that Vardland adopted. Drevna's instruction to its own master is merely a flag-state direction not to obstruct lawful procedure; it creates no evidence that Vardland 'relies on Drevna's commitments' or grants an accommodation, so desired effect (1) is not established. Likewise, not every storm-era outcome can be characterised as a 'breach': Vardland's published commitments are expressly conditional on the vessel being safe and secured with crew safety first, so an inspection deferred because towing or boarding is unsafe in severe weather, or a vessel held at anchorage because the storm prevents a safe tow, is that safety condition operating as stated, not a deviation from any commitment. The equal-treatment framing (2) likewise does not erase the recorded custody/evidence basis of the declined Drevna offers, which concerned control/fuel-dispensing systems under an active Vardland-run evidence chain under national authority; a storm-time humanitarian offer aimed at the vessel rather than at those systems neither removes nor tests that basis. On the record, the effect reads as Vardland applying its own law and safety practice to any vessel, not as Drevna-managed handling or a checkable policy choice of unequal treatment.

Aldmoor's Desired Effect is an outcome asserted, not produced, by the listed actions. It promises priority fuel 'without harmful interruption' while inserting into a small, congested sea armed foreign assets with separate command chains, rules of engagement and caveats, in a corridor where de-confliction parameters remain only in practical effect rather than a binding arrangement. Every added armed actor is a new contact and misidentification vector; any encounter between escorting units and other lawful traffic can halt the very fuel runs or repair work the Effect depends on, so the operation makes the promised interruption-free flow less likely, not more. It also claims the response 'stays visibly county-led and civilian,' yet the visible, checkable content of the operationalisation is foreign warships and patrol aircraft in Vardland waters and airspace; how publics read that is not Aldmoor's to set, and Skarö County's own insistence that national support 'stays in the background' shows how sensitive any visible armed presence is in this emergency. The asserted effects — what 'Drevna sees,' that the militarisation framing 'continues to fail,' that alliance credibility is 'demonstrated' — are perception claims outside Aldmoor's control, not consequences of the actions. And the claimed easing of margins assumes cable restoration from next turn, which the public record ties to work and checks completing, not to this package. Without established facts that no incident occurs, that publics read the operation as civilian, and that repair completes on schedule, the Effect does not follow.

The Desired Effect claims that authority-friction and takeover pressure are 'closed out by verified performance and Cabinet-confirmed governance' and that restoration completion is a 'published, checkable' fact by the turn's close, but neither closure is on the record. The established turn-3 record states that no authoritative Cabinet update to the trigger criteria is on record, so the protocol's full executability and the lawfulness of the posture remain contestable and authority-friction/takeover pressure continue to hold public attention; the County's own Effect then asserts a closure the record denies, so 'nothing on the record shows national direction would serve the island better' cannot settle the very dispute that remains open. 'Verified' and 'checkable' also describe the joint cell's self-published data produced inside the same county-CCA-Cabinet line whose authority questions are live: from the documented start state (systems offline, roughly one-third throughput, reserve floor unrebuilt), completion and a rebuilt floor by turn's close are asserted, not independently verified, leaving the restoration-pace question open on the same numbers. Finally, the sovereign declination of Drevna's civilian offer does not close the selective-engagement frame: a time-limited Aldmoor civilian technical/forensic team is requested into the same harbour control/fuel-dispensing systems under national cyber direction while Drevna's functionally similar civilian offer is declined outright without the same embedding/direction structure being offered — the only checkable difference remains the alliance, so the foreign-access and sovereignty question keeps a subject for Drevna's framing rather than being denied one.

The effect rests on premises the record does not support, so it cannot materialise as claimed. (1) Aldmoor armed transits are not the congestion variable: escorts are few, defensive, off-island, ride only in Vardland-sequenced windows accompanying designated supply vessels and are already being offset wider by Vardland's own corridor cell, while the large Drevnian formation in adjacent waters remains the dominant traffic generator — withdrawing escorts would neither visibly decongest the corridor nor shrink an 'armed foreign footprint' that is invited, time-limited and tied to county-requested support. (2) Drevna's wider margins are self-declared and independently unverifiable, so 'no incident can be attributed to it' is a claim, not an effect: attribution follows evidence, and the independent investigation is still collecting it from the fault site, nearby traffic and the survey vessel recorded on the cable route before the failure. (3) The post-restoration framing fails similarly: the Drevnian exercise continues in the same waters after restoration, so the defence rationale under Vardland's temporary, invited consent does not lapse and the armed presence is not made 'politically indefensible' by restoration alone.

The Desired Effect promises a standing, independently verified, county-preserving trigger capability, but the execution chain the Argument builds cannot deliver it. The organisation operationalising the protocol is Defence Command itself: it designates the single 24/7 verification source, invests it with authority to decide within the one-day air window, and lists among its feeds the county-requested surveillance that Defence Command itself conducts and the joint logistics/liaison cell in which Defence Command sits. A trigger determination produced on an information base and authority structure controlled by the very force whose pre-authorised movement it unlocks is not 'independent verification' in any sense the record establishes. This cuts two ways that both break the effect: in the contested, fast-moving incident for which the protocol is built, competing versions delay an authoritative call past the one-day air window — while a quick, military-sourced call is precisely the defence-led, takeover step the effect claims to avoid, read as Defence Command moving forces on Defence Command's own watch and converting a county-led response into a military one even without a formal alert. And even granting timely verification, the echelon still travels about a day by air and two by sea after the decision while the argument itself concedes the peacetime guard cannot hold both the airfield and the port/cable site at once — so 'arriving in time to protect all three sites' is not established. The effect's central promise — genuinely executable, lawful, yet still civil-led — therefore does not follow from the record.

Drevna's 'selective-sovereignty' and 'equal-treatment' landing fails against the record it cites. Vardland's published grounds for declining Drevna's civilian offers are national custody of the Skarö Hamn control/fuel-dispensing systems and digital-evidence integrity (turn-3 decline and the t3 benchmark), not safety, weather or capacity; Aldmoor's accepted civilian team is hosted only on a formal Vardland request, operates under Vardland's national cyber-security direction, routes evidence through Vardland's chain and publishes only sanitised technical content. A 'custody-neutral' standard for Drevna's unconditional, unsolicited offer is therefore a false equivalence, checkable against Vardland's own published statements: a refusal during the storm records the same custody/evidence-integrity choice already on the record, not a new policy/political choice. The argument also depends on the unverified premise that the master actually accepts the tow-and-secure sequence before the links close; as of the record the vessel has refused boarding inspection and sits ~2nm from the cable landing site with a four-day storm closure imminent, so Drevna's 'no conditions' civilian-cooperation framing can fail on its own vessel's conduct rather than on any Vardland deviation.

Drevna's desired effect rests on claims contradicted by established public facts. Skarö County — the civil authority Drevna claims to defend — formally requested limited defence support (approach surveillance, low-visibility safeguarding, transport) under lawful support-to-civil mechanisms and has publicly stated that defence support stays in the background under civilian control; a 14-day, no-ground-force, defensive-only Aldmoor package consented to by the Cabinet does not militarise a county-led emergency, and the 'Cabinet divided from county' narrative has no factual foundation. The incident-risk argument also inverts the evidentiary picture: the unexplained variable in this small sea is a large Drevnian exercise with amphibious-capable units held near an island whose sole cable failed hours earlier — not escorted civilian supply operating under standard navigation and de-confliction rules. And the 'reasonable neighbour' effect depends on the cause remaining un-attributed, which is not in Drevna's control: an independent investigation is running, and Drevna's own deniable campaign pushing 'takeover' and 'division' stories is visible conduct in Vardland and Aldmoor that contradicts its measured public posture.

The Effect's core assurances (fully executable protocol AND unbroken county-led civilian response with no visible reinforcement) cannot both be checkably established by turn's close, because the redefined criteria make the already-established outage itself a qualifying trigger. The harbour control and fuel-dispensing systems are offline after a cyber intrusion of unknown origin — an established public fact that satisfies 'a verified malicious cyber effect on the Skarö Hamn critical node counts as a qualifying port-incident trigger' as stated. The pre-authorised package is therefore executable immediately through the standing channel with no new Cabinet decision, so 'no visible reinforcement' is an act of restraint, not a property of the protocol; any execution would be a visible military deployment on an unattributed civilian cyber incident, handing Drevna's escalation/militarisation framing exactly the subject the Effect denies and reversing the standing joint line (reaffirmed to Defence Command and by the County/Cabinet this turn) that the outage is NOT a qualifying trigger event. Second, the 'Cabinet's amended turn-3 criteria' are asserted from the protocol side, not established by a Cabinet decision on the record: the visible turn-3 record shows no change in trigger status, and under the total-defence framework alert, trigger-authority and attribution decisions are the Cabinet's alone. Restating changed trigger definitions in a Defence Command argument without a corroborated Cabinet decision leaves the amendment contestable and the authority-friction/reopen-takeover frame alive, so the Effect's claims of fully lawful, undisputed posture cannot be secured.

Drevna's predicted perception shift rests on three claims that contradict the established public record. First, it attacks a deployment that has not occurred: no Aldmoor asset is yet operating in Vardland territory, waters or airspace. The consented package is time-bound (14 days, reviewable and renewable), scope-limited (surveillance and maritime patrol; defensive escort of designated civilian supply vessels; a civilian cable-repair vessel under Vardland oversight), coordinated through Vardland Defence Command and reversible by Cabinet decision. Framing this as 'militarisation of a civilian emergency' misdescribes a civilian-purpose, Cabinet-controlled arrangement, and publics can check that it is not even in operation. Second, the claimed 'division between Cabinet and county' is contradicted by Skarö County Administration's own public statement, in which the county confirms that limited defence support is provided at its request, stays in the background and remains under civilian control; Drevna cannot credibly invoke the county's authority as civil lead while describing the county-endorsed arrangement as Cabinet-imposed militarisation. Third, the incident-risk argument points at the wrong actor: the proximate source of incident risk in the Eastern Sea is Drevna's own large, continuing exercise in the same crowded waters, while its demand that all others keep military assets away from the repair and supply corridor is self-serving and its de-confliction offer presupposes the very contact it condemns. Because these are checkable public facts, the claimed 'widely perceived' framing is fragile and likely to rebound once examined, limiting both the scope-constraining and political-cost effects Drevna seeks.

The Desired Effect promises that this turn's staged release restores and holds the two-day reserve floor, keeps ferries and staff rotation orderly, stabilises public confidence around a county-led civilian response and completes the cable repair on schedule — eliminating any ground for Cabinet transfer or a raised defence profile. The verified record undercuts the causal chain. First, the binding constraints are corridor throughput and on-island logistics, not the availability of staged stock: the record already shows essential-service margins tightening faster than planned, ferry departures and staff rotation facing crowding or delay, and the corridor simultaneously hosting the repair vessel, scheduled fuel and medical runs, Aldmoor escorts and MPA transits and the exercise in adjacent waters, with repeated close encounters and scheduling friction disrupting both the fuel and the repair schedule. Releasing national generators, diesel and dialysis lines can be executed within hours, but the action adds no corridor capacity, unblocks no ferry crowding and does not itself protect the repair timeline — so holding the floor and stabilising confidence are not delivered by this action alone and may fail exactly where they are most needed. Second, the 'repair completes on schedule' promise is conditional on uninterrupted safe access, and the record already shows the repair schedule disrupted by corridor friction; nothing in this step secures that timeline against further incidents in the congested corridor. Third, the claim that the Cabinet will have 'no ground' to transfer county direction or raise the defence profile holds only while no trigger is verified: the standing trigger protocol remains armed, and this very execution draws on Defence Command surveillance and transport support and Cabinet-staged national stockpiles, so a qualifying safety-zone, port or supply-lane event verified under that protocol would move the response to the defence layer within the same window — leaving the takeover and defence-profile outcomes the effect claims to exclude on the table.

The Desired Effect is a Cabinet decision, and the Argument gives the Cabinet no established ground to grant it — against every published commitment it has just made. The cited 'hostile-preparation' evidence is not verified hostile preparation: a survey vessel's recorded position on a charted cable corridor near an unattributed fault shows location, not intent or causation, and the exercise's composition is the long-announced, public, pre-existing baseline, not new preparation; nothing has been independently verified, and under the agreed qualitative standard, posture and position claims are not evidence. In the same period the Cabinet has publicly and privately committed to a civil-led, investigation-first response and tabled concrete de-confliction parameters precisely so the situation stays well below armed conflict; Defence Command recommending partial heightened alert or standing trigger-based pre-authorisation on the current record contradicts that line and, if it ever became visible, would manufacture exactly the 'military takeover'/escalation story the Argument claims to avoid. The rational Cabinet response is therefore to decline alert and refuse standing pre-authorisation on these facts, limiting the Effect to uncommitted mainland planning that — absent a Cabinet decision — moves no reinforcement onto Skarö, secures no single task, and leaves the decision loop exactly where it is.

The Desired Effect depends on Vardland/Aldmoor accepting Drevna's asymmetric pullback, and the verified record contradicts the premise that the armed escort layer is the congestion variable. Defence Command's joint logistics cell has escorts and MPA sequenced inside safety-zone and transit windows so they do not interrupt scheduled traffic; congestion is driven by the corridor's concentrated traffic as a whole, including the exercise itself. The escort/MPA package is time-bound, Cabinet-consented and county-requested, so Vardland can decline any pullback without owning the 'congestion' narrative, while working-level de-confliction already in force addresses incident risk. Absent that acceptance, the armed footprint does not shrink, the 'politically indefensible once the cable is restored' frame fails against the receipt-based public record of managed, sequenced windows, and Drevna's unilateral margin-holding alone cannot ensure no incident occurs or that any incident would be attributed to it.

The Desired Effect rests on outcomes Vardland neither produces nor independently verifies by the turn's close, so the claimed dissolution of the accept/decline binary reads as assertion, not established fact. (1) Restoration cannot be checkably delivered this turn: the Action itself first preserves national custody and the digital evidence chain before any controlled restoration of the compromised control and fuel-dispensing systems, and the joint cell's 'verified' data are self-published with no independent verification; the on-record metrics the Effect claims to dissolve — systems offline, handling at roughly a third of normal speed, and the two-day essential-service reserve floor unrebuilt — are the documented state at the start of the turn and persist through its close, so the restoration-pace and authority questions remain open on the same numbers. (2) The national-custody ground for declining Drevna's civilian offer is undercut by the same decision inviting Aldmoor civilian technical and forensic specialists into identical compromised control, fuel-dispensing and evidence systems while the intrusion is unattributed: the only checkable difference between the two offers is the alliance, which makes the decision read on the record as selective foreign engagement that keeps sovereignty and foreign-access questions alive rather than closing them. (3) The claimed deterrence is overstated: the record shows the trigger-verification protocol is only partially executable, since the safety-zone trigger lost its geographic referent when the repair zone lapsed, so the Effect's 'fully executable protocol' premise is not on the record.

The Desired Effect cannot 'fail' the contested framings because the Cabinet's own turn-4 action and statements — and an active public effect already on the record — keep each framing open and checkable. (1) The argument deploys a Defence Command element to Skarö in the same public statement in which the Cabinet asserts 'no visible reinforcement' and 'garrison posture unchanged': an armed-forces footprint on the island is a material change to the island's defence footprint however it is labelled, so the quiet-militarisation and authorities-contradict-themselves basis survives on the face of Vardland's own text rather than being closed by it. (2) Vardland's own message to Drevna confirms the tow-secure-inspect handling 'as the first priority', and its public statement frames the handling as coordinated with Drevna — i.e., the sequence Drevna proposed and publicly instructed its master to accept — so the accommodation reading is anchored in Vardland's own wording and the active turn-4 record already records that framing as taking hold; a release deferred on 'conditions' would record a checkable storm-time outcome, not a refutation. (3) The storm-time decline of Drevna's civilian support as 'not required' rests on custody/evidence grounds recorded for Skarö Hamn's control/fuel-dispensing systems under an active evidence chain — a different class of assistance from vessel salvage/tow support and general storm relief — while Aldmoor's civilian team remains hosted under national direction, so the unequal-treatment comparison remains checkable on the very record Vardland cites. The Desired Effect therefore rests on a premise the same turn's record contradicts.

effects.description: The repair-and-supply corridor off Skarö is now simultaneously hosting Aldmoor defensive escorts and MPA surveillance sorties, the Drevnian exercise in adjacent international waters, the notified safety zone with the civilian repair vessel, and the scheduled fuel and medical resupply ships; despite the de-confliction parameters being in force, this concentrated traffic produces repeated close encounters and scheduling friction that disrupts the fuel and repair schedule. Drevna's escalation framing failed to take hold, but the genuine congestion now gives its incident-risk warning concrete, observable material that Vardland's own public line cannot dismiss.
effects.rationale: Aldmoor's escorts and the repair vessel (100d5c0c, 3f36ef87) and the fuel chain (756e4b6a) share the same narrow corridor that borders the Drevnian exercise area (d599c258, 43bfec7a); the friction reported by Aldmoor's outcome (0f2da2d2) is the combined result of these simultaneous presences. Although Drevna's framing was undercut (1a8ab819), the tabled de-confliction parameters (756e4b6a) do not remove the physical congestion, so Drevna's incident-risk concern now rests on observable facts rather than narrative.

effects.description: Skarö's on-island public confidence is softening and pressure is mounting for the Cabinet to take over the response or adopt a more visible defence role, at the very moment a pre-staged reinforcement echelon and a trigger-based pre-authorisation are ready to execute; any move to visibly strengthen the defence role would shift the response from civil-led to defence-led and hand the takeover/militarisation narratives their subject, while inaction lets essential-service margins keep tightening.
effects.rationale: County reporting shows softening confidence and Cabinet-takeover pressure (419b155a) concurrent with corridor friction (0f2da2d2), while Defence Command's pre-staged echelon (62f23a6b) and the standing trigger-based pre-authorisation (a3aac1cc, d33037c5) provide a ready mechanism for exactly the more visible defence role being demanded. The combination makes the Cabinet's visible-posture decision the central political crux of the turn, a convergence no single outcome alone produced.

effects.description: Drevna's standing civilian cable-repair-vessel offer is now publicly moot: repair is already under way at the fault by the Aldmoor civilian vessel under Vardland oversight in the notified safety zone, so the offer no longer reads as a constructive civilian contribution and further hollows Drevna's reasonable-neighbour posture.
effects.rationale: Drevna's offer is on the public record (43bfec7a), but safe access and repair work have already begun by the Aldmoor civilian vessel (3f36ef87, 100d5c0c), so the standing offer has lost its object; combined with the failure of Drevna's escalation framing (1a8ab819), the offer's redundancy visibly undercuts its intended reasonable, civilian image.

effects.description: The Skarö cable is restored and the Aldmoor escort/MPA element stands down while Skarö's two-day essential-service reserve floor is still unrebuilt; the island enters the post-repair window with the priority now shifted to rebuilding reserves through normal county-led resupply, with no repair safety zone or foreign escort layer still in place.
effects.rationale: Aldmoor's completed repair and scheduled stand-down (event 5935; effects 81b92... and e69facdf...) occur while the county's staged release failed to rebuild the reserve floor and corridor friction persisted (event 5923; effects e90d... and 3e439e...). Together, these outcomes create a recovery gap that neither outcome alone would establish: the cable milestone has passed before the reserve buffer has been restored.

effects.description: By the close of the turn, the reduction of armed presence on the Skarö corridor has occurred through Aldmoor's scheduled, time-limited stand-down rather than through Drevna's reciprocal-restraint proposal; Drevna's accepted de-confliction margins and its mutual-restraint proposal therefore remain on the record without any reciprocal concession having been granted in return.
effects.rationale: Drevna accepted the de-confliction channel, directed wider stand-off margins and tabled the mutual-restraint proposal, but Vardland declined the reciprocal pullback (event 5865; effects 6850..., 98e85..., 3e2b... and f09b51...). Aldmoor then completed and stood down under the original terms (event 5935; effect e69facdf...). The interaction closes Drevna's corridor-related initiative without the concrete result it was designed to produce.

effects.description: The trigger-verification protocol remains in force after the cable repair, but its 'safety-zone incident' trigger now lacks a geographic referent because the notified repair safety zone has lapsed; port, airfield and supply-lane triggers remain verifiable, so the protocol is only partially executable until a new zone is notified or the protocol is updated.
effects.rationale: Defence Command operationalised a rehearsed trigger-verification protocol covering qualifying safety-zone/port/airfield/supply-lane incidents (event 5895; effect f9927...), while Aldmoor's completed repair caused the notified repair safety zone to lapse (event 5935; effect 81b92...). The two successful outcomes together leave a written trigger category with no active geographic definition at the moment the Drevnian exercise continues nearby.

effects.description: Skarö Hamn is operating again at normal manual throughput with its control and fuel-dispensing systems restored, while the same systems are now the subject of an active digital-evidence chain under Vardland's national cyber-security authority. For the up-to-14-day term of Aldmoor's embedded civilian forensic team, the restored harbour systems are simultaneously working infrastructure and preserved forensic exhibits.
effects.rationale: The County and CCA completed the Hamn restoration and rebuilt the reserve floor (events 6064 and 6086; effect 4dc06257-e46d-47af-af5a-76a5cabf9da6), while Aldmoor's accepted civilian team embeds under Vardland's national cyber-security authority with evidence routed to the independent investigation (event 6102; effect ed11a371-b616-457a-b17f-c9a8a549cae1). No single outcome created this dual operational-and-evidence status; it emerges only from the completed restoration and the forensic team's active presence together.

effects.description: A visible public benchmark for acceptable foreign civilian assistance to Vardland critical infrastructure is now on the record: Aldmoor's civilian technical/forensic team is accepted, time-limited, under Vardland national direction and has no armed footprint, while Drevna's civilian restoration offer remains formally declined on national-custody and evidence-integrity grounds. The two offers are directly comparable public facts that any actor can cite.
effects.rationale: This aggregate consequence combines Drevna's publicised offer and escalation framing (event 6014; effect 470931c0-f86f-476b-b74c-f742a5256033), the Cabinet's formal decline of Drevna's offer while requesting Aldmoor's civilian team (event 6032; effect 0cee85b1-aea2-4ce7-8399-56f35d073caa), and Aldmoor's accepted civilian, no-armed-footprint commitment aligned with Vardland's update (event 6102; effects 472e4413-0db3-4fae-8e80-b9be9392b3e0 and ed11a371-b616-457a-b17f-c9a8a549cae1). Each outcome alone only established one side of the contrast; together they define a public reference point for any future foreign civilian offer to Skarö.

effects.description: Skarö Hamn's restored control and fuel-dispensing systems are no longer simultaneously working infrastructure and preserved forensic exhibits under Aldmoor's embedded team: the up-to-14-day civilian forensic task has ended, evidence custody has passed to Vardland's agreed chain, and the systems now operate as normal port assets while any investigative work proceeds from the handed-over evidence.
effects.rationale: Active effect 526b made the harbour systems dual-status 'for the up-to-14-day term of Aldmoor's embedded civilian forensic team.' Event 6232 and its created effect a0aa record that the team completed its scope on schedule, handed over evidence through the agreed chain, and stood down with no extension. Together these end the forensic-exhibit phase for the operational systems without prejudging the investigation.

effects.description: Drevna's public invitation to Aldmoor to endorse its 'equal, custody-neutral, time-limited' treatment standard has no acceptance on the record: Aldmoor's closing statement aligns with Vardland's verified account, restates that any further Aldmoor role would require a fresh Vardland Cabinet request, and offers no additional capability, so Drevna's proposed standard remains solely a Drevnian position.
effects.rationale: Event 6160 records Drevna's invitation for Aldmoor to endorse the equal-treatment standard. Event 6232 provides Aldmoor's only response in the turn: an aligned closing statement, no extension, no renewed role, and no additional capability. Read against active effect e61's public benchmark, the record closes with Drevna's framing receiving no allied endorsement.

effects.description: Drevna's storm-time civilian assistance offer times out without uptake: with the storm closure passed, CCA having initiated the first post-storm resupply under standing release authority, and the county confirming the first opening-window berth and priority list, the storm-scoped Drevnian offer is no longer actionable and remains on the public record only as a rhetorical position.
effects.rationale: Event 6160 framed Drevna's civilian repair/salvage-capable support as available for the storm period. Event 6208 records that the storm closure ended, the verified full-window account was published, and CCA began the first post-storm resupply; event 6223 confirms the county-directed berth and priority list. Combined, these leave no operational slot for the storm-time offer within the turn.

effects.description: Skarö is running on backup generation. Hospitals, water and heating are prioritised, and fuel must arrive by sea or air.
The Skarö garrison is at internal readiness by order of Defence Command. This is not public.
Vardland has not declared heightened alert. The Skarö garrison is at its normal peacetime level.
No foreign military forces operate on Vardland territory, in its territorial waters or in its airspace.
Skarö's only subsea power and data cable to the mainland has failed. The cause has not been established.
Online claims that the Vardland government caused the outage through neglect are spreading quickly.
A large Drevnian naval and air exercise is under way in international waters near Skarö.
Skarö County Administration directs the civil emergency response on the island.

Despite the operational package, friction or delay in the congested corridor disrupts the fuel or repair schedule, tightening Skarö's margins and giving Drevna's foreign-militarisation framing fresh traction.

Aldmoor's support elements covered by the recorded consent run on Defence Command timelines: the joint liaison cell is active, defensive escorts accompany designated fuel-supply vessels on the Skarö run, the civilian repair vessel continues in the notified safety zone under Vardland oversight, and the sanitised technical evidence package is handed to the independent investigation. The earlier standing fact that no foreign military forces were present no longer holds.

Drevna's standing civilian cable-repair-vessel offer is now publicly moot: repair is already under way at the fault by the Aldmoor civilian vessel under Vardland oversight in the notified safety zone, so the offer no longer reads as a constructive civilian contribution and further hollows Drevna's reasonable-neighbour posture.

The escalation framing fails to take hold: Vardland and Aldmoor publicly point to the county-requested support, the package's time/scope limits and Drevna's own large exercise, so the de-confliction proposal is read as a pretext and Drevna's reasonable-neighbour posture is undercut.

CCA stands up a single public-information cell with the County and Defence Command, publishing verified operational facts and countering the false neglect/takeover narratives and external amplification without official state attribution.

The notified safety zone is in force and the Aldmoor civilian cable-repair vessel begins repair work under Vardland oversight this turn; full cable restoration remains possible only from the following turn.

Essential-service margins tighten faster than planned: resupply does not fully keep pace with demand, ferry departures and staff rotation face crowding or delay, the repair vessel is still not at the fault, and county-led updates only partially counter online narratives, so public confidence softens and pressure grows for the Cabinet to take over the response or for a more visible Defence role.

Drevna's formal de-confliction proposal covering repair/supply routes and the exercise area, and its standing civilian cable-repair-vessel offer, are on the public record while Drevna's exercise remains confined to international waters.

Skarö's on-island public confidence is softening and pressure is mounting for the Cabinet to take over the response or adopt a more visible defence role, at the very moment a pre-staged reinforcement echelon and a trigger-based pre-authorisation are ready to execute; any move to visibly strengthen the defence role would shift the response from civil-led to defence-led and hand the takeover/militarisation narratives their subject, while inaction lets essential-service margins keep tightening.
Defence Command pre-stages the first reinforcement echelon at mainland departure points.

Skarö's essential services keep running through the turn on the scheduled chain; public trust holds and the externally amplified rumour campaign fails to move opinion, with the response staying visibly county-led and defence support confined to civil-requested roles.
The tabled technical de-confliction parameters take practical effect with the Drevnian exercise, and priority fuel reaches Skarö this turn without harmful interruption.
The Cabinet grants the fallback standing trigger-based pre-authorisation to execute the prepared package upon independent verification of a stated trigger.

CCA establishes the Skarö fuel and medical resupply chain in coordination with the County, stages the national generator stockpile and chronic-care/dialysis lines as contingency, and files the 48-hour Treasury case.

The repair-and-supply corridor off Skarö is now simultaneously hosting Aldmoor defensive escorts and MPA surveillance sorties, the Drevnian exercise in adjacent international waters, the notified safety zone with the civilian repair vessel, and the scheduled fuel and medical resupply ships; despite the de-confliction parameters being in force, this concentrated traffic produces repeated close encounters and scheduling friction that disrupts the fuel and repair schedule. Drevna's escalation framing failed to take hold, but the genuine congestion now gives its incident-risk warning concrete, observable material that Vardland's own public line cannot dismiss.

The Cabinet orders the Skarö lifeline operation: CCA and Defence Command are directed to coordinate priority fuel shipments with the county, Defence Command to establish a notified safety zone at the cable fault, and the independent technical investigation to expedite evidence collection from the fault site, the survey vessel and nearby traffic.

Defence Command is thereby enabled to move first reinforcements to Skarö within about one day by air and two days by sea, and to cover the cable landing site, port and airfield as a single task, subject to the trigger condition.

Consolidated county civil-continuity directive is in force: distribution priorities, a two-day reserve-buffer floor for fuel and medical essentials at hospital, crisis centre and water/sewage plant, police-/port-authority-led access management at Skarö Hamn and the cable landing site, an orderly ferry-departure and essential-staff-rotation arrangement, daily county-led public updates with verified facts and departure guidance, and a formal county request to Defence Command for low-key surveillance and transport support under support-to-civil rules.
Cabinet confirms CCA's standing release authority and makes the contingent priority-resupply funding decision; no heightened alert is declared and no visible reinforcement is ordered.

The external target is not secured: Vardland does not get a settled, visible civilian-corridor outcome or a decisive denial of Drevna's framing by turn's end, leaving the no-alert line still exposed to political pressure and Drevna able to contest the corridor picture.

The reciprocal stand-off is not accepted: Vardland does not treat the armed escort layer as the congestion driver, Aldmoor escort and MPA transits continue under existing authorities, and the immediate corridor’s armed foreign footprint is unchanged. Drevna’s unilateral margins and proposal stay on the record, but there is no reciprocal concession and the corridor’s congestion and attribution questions remain open.

The shared corridor remains congested — ferry or staff-rotation delays and repair-corridor pressure at the cable landing site — producing the verified conditions for Cabinet review and reviving takeover pressure and criticism of county leadership.

The joint public-information cell expands the daily verified update to radio and the mainland relay, publishing checkable aggregate corridor data (window adherence, escort placement inside sequenced windows, incident log, reserve levels) without disclosing ship movements.

The 72-hour Ska rö resupply and transit window table is finalised between CCA, Skarö County Administration and Defence Command, with priority fuel and medical runs and diesel/dialysis pre-positioned at mainland departure points, releasable within hours on the County's call without further Cabinet decision.

Skarö County executes the agreed staged release of reserve generators, fuel and chronic-care/dialysis lines under its standing call and keeps the response county-led, civilian and low-key, with daily verified updates and continued police/port-authority access management.

Drevna accepts the Vardland-proposed near-real-time de-confliction channel and has directed its exercise command to hold additional unilateral stand-off margins around the notified repair safety zone and the Skarö resupply track; the resulting schedule changes are shared through that channel.
The Skarö subsea power and data cable is repaired and brought back online; Skarö returns to mains power, ending backup-generation dependence, and the notified repair safety zone lapses.

By the close of the turn, the reduction of armed presence on the Skarö corridor has occurred through Aldmoor's scheduled, time-limited stand-down rather than through Drevna's reciprocal-restraint proposal; Drevna's accepted de-confliction margins and its mutual-restraint proposal therefore remain on the record without any reciprocal concession having been granted in return.
Drevna tables the mutual-restraint proposal: Aldmoor’s escort and MPA transits are invited to mirror those margins, with corridor de-confliction handled through the technical channel.

The completed, published restoration removes the repair-corridor incident and foreign-militarisation material basis and allows fuel and medical resupply to return to a normal cadence under county-led direction.

The trigger-verification protocol remains in force after the cable repair, but its 'safety-zone incident' trigger now lacks a geographic referent because the notified repair safety zone has lapsed; port, airfield and supply-lane triggers remain verifiable, so the protocol is only partially executable until a new zone is notified or the protocol is updated.

The temporary consented Aldmoor role concludes on schedule and on the record: the civilian repair vessel, defensive escorts and MPA surveillance stand down under the original terms with no standing deployment, and the joint cell publishes verified completion and corridor receipts.
Despite the release, corridor and on-island logistics friction prevents rebuilding the two-day floor: essential-service margins stay tight or worsen.

The Skarö cable is restored and the Aldmoor escort/MPA element stands down while Skarö's two-day essential-service reserve floor is still unrebuilt; the island enters the post-repair window with the priority now shifted to rebuilding reserves through normal county-led resupply, with no repair safety zone or foreign escort layer still in place.

Vardland publishes the verified corridor schedule, acknowledges Drevna's wider margins as welcome safety measures, declines the reciprocal pullback, keeps the invited Aldmoor escort within existing time-limited consent, and sets the standby arrangements in writing.

A standing, rehearsed trigger-verification protocol is in force at Defence Command: a 24/7 channel, drawing on county-requested surveillance and civilian-fused feeds, can verify qualifying safety-zone/port/airfield/supply-lane incidents against the Cabinet's pre-agreed criteria quickly enough to trigger the pre-authorised air echelon within the one-day air window. No heightened alert is declared, no reinforcement is visibly deployed, and the response remains county- and civil-led until a trigger is verified.

Vardland formally declines Drevna's Skarö Hamn restoration offer while the intrusion is unattributed, citing national custody of the control/fuel-dispensing systems and digital evidence chain; the offer remains on the record.

The published receipts give a checkable sovereign answer to the accept-or-look-slow choice: authority-friction and takeover pressure recede, the restoration-pace dispute loses its factual basis, and Drevna’s selective-engagement framing finds no new subject.

Because no authoritative Cabinet update to the trigger criteria is established, the protocol's full executability and the lawfulness of the posture remain contestable; authority-friction and takeover pressure continues to hold public attention despite the low-key posture.

Vardland's formal written request defines a strictly time-limited Aldmoor civilian technical/forensic role embedded under national cyber-security direction; Aldmoor's decision on providing the team remains pending.

The escalation framing gains public standing: renewing an armed foreign layer on the corridor or moving the response to an alert footing is publicly treated as escalation, and Drevna's conduct gives no public basis for treating the outage or restoration as attack or interference.

Aldmoor's parliament announcement aligns with Vardland's published verified update, restating that the role is civilian, sovereignty-respecting and time-limited, with no base and no renewal of an armed role; any further Aldmoor role requires fresh Vardland Cabinet agreement. The public record gives Drevna's base-on-Skarö and escalation/selective-engagement framings no new subject, and the response remains visibly county-led and civilian.

Skarö Hamn control/fuel-dispensing systems are restored on the published county restoration track; manual throughput normalises, the two-day essential-service reserve floor is rebuilt, and a standing releasable contingency stock plus normal-cadence resupply are in place, keeping essential services secure under county-led civil direction.

Skarö Hamn is operating again at normal manual throughput with its control and fuel-dispensing systems restored, while the same systems are now the subject of an active digital-evidence chain under Vardland's national cyber-security authority. For the up-to-14-day term of Aldmoor's embedded civilian forensic team, the restored harbour systems are simultaneously working infrastructure and preserved forensic exhibits.

Defence Command continues the standing County-requested watch and evidence routing; no visible reinforcement or heightened alert is introduced, no renewed armed foreign layer is ordered, and the air backstop remains available only on the County's call.

Restoration progress remains disputed and the two-day reserve floor is not rebuilt; Drevna's framing of the decision as selective foreign engagement persists, keeping restoration-pace, sovereignty and authority-friction pressure alive.

The pending harbour-restoration choice becomes a visible public fact: Vardland's answer to the offer is on the record, and public discussion reads it as either accommodation of Drevna's civilian role or as slow, strained, authority-friction-affected restoration, with reduced-throughput and unrebuilt-reserve numbers carrying that framing.

Drevna's leadership extends the exercise by one week. It wants a visible result before the exercise ends: a public Vardland concession, a public dispute between Vardland and Aldmoor, or evidence that Vardland's authorities contradict each other. A quiet end counts as failure.

Drevna's civilian-scope offer for Skarö Hamn restoration (specialists and restoration equipment deployable within days at Vardland's request) is public and stands ready; Drevna confirms its exercise holds the agreed de-confliction parameters and stand-off margins, accommodates revised harbour/transit windows through the near-real-time channel, and states publicly that any renewed armed foreign layer on the corridor or alert-based militarisation would be escalation inconsistent with Vardland's county-led civilian posture.

Residual trigger-criteria contestability remains a Defence/Cabinet governance matter, but verified restoration receipts shift public attention away from authority-friction and takeover pressure, and Drevna's selective-engagement framing finds no new subject by the close of turn.

By the close of the turn, Skarö Hamn’s control/fuel-dispensing systems are restored or on a published, checkable restoration track; manual throughput normalises, the two-day essential-service reserve floor is rebuilt, and essential services keep running under county-led civilian direction.

Aldmoor's parliament will debate the Skarö crisis within days. Your government must state what role Aldmoor will play and for how long. Without a formal written Vardland request that defines that role, it will announce that Aldmoor forces stay outside Vardland's territory, waters and airspace.

The control and fuel-dispensing systems at Skarö harbour go offline after a cyber intrusion of unknown origin. Fuel and cargo can still be handled manually, but at about a third of normal speed until the systems are restored. The harbour operator asks for national help.

Daily verified county updates continue from the joint public-information cell; police/port-authority access management remains at Skarö Hamn and the cable landing site with low-key civil-requested Defence support, no heightened alert, visible reinforcement or renewed armed foreign layer; Drevna's civilian offer stays at national level with no county uptake; the air backstop remains on County call only.

A visible public benchmark for acceptable foreign civilian assistance to Vardland critical infrastructure is now on the record: Aldmoor's civilian technical/forensic team is accepted, time-limited, under Vardland national direction and has no armed footprint, while Drevna's civilian restoration offer remains formally declined on national-custody and evidence-integrity grounds. The two offers are directly comparable public facts that any actor can cite.

Aldmoor's civilian technical/forensic team is confirmed and stood up under Vardland's national cyber-security direction for a defined term of up to 14 days with a clear scope and end point, no armed footprint and no standing presence; work is directed by Vardland, evidence is routed through the agreed chain to Vardland's independent investigation, and only sanitised technical content is shared with no official attribution.

CCA sustains and expands the Skarö Hamn surge under County direction—ICS/cyber-security and manual-handling specialist support, prioritised restoration equipment and satellite comms—while publishing daily verified restoration milestones, throughput, window adherence and reserve-floor data from the joint public-information cell; the present outage is not treated as a heightened-alert trigger, no visible reinforcement or renewed armed foreign layer is introduced, the air backstop remains on County call only, and any trigger-criteria change is left to the Cabinet on the record.

Drevna's accommodation, selective-sovereignty and unequal-treatment framings keep public standing through the storm: the element deployment and offer decline remain checkable as an authorities contradiction and unequal treatment on Vardland's own record, the public contest stays open, and Drevna's framing campaign continues toward a visible result.

Drevna's public invitation to Aldmoor to endorse its 'equal, custody-neutral, time-limited' treatment standard has no acceptance on the record: Aldmoor's closing statement aligns with Vardland's verified account, restates that any further Aldmoor role would require a fresh Vardland Cabinet request, and offers no additional capability, so Drevna's proposed standard remains solely a Drevnian position.

Skarö Hamn's restored control and fuel-dispensing systems are no longer simultaneously working infrastructure and preserved forensic exhibits under Aldmoor's embedded team: the up-to-14-day civilian forensic task has ended, evidence custody has passed to Vardland's agreed chain, and the systems now operate as normal port assets while any investigative work proceeds from the handed-over evidence.

A Drevnian-flagged fishing vessel reports engine failure and drops anchor inside Vardland's territorial waters, about two nautical miles from the Skarö cable landing site. Its master asks for a tow and refuses a boarding inspection. Drevna says the vessel is in distress.

The storm closure passes without a verified port, airfield, supply-lane or vessel incident, without interference and without evidence-backed attribution; essential services and protected sites remain county-led and the anchored Drevnian vessel is released only on the published safety condition when weather permits.

The national weather service warns of a severe winter storm. Sea and air links to Skarö are expected to close for up to four days from the end of this turn. Anything the island needs during the storm must arrive before then.

Drevna's storm-time civilian assistance offer times out without uptake: with the storm closure passed, CCA having initiated the first post-storm resupply under standing release authority, and the county confirming the first opening-window berth and priority list, the storm-scoped Drevnian offer is no longer actionable and remains on the public record only as a rhetorical position.

The joint cell publishes the verified full-window storm/recovery account (pre-storm departure and delivery receipts, reserve-floor logs, county-led civil continuity, the support-to-civil element's defined role and stand-down, the vessel's securing/inspection/release, and the Aldmoor forensic-team terms); CCA exercises the Cabinet-confirmed standing release authority to initiate the first post-storm resupply for stock rebuilding, and submits the sustained-operation costing to Treasury.

Drevna's public humanitarian demarche is on the record—calling for storm-time civilian assistance to Skarö to be treated on equal, custody-neutral, time-limited terms under Vardland direction, offering Drevna civilian repair/salvage-capable support without conditions, recording reliance on the safe sequence and prompt release after inspection, and inviting Aldmoor to endorse the standard—and Drevna issues a flag-state instruction to the vessel's master to accept tow and securing first, with inspection only after the vessel is safe and secured and with consular observation at a safe distance.

The Drevnian-flagged fishing vessel is towed and secured at the eastern anchorage clear of the cable landing site and critical infrastructure; a routine territorial-waters inspection with consular observation proceeds without forcible boarding, with release depending on weather and crew-safety conditions. The Cabinet declines Drevna's storm-time civilian assistance offer as not required on the recorded national custody/evidence-integrity grounds.

Aldmoor's civilian technical/forensic team completed its defined up-to-14-day scope on schedule, handed over evidence through the agreed chain for Vardland's independent investigation, and stood down cleanly with no extension, no standing presence and no armed footprint; Aldmoor publicly confirmed this completion/stand-down aligned with the joint cell's verified full-window storm/recovery account and restated that any further role would require a fresh formal Vardland Cabinet request.

On the public record, Drevna's accommodation, unequal-treatment and authorities-contradiction framings lose standing: the published, checkable account is accepted as the consistent county-led civilian record, the quiet-militarisation and abandonment readings gain no traction, and the public contest closes as the crisis returns to normal cadence.

Drevna's framing takes hold on the public record: Vardland's storm-era handling of the vessel is seen as an accommodation of the Drevna-proposed safe sequence, and Vardland's non-acceptance of Drevna's civilian assistance is recorded as a checkable policy/political choice of unequal treatment rather than a custody/safety necessity; no storm-window incident or evidence-backed attribution involving the vessel or the exercise enters the record.

Through the four-day storm closure, Defence Command keeps the county-requested logistic/engineering element sustaining cable-landing-site, port-ham and airfield resilience and supporting the coast guard in holding the secured Drevnian vessel clear of critical infrastructure, while the standing verification watch, evidence routing and joint-cell verified reporting continue without heightened alert, visible reinforcement, town presence, armed foreign layer or official attribution; the pre-authorised package remains executable on verified port/airfield/supply-lane triggers or Cabinet decision once links reopen.

The final pre-storm resupply is completed and a small unarmed logistic/engineering element is in place on Skarö as county-requested storm assurance under support-to-civil rules; no heightened alert, visible garrison reinforcement, town presence, or armed foreign layer are introduced.

scenario_rules.text: Only the Vardland Cabinet can declare heightened alert, partial or full. A declaration takes effect as a public fact from the turn it is adjudicated. Under heightened alert, Defence Command may call up reservists and move units onto Skarö without further approval, and the Civil Contingencies Agency may direct fuel, generators and medical supplies across counties. Without a declaration, neither may do so.

Without heightened alert, Defence Command may support civil authorities on Vardland territory with transport, engineering, surveillance and protection of military sites, but only at a civil authority's request. It may not order a civil evacuation, restrict civilian movement or use force against civilians under any alert level. Those powers belong to civil authorities.

Skarö County Administration directs the civil emergency response on Skarö: shelters, evacuation, and priorities for power, fuel and water between essential services. It keeps that direction until the Cabinet transfers it to national level. The Civil Contingencies Agency coordinates and supplies, but does not command, the county response.

Foreign military forces may operate on Vardland territory, in its territorial waters or in its airspace only with a Cabinet decision. Aldmoor cannot deploy forces there by its own decision, whatever its treaty obligations or its assessment of the threat. Consent may be limited in scope, place and time.

An armed attack on Vardland obliges Aldmoor to consult with Vardland on assistance. It does not oblige Aldmoor to deploy forces. Incidents below the threshold of armed attack, such as sabotage that cannot be attributed, cyber disruption or disinformation, trigger no treaty obligation. They may still justify voluntary assistance.

Only the Vardland Cabinet can officially attribute a hostile act to a state. Other Vardland actors may share evidence with the Cabinet or with Aldmoor, but cannot make an official attribution. An attribution without supporting evidence in an active fact is a political claim, not an established fact.

Repairing the Skarö subsea cable needs a cable-repair vessel on site and safe access to the fault. Repair cannot be completed in the turn in which safe access is first secured. At the earliest, it completes in the following turn. Until then, Skarö depends on backup generation and fuel deliveries by sea or air.

Military strength and readiness are qualitative in this scenario. No Argument succeeds or fails on unit counts, weapon ranges or attrition. Posture is judged from established facts and public Resources, and a claim of superiority is not evidence.

game.scenario_summary: A four-turn, six-actor total-defence crisis in a fictional northern European setting. The island county of Skarö, which belongs to the Kingdom of Vardland, lies in the Eastern Sea close to the Drevnian Federation. Skarö's only subsea power and data cable to the mainland has failed. The island now runs on backup generation, while a large Drevnian naval exercise continues nearby and conflicting stories about the cause spread online. No state of war exists. Vardland's government, armed forces, civil-contingencies agency and Skarö's county administration share responsibility for the response under overlapping rules of authority. An allied partner, the Kingdom of Aldmoor, offers help that needs Vardland's consent. Drevna seeks political advantage below the threshold of armed conflict. Each turn represents about three days. New developments arrive at the start of turns 3 and 4 whatever the Actors have done. Military posture is qualitative: there are no unit counts, ranges or combat tables.

messages.text:
From the Government of the Kingdom of Vardland. We thank Aldmoor for its offer of assistance and for its readiness to help its partner at short notice. We are grateful and we intend to take it up - on terms that Vardland controls and that fit the situation as it actually is.

The Cabinet is prepared to consent, by formal decision, to Aldmoor surveillance aircraft operating in Vardland airspace and territorial waters around Skarö for a defined period, to strengthen shared situational awareness while the cable fault is investigated and repaired. We ask that we agree the scope, geography and time limits together, and that operations be coordinated with our own authorities to avoid any ambiguity or incident.

We would also welcome a conversation about whether Aldmoor can make naval assets available to help secure safe access to the fault for the repair vessel when the time comes - our primary need is to restore power and communications to Skarö as quickly and safely as possible.

We are not, at this stage, seeking ground forces on Skarö. That would change the character of our response and we judge it neither necessary nor wise now. We reserve the option to revisit if the situation worsens.

Please let us know your assessment and proposed modalities, including how quickly surveillance support can begin once our decision is formalised.

Statement from the Government of the Kingdom of Vardland on the Skarö cable failure.

The government is treating the failure of Skarö's power and data cable with the full seriousness it deserves. An independent investigation into the cause is under way. We will not speculate: we will establish the facts and report them to the public when they are established.

The first priority of the government is the safety and welfare of Skarö's residents. Fuel deliveries continue, back-up generation is being sustained, and additional capacity is being organised. Skarö County Administration leads the island's civil response and has the full support of national authorities and of our allies, with whom we are in close contact.

Claims circulating online that the government caused this outage through neglect are false. The public should rely on official channels for information. Vardland will respond calmly, lawfully and in full strength, and we will restore power and communications to Skarö as quickly as possible.

For consultation, restricted: Defence Command's assessment records a Drevnian-contracted survey vessel moving slowly along the Skarö cable route about twelve hours before the failure — position and speed only, no observed activity. We assess sabotage plausible but not proven, and note this year's Drevnian exercise includes landing ships. We welcome Aldmoor's readiness to assist. Per our law, any deployment of Aldmoor forces on Vardland territory, in our waters or in our airspace requires a Vardland Cabinet decision; we will advise you promptly if and when that occurs. We propose continued dialogue on contingency coordination within existing treaty consultations.

Statement from Skarö County Administration: The County Administration is directing the civil emergency response on Skarö. Backup generation is prioritising the hospital, water and heating. Fuel for the island's generators is being secured and a tanker delivery is being arranged to arrive within the coming days; the port will give priority to supply. We ask residents to limit non-essential electricity use and to follow official channels, which we will update daily. Reports that the army is preparing to take over Skarö are false: the civil response remains in the hands of the County Administration, and we will say so plainly if that ever changes. Please treat unverified claims online with caution — official county channels are your reliable source.

From Skarö County Administration — formal request. (1) Prioritise delivery of the fuel tanker from the mainland port to Skarö: we hold roughly five days of backup-generation fuel at current consumption and need a reliable resupply soon. (2) Release mobile generators and satellite communication kits from the national stockpile to cover the hospital and the county crisis centre. (3) Confirm safe-berth priority at Skarö port for the tanker and any follow-on supply vessels. Separately, we are sharing for your assessment the grid operator's confidential finding that the fault is consistent with an anchor or dragged object approximately 18 km off the coast; official attribution remains a matter for the Cabinet. The County Administration retains direction of the civil response and asks that this continue unless national direction clearly serves the island better. We are ready to co-operate fully and to provide whatever information you need.

From Skarö County Administration — formal request for military support to civil authorities. We ask Defence Command to assist with: transporting fuel, generators and specialist personnel to Skarö; securing the port and the cable landing site; and surveillance of the sea and air approaches to the island while the tanker sails. We ask that support be calibrated and low-key: the people of Skarö are steadied by a civil-led response, and a visible military build-up could undermine public calm. Support should remain support, with the County Administration keeping direction of the civil emergency response. Please confirm what you can lawfully provide under current arrangements, and tell us of any requested capability that would require a heightened-alert decision so we can raise it with the Cabinet ourselves.

OFFICIAL STATEMENT OF THE DREVNIAN FEDERATION ON THE SITUATION IN THE EASTERN SEA.

The Drevnian Federation has followed with concern the hardship that the failure of the subsea cable serving the island county of Skarö has caused for its residents. As a manifestation of good neighbourliness, the Federation is prepared to dispatch a civilian cable-repair vessel, operated under Drevnian flag by a commercial operator and supervised by our maritime authorities, to assist in restoring power and connectivity to the island as soon as Vardland signals its readiness. The offer is purely civilian. It entails no military element, no change in the security posture of any state, and no claim over Skarö or its waters.

We remain ready to agree transparency and de-confliction arrangements covering all activity in the Eastern Sea, including our long-announced exercise, which continues — as always — entirely in international waters and airspace and in strict compliance with international law.

The Federation calls on all parties to treat this matter as what it is: a serious technical incident affecting ordinary people. The facts should be established calmly and objectively. The Federation has nothing to hide in relation to this incident and will cooperate with any objective, technical examination conducted by Vardland's own authorities or by international civilian experts. Politicising the outage, or turning it into a pretext for militarisation, would only add to the suffering of the island's residents and is in no one's interest.

TO THE GOVERNMENTS OF VARDLAND AND ALDMOOR, AND TO THE AUTHORITIES OF SKARÖ COUNTY: AN APPEAL FOR A CIVILIAN, ISLANDER-FIRST RESPONSE.

The people of Skarö need fuel, power, working hospitals and functioning communications. What they do not need is further escalation around their shores. The Drevnian Federation therefore calls on all governments to keep this response civilian, humanitarian and fast.

We call in particular on the Kingdom of Aldmoor to route any assistance through civilian mechanisms and through Vardland's proper constitutional processes. A foreign military deployment to Skarö, its waters or its airspace would be an escalation that endangers rather than reassures the islanders and would deepen the crisis. Any such step taken without the genuine, transparent consent of Vardland's accountable institutions would further damage trust across the region.

The Federation's own posture in the Eastern Sea remains unchanged, lawful and transparent. We invite Vardland to accept our civilian repair offer and to work with us on de-confliction, so that every vessel and aircraft in the region operates with full predictability. The alternative — talk of bases, reinforcements and foreign deployments — leads nowhere good for anyone.

QUESTIONS THE FEDERATION BELIEVES SKARÖ'S RESIDENTS ARE ENTITLED TO HAVE ANSWERED.

Days into the outage, Skarö's residents are still being told in general terms that 'all possibilities are being examined', while no heightened-alert declaration has been made and no publicly explained plan for restoring the island's power and connectivity has been presented. The Federation does not presume to direct Vardland's internal procedures. But when an island depends on backup generation and delivered fuel, its residents deserve a clear, timely and honest account of what is being done and by whom.

For its part, the Federation stands ready to help today, with civilian means and without preconditions: a repair vessel, fuel or humanitarian goods. We will not dramatise, and we will not lecture. We simply note that in this crisis, the fastest offer of help available to the islanders is civilian help from across the Eastern Sea.

Civil Contingencies Agency to Skarö County Administration. We are fully engaged in support of your county-directed response. Current national readiness: backup-generation fuel for Skarö is about five days at current use; a fuel tanker is at the mainland port, about one day's sailing, and needs a safe berth; our national generator stockpile can cover about half of Skarö's backup generation should primary units fail; satellite communications kits are limited and we propose prioritising your hospital and county crisis centre. Please confirm: (a) current fuel burn and minimum reserve you want kept, (b) harbour/airfield receiving capacity and any berthing constraints, (c) whether you want us to pre-position generators now, and (d) your current priorities for power, fuel and water so we can synchronise deliveries. We also propose a single-voice public information arrangement, with your office as the authoritative on-island source supported by our national information cell, so the population hears accurate, coordinated information.
