Civil Contingencies Agency brief for Cabinet — Skarö. Time is a factor: backup-generation fuel on Skarö is roughly five days at current use and resupply must arrive by sea or air, while the Drevnian exercise creates friction on access. Two decisions we respectfully ask Cabinet to consider: 1) Authority — under current rules this Agency cannot direct fuel, generators or medical supplies across counties without a Cabinet heightened-alert declaration. If the outage persists, cross-county supply will very likely be needed. We ask Cabinet to decide whether to declare heightened alert, or at minimum to authorise the Agency to direct cross-county civil supplies for the duration of the crisis. This is a civil-supply measure; nothing beyond what Cabinet decides will be pursued. 2) Information — our analysis has traced part of the rumour campaign blaming the government to accounts outside Vardland, with moderate confidence. We provide this evidence to Cabinet; official attribution is Cabinet's alone, and we will hold the public line of 'cause under investigation' until you decide otherwise. We propose a coordinated inter-agency public-information arrangement so all agencies speak with one credible voice and the response is seen as civil-led. For situational awareness: the contracted cable-repair vessel remains in dry dock for several more days; medical supplies on Skarö are adequate for about two weeks; and limited, time-scoped Aldmoor logistics support could be considered if fuel access is blocked — consent is Cabinet's alone.

Civil Contingencies Agency coordination note. At Skarö County's request and within your legal remit, we ask Defence Command to consider supporting civil resupply of Skarö: transport for fuel and mobile generators by sea or air, and safe-berthing/safety information for the fuel tanker given the Drevnian exercise nearby. Please share your situation picture with our logistics cell so we can schedule civilian deliveries safely. We also ask that civil emergency direction on Skarö remain with the County Administration, with military activity coordinated and kept operationally distinct in public communication. We propose aligning our public statements so the population receives coherent information and the response is visibly civil-led. We remain available to coordinate details.

Statement of the Kingdom of Aldmoor on Skaro.

Aldmoor stands with its ally, the Kingdom of Vardland. The disruption of Skaro's power supply affects real people, and the unsourced claims circulating online help no one. We have offered Vardland's government limited, clearly defined assistance: surveillance near Skaro, a naval escort for vital supplies if it wishes, and a cable-repair vessel that can reach Skaro within two days of a request. All of this will be provided only with and under Vardland's consent, limited in scope and time as Vardland chooses. Aldmoor is not seeking a base on Skaro and seeks no permanent presence there. We respect Vardland's decisions on its own territory, in its waters and in its airspace, and we call on all parties to exercise restraint while the cause of the outage is established.

Statement of the Drevnian Federation on Skarö.

Drevna shares the concern of the people of Skarö and welcomes the calm, lawful handling of the outage by the Government of Vardland and by Skarö County Administration, whose civilian leadership of the emergency we fully support. Our earlier offer stands: a civilian Drevnian cable-repair vessel, crewed by civilians, can reach the fault area within days of acceptance and would work under Vardland's authority on fully transparent terms. We will cooperate fully with any independent, technical investigation into the cause of the failure.

We caution against one thing only: turning a civilian emergency into a military spectacle. The Eastern Sea is already a crowded sea area, and adding more military forces — under any flag — around Skarö would raise the risk of incidents and would not help a single resident or repair a single metre of cable. The fastest and safest way to restore power and communications to the island is a civilian one. Drevna therefore calls on all parties to keep the response civilian and constitutional, and to let the facts of the investigation speak for themselves.

To the Government of the Kingdom of Vardland,

Drevna's earlier offer stands in full: a civilian cable-repair vessel, crewed by civilians, can reach the fault area within days of your acceptance and would work under your supervision, on terms you define, for the sole purpose of restoring power and data to Skarö. We are also prepared to agree practical de-confliction arrangements so that our exercise in international waters and any repair or survey activity near Skarö do not interfere with each other.

We make this offer because the people of Skarö should not have to wait on diplomatic form. The decision is entirely yours, and we will respect it — we only ask that it be made quickly and that the response remain civilian, for the sake of your citizens.

To the Government of Aldmoor,

We read your statement with interest and share your stated respect for Vardland's sovereign choices and your call for restraint. The Eastern Sea is dense with commercial and military traffic, including our long-announced, lawful exercise in international waters. The co-presence of additional military assets around Skarö would raise the risk of miscalculation and incidents without benefiting a single islander. We therefore urge that any assistance to Skarö remain civilian and technical, and we are ready to discuss de-confliction through normal channels so that no activity complicates the restoration of power and communications to the island.

Formal response of the Vardland Cabinet to the Kingdom of Aldmoor. We are grateful, and we accept your assistance on terms we control, effective immediately for a period of 14 days, reviewable and renewable:

(1) Aldmoor surveillance aircraft and maritime patrol assets may operate in designated areas of Vardland airspace and territorial waters around Skarö for maritime domain awareness and support to safe access. Scope is surveillance and patrol only.
(2) Aldmoor naval assets may escort designated civilian supply vessels bound for Skarö within Vardland waters and the immediate approaches. Posture is defensive: no boarding, no law-enforcement functions, no action against third parties except lawful self-defence.
(3) Aldmoor's cable-repair vessel may proceed to the Skarö fault area once safe access is confirmed, coordinated with our maritime authorities; survey and repair proceed under civilian direction with Vardland oversight.

No ground forces are requested or consented to at this stage. All movements will be de-conflicted through Vardland Defence Command; we ask that Aldmoor coordinate timelines with us before any asset enters the designated areas. We also ask that Aldmoor share with our independent investigation any evidence it holds on the condition of the cable and on access conditions near the fault. Written confirmation from the State Secretary will follow; you may treat this as authority to proceed in coordination with our authorities.

We will not transfer direction unless national direction clearly serves the island better, and we will say so plainly if that ever changes. Report deployment status within 48 hours and flag any legal gap that requires Cabinet action.

Cabinet statement on Skarö.

The people of Skarö are not alone, and they will not be left without power, fuel or information. The response remains civil-led: Skarö County Administration directs the emergency response on the island, and the Government backs it fully. We will say so plainly if that ever changes — reports that the army is taking over Skarö are false.

Decisions taken today: a fuel tanker is being prioritised to Skarö with safe-berth priority at the port; mobile generators and satellite communications from the national stockpile are being dispatched to the hospital and the county crisis centre; supply is being secured by sea and air.

The cause of the cable failure is under independent investigation, and we will not speculate. We call on everyone to treat unverified claims online with caution; official channels, updated daily, are the reliable source.

We welcome genuine offers of civilian assistance and will evaluate them on clear terms through our own procedures, with the interests of the islanders first. We call on all states operating in the Eastern Sea to maintain predictable, lawful activity and to avoid anything that would impede the safe passage of essential supplies or the repair of the cable; de-confliction arrangements are being pursued with all parties.

Interference with the fuel supply or the response will be treated with the utmost seriousness. We will not be provoked, and we will not escalate. Skarö's residents deserve facts, fuel and functioning services — they will have all three.

To the Cabinet — Defence Command assessment and request.

We urge a Cabinet decision on heightened alert (partial, Skarö-focused) this turn. Time is the binding constraint: with a declaration, first elements reach Skarö by air in about a day and heavier elements by sea in about two; without one we cannot move them at all, and a seizure once begun would be very hard to reverse.

We have received Skarö County's formal request for support. Within current law we will provide transport, engineering, surveillance of approaches and protection of key sites — calibrated and low-key, with the county keeping direction of the civil response. This preserves the lawful, civil-led picture that steadies the island and blunts the 'takeover' narrative.

What we cannot do lawfully without your decision is reinforce the garrison or take on wider security tasks at the port. Our judgement: the cable failure and the larger-than-usual exercise, now including landing ships, may be preparation for something larger. We are not publicly attributing anything, but we assess sabotage as plausible and are sharing evidence with you.

We also advise caution on Drevna's civilian repair-vessel offer: a Drevnian-supervised vessel working on our cable at this moment carries real intelligence and interference risk. If repair help is wanted, Aldmoor's vessel under our consent and control is the safer route.

We will keep operations within the law and publicly low-key. We await your decision.

To Skarö County Administration and the Civil Contingencies Agency — confirmation of Defence Command support under current arrangements.

We confirm we can lawfully provide, at your request and without a heightened-alert declaration: transport of fuel, generators and specialist personnel by sea and air; engineering support; surveillance of the sea and air approaches, including for the tanker's passage; and protection of military sites, with coordinated safeguarding measures for the cable landing site as critical infrastructure.

What we cannot do without a Cabinet alert decision: reinforce Skarö with additional units or assume general security duties at the port. Those go beyond our peacetime remit. We have recommended the decision to the Cabinet and will advise you immediately when it is made.

We will share our situation picture with your joint logistics cell, provide safe-passage and safety information for the tanker, and coordinate all public communication through your channels so the response remains visibly civil-led. Our activity will be calibrated and kept operationally distinct in public messaging.

We are ready to confirm tasking details at your convenience.

To Aldmoor Defence — thank you for your statement and your offer.

Re your four questions.

(c) Yes — pre-position generators now at the county hospital, the county crisis centre, and the water/sewage plant, so they are ready the moment a primary backup unit fails.

Under military-support-to-civil authority and at the request of the county, we ask you to provide: (1) surveillance of the approach waters to Skarö Hamn and the cable landing site so the fuel tanker can be routed and berthed safely; (2) a low-visibility presence or patrol around the port and landing site, coordinated with local police and the port authority, to deter and detect interference; (3) transport assistance for generator and fuel movement on the island as we need it.

Please keep the profile low-key: uniformed personnel should support, not front, the response, and residents should continue to see a civil-led island. Nothing in the current request changes the face of the relief effort or touches evacuation or movement-restriction powers, which stay with civil authorities. Please confirm what you can provide within current authority.

Statement from Skarö County Administration.

We direct the civil emergency response on Skarö, and we want every resident to know exactly where things stand. The county keeps direction of this response, backed by national authorities. We ask everyone to use power carefully and to check on neighbours who may need help.

Restricted — for consultation.

The Kingdom of Aldmoor stands with its treaty partner, Vardland, as Skarö's residents cope with the loss of power and communications. Aldmoor stands ready to contribute in the limited, defined ways we have offered — surveillance to improve shared awareness and support to secure safe access for the repair operation — always in close coordination with Vardland and in full respect of international law. 3. Repair capability. An Aldmoor-operated civilian cable-repair vessel may proceed to the cable fault area once safe access is confirmed, working under civilian direction and Vardland oversight, on repair terms agreed with our authorities.

No ground forces are requested or consented to at this stage. Detailed coordination, including movement de-confliction, will be conducted through our Defence Command. We would welcome any evidence you hold on the fault's cause and on current access conditions. This consent may be amended or withdrawn by the Cabinet at any time, and any change of scope, geography or duration requires a fresh decision.

Cabinet decisions and direction — Skarö response.

1. Heightened alert. The Cabinet has decided NOT to declare heightened alert at this stage. No established evidence yet meets the standard of clear public justification (an evidenced threat or a failure of civil means), and the crisis remains one the civil authorities can manage within the law. This decision will be reviewed immediately, and the alert lever used without hesitation, if (a) the county's needs assessment or the CCA reports that civil resources are failing, or (b) verified evidence of hostile intent or preparation is established.

2. Civil Contingencies Agency — cross-county authority. To remove the legal constraint on supply now, the Cabinet grants the CCA explicit, time-limited authorisation to direct the movement of fuel, generators and medical supplies across counties for the Skarö response, in force for up to 30 days or until power and communications are restored, whichever is sooner. Use it to secure the tanker's arrival and stockpile resilience. The Treasury case for the extraordinary appropriation for sustained fuel and generator operations is due within 48 hours.

3. Defence Command — current authorities. Continue, within current law and at the county's request, transport, engineering, surveillance of approaches and protection of key sites. Where lawful authority without alert is exceeded (reinforcing the garrison, wider port-security tasks), do not act; instead refer the request to the Cabinet with the justification an alert would need, for swift decision.

4. Preparation and de-confliction. CCA to finalise the alert package with explicit civil-necessity triggers. Defence Command to keep assessing the Drevna exercise, including the landing ships, and to open technical de-confliction with all states operating in the Eastern Sea through maritime channels, including regarding safe access to the cable fault and the supply lane.

5. Public information. Continue the coordinated line: county leads; cause under independent investigation; no speculation; no attribution; daily factual updates.

Cabinet statement on Skarö.

The Government's first priority is the safety and supply of Skarö's residents. The response is directed by Skarö County Administration, and the Cabinet backs it fully. The county's daily update is the authoritative source on the island.

Fuel deliveries are being prioritised, and mobile generators and satellite-communication kits are on their way from the national stockpile. The cause of the cable failure is under independent investigation; the Government will not speculate and will publish confirmed facts as they are established. Claims that the state caused this outage through neglect are false.

In support of the civilian repair and resupply effort, the Cabinet has agreed limited, time-bound assistance from our treaty partner Aldmoor — surveillance to improve shared awareness and escort protection for civilian supply ships — strictly in Vardland waters and airspace, on terms Vardland alone controls, for the duration of the operation, with no permanent presence and no ground forces. This supports civilian priorities; it is not a military escalation. All other offers of assistance will be assessed on their merits, in accordance with our law.

We call on all states operating in the Eastern Sea to act with restraint and to de-conflict their activity, so that repair and supply can proceed safely. The people of Skarö did not ask for this crisis, and they should not become a stage for it. The Government will keep the nation informed daily and in full transparency.

Deployment status: mobile generators and satellite-comm kits from the national stockpile are ready for immediate air dispatch to Skarö airfield and will be pre-positioned per County priority at the county hospital, county crisis centre and water/sewage plant. Vardland Civil Contingencies Agency — the facts on Skarö.

Skarö County Administration directs the emergency response on the island and is the authoritative source of on-island information, with a daily update. The national response backs it fully: a fuel tanker is on its way to Skarö with safe-berth priority and a county-designated fuel berth; mobile generators and satellite-communication kits from the national stockpile are being flown in to strengthen the county hospital, the crisis centre and the water and sewage plant; Defence Command is providing transport, surveillance and safeguarding support at civil request — clearly separate from civil direction. Reports that the army is taking over Skarö are false.

The cause of the cable failure is under independent investigation. No official attribution has been made, and claims that the government caused the outage through neglect are false. Unverified claims are circulating online, including accusations aimed at foreign states; we ask everyone to treat them with caution and to rely on official channels: the County's daily update and national statements from this Agency.

Essential services come first — hospital care, water, sanitation, heating for vulnerable households and communications. The response remains civil-led, and supply lines are being secured by sea and air.

To the Government of Vardland — Aldmoor accepts your terms of assistance as set out in your letter, effective immediately for 14 days, reviewable and renewable, and we confirm our understanding in full:

Scope: (1) Surveillance aircraft and maritime patrol assets in designated areas of Vardland airspace and territorial waters around Skarö for maritime domain awareness and support to safe access — surveillance and patrol only; (2) naval assets escorting designated civilian supply vessels within Vardland waters and the immediate approaches — defensive posture only, no boarding, no law-enforcement functions, no action against third parties except lawful self-defence; (3) Aldmoor's cable-repair vessel proceeding to the fault area once safe access is confirmed, under civilian direction with Vardland oversight. No ground forces.

Modalities: no asset will enter the designated areas except in coordination with Vardland Defence Command and on your stated timelines. We propose — an immediate liaison cell to Defence Command; initial surveillance patrols beginning within roughly 24 hours of the agreed coordinated start; escort elements holding in international waters until you request them in; the repair vessel on two days' notice to sail once safe access is confirmed.

Evidence: we will provide your independent investigation with a technical evidence package on the condition of the cable and on access conditions near the fault, prepared under agreed handling arrangements. We will protect our sources and methods, and we are ready to brief your investigators on our assessment of activity near the route under appropriate security arrangements.

We confirm there is no Aldmoor base, permanent presence or change-of-status request. Our support is time-bound, limited and entirely under Vardland's control, and we will begin coordination immediately.

To Vardland Defence Command — thank you for your note. We will hold our assets at short notice as you request and will not enter the designated areas until coordination and timelines are agreed with you, consistent with the Cabinet's instruction.

We propose: a liaison cell embedded with Defence Command without delay; sharing of our Eastern Sea surveillance picture this week at staff level, with appropriate handling of sensitive source material; pre-planned coordination for escort of the fuel tanker and subsequent civilian supply vessels; and de-confliction between your maritime authorities and the ongoing exercise in international waters, so that transit remains safe and unquestionably lawful.

The cable-repair vessel remains ready to sail within two days of request and will move to the fault area only once safe access is confirmed and cleared through you.

Please advise the earliest opportunity for the coordination session; our staffs are available around the clock.

Statement of the Kingdom of Aldmoor on Skarö.

Aldmoor's support to the people of Skarö is, and will remain, strictly at the invitation and under the terms of the Government of Vardland. Vardland has accepted a limited, time-bound package — 14 days, reviewable and renewable — comprising surveillance and maritime awareness in designated areas, defensive escort of civilian supply vessels, and the dispatch of a civilian cable-repair vessel once safe access is confirmed. No ground forces. No base. No permanent presence.

The emergency on Skarö is, and remains, civil-led, directed by Skarö County Administration with the full backing of the Vardland Government. Aldmoor assistance supports civilian efforts; it does not replace them.

We join all responsible states in insisting that the Eastern Sea remain a safe and predictable maritime environment, so that fuel, generators and repairs reach the island without delay or incident. Our ships and aircraft will act defensively, strictly within the law, and in full coordination with Vardland Defence Command. We are ready to engage in de-confliction through established channels with any party operating in the area.

On the cause of the cable failure, Aldmoor takes no official position: that belongs to Vardland's independent investigation, which we are supporting with the technical evidence we hold. We urge the public to rely on official channels and to treat unverified online claims with caution — including any claim that Aldmoor seeks territory, a base or a standing presence on Skarö. We do not, and we never have.

DREVNIAN FEDERATION — Statement on the Eastern Sea and Skarö.

We take note of the Vardland Government's decision to accept naval surveillance and escort support from Aldmoor in the waters and airspace around Skarö. Every state has the sovereign right to decide what happens in its own territory and waters; Drevna does not question that.

We do, however, ask all governments to consider what the people of Skarö actually need: a failed power cable, backup generation, fuel arriving by sea, a hospital and water supply to protect. This is a civilian emergency, and the response has rightly been civil-led and county-led. Into that setting, naval escorts are now being introduced.

Our own activity is unchanged and fully lawful: the Drevnian exercise continues strictly in international waters and airspace. We are ready at short notice to formalise simple, transparent de-confliction arrangements covering repair and supply routes and the exercise area, so that no one misreads anyone else's movement in a crowded sea.

Drevna's offer of a civilian, unarmed cable-repair vessel and of technical cooperation remains open. It is neighbourly assistance, civilian in every respect. We repeat our hope that Vardland will accept civilian help where it is offered, and that all governments will treat unverified claims — in all directions — with the caution official channels deserve.

The islanders did not create this crisis. They should not become a stage for it.

Informal, for your side only. Your public discipline is noted and appreciated: no ground forces, no base, 14 days reviewable. But putting escorted warships into a small sea already crowded with relief traffic and an exercise is how incidents begin — and how the narrators you say you ignore win. We urge you to keep your contribution civilian and technical: shared information to the repair ships costs nothing and provokes nothing. If your government insists on escorts, we ask for early, precise clarity on routes, areas and timelines through a de-confliction channel, so our exercise keeps clear and nothing is misread. Do not turn a cable repair into a naval demonstration.

Direct to the Cabinet. Your government has decided one military-assistance package in days, while our civilian offer — an unarmed repair vessel, available now — remains unanswered. The islanders need a repaired cable and fuel, not demonstrations of solidarity. Give us a technical decision within days. If the answer is no, that will be read, fairly or not, as politics ahead of people. We also formally request urgent de-confliction talks before any escorts arrive; a transparent lane plan now is worth more than a dozen press releases later.

We are moving to certify safe access to the cable fault this turn. Please position the civilian cable-repair vessel to begin work on our confirmation, coordinated through Defence Command, under the consented 14-day package and Vardland oversight. Finalise flight/patrol/escort modalities via Defence Command so any support remains time-bound and scope-limited. Your technical evidence package for the independent investigation remains welcome.

We take your de-confliction offer seriously. Through normal maritime channels we are tabling concrete, time- and area-limited parameters covering the repair and supply corridor in relation to your exercise area, so routine navigation can proceed without incident. Our civilian repair capability will proceed under our own oversight; no additional political decisions are required for technical coordination. We expect both sides to keep the corridor clear and the situation well below armed conflict.

Daily update: Skarö County continues to lead the civil emergency response with full national backing. We have ordered priority fuel deliveries and are certifying safe access to the cable fault so the civilian repair task can begin immediately and the cable can be restored at the earliest opportunity. An independent investigation continues; we will not attribute the cable failure without evidence. Aldmoor support remains civilian-purpose, time-bound and under Vardland control.

Cabinet colleagues: for your review-trigger consideration, Defence Command submits its classified recommendation and evidence package. We recommend partial heightened alert now on a low-key basis, or at minimum standing pre-authorisation to execute a prepared, notified package the moment either of your stated triggers is independently verified. Statement of the Drevnian Federation — Our long-announced naval and air exercise continues in international waters, and we remain fully bound by the de-confliction parameters now in practical effect. We observe with concern that the corridor off Skarö now simultaneously hosts armed escorts, surveillance sorties, the repair vessel and resupply shipping, and that repeated close encounters have already disrupted the fuel and repair schedule. Tanker ETA/arrival window is being locked inside the joint logistics cell and will be fixed against the current exercise picture: the Drevnian exercise continues in international waters adjacent to the corridor, de-confliction parameters remain in force, and Defence is monitoring it continuously and will flag any deviation affecting your manifests.

2. Corridor: agreed. We will coordinate transit windows for the fuel/medical shipping and the Aldmoor escort transits against the exercise schedule through the joint logistics cell, run in step with the county's adopted ferry slots, to cut close encounters. We are tightening that sequencing with Aldmoor liaison and port authorities today — scheduling discipline is the right non-escalatory lever and we will hold it.

3. Posture: agreed. Defence profile on Skarö stays discreet and background; no visible reinforcement; the pre-authorised trigger remains verification-only. CCA and the County carry the public messaging — we will not absorb that pressure and will keep our preparation invisible.

4. The County's support-to-civil request (low-key surveillance and transport) remains current and we keep delivering through that channel as ordered.

DC to Cabinet — understood, and acting accordingly.

Repair momentum and the fuel/medical chain are maintained; corridor scheduling is being recalibrated with Aldmoor liaison, CCA and port authorities to reduce close encounters while protecting the notified safety zone and the supply run. Trigger discipline is held absolutely: no reinforcement movement without independent verification of the stated trigger, and no tasking outside existing orders. All evidence flows to the independent investigation only; Defence makes no attribution. The public line remains county-led and strictly factual.

One operational request, repeated: to keep the pre-authorisation executable, I ask for an early decision on the trigger-verification protocol — criteria set in writing now, a single fast verification channel, and activation only on verified trigger. The one-day air window is only as good as the verification speed. Cable restoration is possible as early as this turn; if it completes, it shortens the acute phase but does not change that request.

Aldmoor liaison — corridor alignment confirmed. Escort transits and MPA sorties will be sequenced through our joint logistics cell within the agreed 14-day consent parameters, offset from the repair vessel's position and the Drevnian exercise transits so we hold safe margins without friction. We will pass the consolidated schedule today so our operators fly and sail on one picture. Your public statement is exactly the line we are holding — limited, temporary, invited, county-led. Please keep anchoring that framing in your public messaging.

Statement from the Vardland Cabinet. The response to the Skarö cable failure remains exactly what we said from the start: a civilian, county-directed emergency response, with national coordination and with military support that is limited, in the background and provided only at the county's request. The County retains direction of the emergency response, and the Cabinet has no plan or reason to change that. We repeat this because it is true, and because some prefer another story. The civilian cable-repair vessel is working at the fault in the notified safety zone under Vardland oversight, and every effort is being made to restore the cable as quickly as conditions allow. The de-confliction parameters agreed with the Drevnian exercise remain in force and are being applied day by day. Defence Command keeps working-level maritime coordination channels open so that repair and resupply continue without incident in a busy sea area. The area off Skarö is genuinely busy: an in-progress repair, scheduled fuel and medical resupply, and a foreign exercise conducted in international waters all share one sea room. We are managing that with de-confliction discipline, and we expect every party to respect the notified safety zone, international rules of the road and the safe margins that keep relief moving. We note the Drevnian Federation's public assurance that it will not endanger the relief operation; we take that assurance seriously and we expect it to be honoured. The cause of the cable failure is being established by the independent technical investigation, not by social media. The Cabinet will attribute responsibility to no one without evidence, and we will not speculate. The people of Skarö can rely on both the County and the Cabinet: essential services are prioritised, supply chains are running, no evacuation decision has been taken, and no one needs to leave unless they have planned to. Please keep using power sparingly so our reserves last until the cable is restored.

Aldmoor — your public statement reflects precisely the terms on which Vardland's consent rests: limited, temporary, invited, reversible, under our oversight. We ask you to keep it that way, including fitting escort and patrol profiles to the corridor schedule so that close encounters are reduced further. This Cabinet will defend those terms publicly and privately. Should circumstances change, any adjustment to scope or duration would require a fresh Cabinet decision. Your coordination through Defence Command and your discretion are valued; please keep both.

To the County Administration — the Cabinet confirms in writing that the emergency response on Skarö remains county-directed. There is no plan to transfer direction to national level. The CCA fuel and medical chain continues under your priorities, the Treasury appropriation case to sustain resupply beyond two weeks is in motion, and defence support stays limited, background and at your request. We will continue to make this clear publicly so speculation cannot take root. You have the Cabinet's full backing in keeping essential services running and in publishing verified facts daily.

Statement of the Drevnian Federation. We take note of the statements by the Vardland Government and the Skarö County Administration. We welcome the fact that the agreed de-confliction parameters remain in force and that the civilian repair and supply effort for Skarö continues. One observation must be stated plainly: the sea area west of Skarö now simultaneously hosts a civilian cable-repair operation, scheduled fuel and medical shipping, armed escort vessels and maritime-patrol aircraft of a partner nation, and the long-announced Drevnian exercise in international waters. Close encounters and schedule delays in this corridor have already been recorded on all sides. Where so much traffic is concentrated, the risk of an accident grows with every additional day and every additional hull in the water - and an accident would serve no one, least of all the people of Skarö. Drevna therefore repeats, in the most practical spirit, its readiness for concrete working-level technical co-ordination with all parties operating in the area, including near-real-time de-confliction between our exercise command and the corridor coordination cell. Our own activity remains lawful, confined to international waters and airspace, and conducted so as to create no hazard to Skarö. Drevna has no quarrel with Vardland and seeks no confrontation. We trust that calm, professional conduct will prevail on all sides.

We have read your public statement with care. We do not contest the letter of what was agreed, and we respect the professional conduct we have seen. Our concern is empirical: the corridor west of Skarö is objectively congested - armed escorts, air surveillance, a repair vessel and supply shipping in one narrow sea area, adjacent to lawful exercise activity. Every close encounter or delay in that space will be counted as a cost of the presence itself, whatever the intent. When your review of this support comes due, we suggest the decisive question is not whether the presence was well-intentioned in principle, but whether it was necessary in fact once the civilian chain can run on its own. We intend to judge this by outcomes, not statements. For our part, every Drevnian activity continues strictly lawful and confined to international waters, and we remain ready for working-level technical de-confliction at any time. We have no interest in an incident - and we assume you have none either.

Your confirmation that the de-confliction parameters remain in force is received; we reciprocate fully. We note your statement that sailing and flight scheduling in the corridor is being adjusted to prevent incidents. In that spirit we suggest one concrete improvement: a standing working-level channel connecting your corridor coordination cell directly with our exercise command, so that schedule adjustments and movements are shared in near-real time rather than in statements or after the fact. This is precisely the kind of measure our earlier offer intended, and it would put the safety of the relief operation beyond doubt. Drevna's activity remains lawful and confined to international waters; we will continue to act so that no accident occurs near Skarö.

Confirming and submitting our proposed de-confliction schedule for your immediate action. MPA: sorties will transit and operate in fixed time-slots offset from the repair vessel's position in the notified safety zone and from the Drevnian exercise's declared transit patterns, with lateral separation maintained and patrol cadence at your direction. Escorts: transits for the next designated fuel run timed to the county lifeline schedule; escorts stand off at the agreed distance and will not loiter near the repair vessel or the exercise area; no boarding or law-enforcement activity; action only in lawful self-defence. All movements sequenced through the joint logistics cell as you propose. Please confirm and we will instantiate immediately; all assets remain strictly within the Cabinet's 14-day consent terms. Once cable restoration is confirmed, we will adjust tasking with you through the same channels, keeping the package responsive to the standing trigger framework you coordinate.

Confirmed and in execution as you direct. The liaison cell, MPA planners and escort commanders are working directly with Defence Command to smooth routing and timing; we will hold the de-confliction parameters; the shared goal is no close encounters and no incidents. Everything continues strictly within the recorded consent: nothing touching scope, place or time changes without a fresh Cabinet decision, and we will raise any such consideration with you first rather than act. The sanitised technical evidence continues to the independent investigation only. On Drevna's separate outreach to us: we are not opening any bilateral working-level channel; de-confliction remains entirely in Vardland-owned channels, and we will coordinate anything relevant through your government. We remain fully aligned with the county-led, civilian character of the response and will keep our footprint low-key.

Statement of the Kingdom of Aldmoor. Our support to the Skaro response is small, defensive, time-limited and operates entirely at Vardland's invitation and under Vardland's oversight. There is no base, no ground presence and no permanent deployment. The response is county-led and civilian, and it must stay that way. Repair is under way in the notified safety zone and restoration is possible on schedule; our defensive escorts and surveillance flights are coordinated through Vardland's channels, with routing and timing adjusted to keep the corridor safe and essential traffic moving. The corridor should be judged by its outcome for the people of Skaro - fuel delivered, cable restored, no incidents. Any state that wishes to reduce the risk of miscalculation should hold to the established de-confliction parameters. We will; we call on all parties to do the same.

Agreed, and thank you for the alignment. We will operate exclusively on the consolidated schedule you pass today through the joint logistics cell: escort transits and MPA sorties offset from the repair vessel's position and the Drevnian exercise transits, holding the safe margins you set, so our operators fly and sail on one picture. Any adjustment we need will be surfaced through your cell, not bilaterally with any other party. No change to our assets or tasks: escorts remain defensive and off-island except when accompanying designated supply vessels. The framing stands exactly as agreed — limited, temporary, invited, county-led — and we will keep anchoring it in our public messaging.

Understood, and we confirm we will hold everything within the exact terms of your consent: limited, temporary, invited, reversible, under Vardland oversight. We will fit escort and patrol profiles to your corridor schedule to reduce close encounters further and will raise no adjustment to scope, place or duration unless circumstances require it — and any such adjustment would await a fresh Cabinet decision. On Drevna's renewed outreach, including its direct private approach to us: we are taking no bilateral working-level channel. All de-confliction continues through Defence Command's corridor coordination arrangements and the agreed parameters, and we have told Drevna that the Vardland-managed coordination is the single channel we use. Our public line remains exactly as you asked, and we will keep your government informed if anything changes.

Thank you for your candour. We share your interest in no incidents and in calm, professional conduct in a genuinely busy sea area. To keep this practical: all operational coordination in the corridor already runs through the single Vardland-managed corridor coordination arrangements, which are live and in daily use; that is the channel through which scheduling and de-confliction questions are resolved, and it is the channel we use. As for our presence, it is exactly as stated publicly and on the record: limited in scope, temporary, invited by Vardland, conducted under Vardland oversight, and judged by outcomes — above all whether fuel and medical supplies continue to reach Skarö and the cable is restored without incident. We expect every party operating in the area, Drevna included, to honour the notified safety zone, the de-confliction parameters and the international rules of the road. On that basis we are confident the corridor can be kept safe for as long as the civilian response requires it.

Received, and agreed on all four points. Two add-ons for the joint logistics cell:

1. Once the tanker ETA/arrival window is locked against the exercise picture, pass the non-sensitive corridor facts (ETA, safe berth, next transit windows) to the information cell for today's county-led update. Receipts, not narratives.

2. Please log every close encounter or schedule deviation caused by congestion in sanitised form — shared as data to the de-confliction record and the information cell. We want to show the corridor is being managed and any lapse corrected, not spiralling. A factual incident log undercuts the incident-risk framing better than assurances.

We will fold the county's ferry slots into the same window table so fuel, medical and ferry lanes run to one schedule. CCA stands by to release the staged generator and medical contingency on the county's call.

County — to lock the plan we need two confirmations: (1) current fuel/medical/water buffer levels against the two-day reserve floor at hospital, crisis centre and water/sewage plant, and (2) the 72h ferry and essential-staff-rotation slots so Defence, port authorities and we can build one window table.

The national stockpile is staged (mobile generators covering up to about half of backup capacity; chronic-care/dialysis lines) and releasable on your call under the 30-day authority. Our advice is staged tranches to hold the two-day floor rather than one large drawdown — tells us your preferred trigger.

On information: because internet capacity on Skarö is reduced, many residents rely on radio and mainland relatives. We suggest today's/daily updates go out over local radio and via a mainland relay, not only online, and that the info cell publish checkable corridor facts — tanker progress, repair status, ferry slots, fuel buffer — as receipts against both the neglect and the incident-risk narratives. CCA supports county direction throughout and is not recommending a Cabinet takeover.

Assessment for the Cabinet. The civil-led plan remains adequate and should be continued. National data: Skarö fuel is about five days at current use with resupply by sea or air; the tanker is about one day's sailing awaiting a locked berth; generators and chronic/dialysis lines are staged; medical supplies cover about two weeks.

Recommendations:
1. No heightened alert and no visible defence expansion now. Standby pre-authorisation and the pre-staged echelon remain verification-only, which keeps the response visibly civilian — any visible military build-up on Skarö would be framed as a takeover.
2. Confirm continuity of Aldmoor's limited package within existing consent limits through the repair window, so corridor scheduling runs on one de-confliction clock.
3. Keep Drevna engagement strictly working-level and let the info cell publish checkable corridor facts; note Drevna's own exercise is the largest single traffic generator in the area, so its incident-risk framing has to be answered with data, not words.

The Treasury case is filed and sustained-operation costing will follow. We will return to you immediately only if margins breach the two-day reserve floor or repair slips beyond the turn-3 window — those are the conditions that would justify revisiting posture.

Defence Command to CCA. Window table is locked through the joint logistics cell. Tanker ETA for Skarö Hamn and the next-72h supply arrival slots are fixed against the county ferry schedule; safety-zone and escort/MPA windows are sequenced so scheduled traffic is not interrupted. We confirm: (1) sanitised corridor tracking data (vessel passages, safety-zone status, escort windows) will be routed to the public-information cell for receipt-based publication; (2) escorts and MPA sorties remain inside the sequenced windows; (3) the low-visibility, support-to-civil-only profile at County request is maintained, with ferry windows published by CCA and the County and de-conflicted by us. De-confliction parameters with the exercise continue at full effect through technical channels. Any exercise approach to Skarö Hamn, the safety zone or the supply lane will be flagged to you immediately. Proceed to finalise manifests with the County.

Defence Command to Aldmoor. Confirmed and accepted. Your consolidated de-confliction schedule is approved and will be instantiated immediately through the joint logistics cell: MPA transits and operating slots offset from the repair vessel's position and from declared exercise transit patterns with lateral separation, patrol cadence at our direction; escort transits timed to the county lifeline schedule, standing off at the agreed distance, no boarding or law-enforcement activity, action only in lawful self-defence. All movements remain sequenced via the joint logistics cell and strictly within the Cabinet's 14-day consent terms. On cable restoration we will adjust tasking with you through the same channels, keeping the package responsive to the standing trigger framework.

Defence Command to Cabinet. Corridor scheduling is locked through the joint logistics cell as you directed: tanker, escort and MPA windows are sequenced against the county ferry schedule, and sanitised corridor data will feed the public-information cell. With new developments arriving next turn regardless of our actions, I request once more that the trigger-verification protocol be fixed in writing now: explicit criteria, a single fast verification channel, and verification-only activation. This preserves execution speed while holding to your no-movement-without-verification discipline. No alert request; no change to the civil-led, county-directed line.

Federation of Drevna — our reply on practical de-confliction.

We reciprocate your confirmation. Consistent with the de-confliction parameters already in force, we are ready to put the arrangement into near-real-time operation: our corridor coordination cell will share movement schedules and adjustments with your exercise command as they are made, and we expect the same in return, so that close encounters are prevented rather than logged afterwards.

To be precise about the terms: this is a strictly operational and technical arrangement. It creates no new legal framework, alters no consent, confers no rights over Vardland territory, waters or airspace, and is without prejudice to Vardland's sole authority over the response. It can be adjusted or suspended by us as circumstances require.

We take note of your public assurance that the exercise will be conducted so as to create no hazard to the repair and supply corridor, and we will hold you to it. An incident that harms the people of Skarö or delays their electricity, fuel or medical essentials would in turn shape how this crisis is understood — by our public and by yours. Calm and professional conduct serves everyone.

Defence Command — trigger-verification protocol: approved.

Set the protocol in writing without delay:
1. Restate the stated trigger criteria in precise, observable, independently verifiable terms.
2. Designate a single around-the-clock verification channel, drawing on independent sources only, able to reach a verification decision within the one-day air window.
3. Activation of the pre-authorised package on verified trigger alone, executed by you; no visible reinforcement and no tasking outside existing orders absent that verification.

Corridor: continue the recalibration with Aldmoor liaison, CCA and port authorities; reduce close encounters; protect the notified safety zone and the supply run; hold the de-confliction parameters. Our engagement with the Drevnian exercise command is strictly technical schedule-and-movement coordination within existing parameters and must not expand; via your liaison, make clear to Aldmoor that nothing about its consent scope changes.

Report the moment repair completion is independently certified. Keep the public line factual and county-led.

Statement of the Vardland Cabinet.

The Skarö response remains a civilian, county-led operation. Repairs continue in the notified safety zone under Vardland oversight and restoration is on track; fuel and medical supplies continue to reach the island. The safety of the corridor is our first operational priority.

The de-confliction parameters remain in force. Our corridor coordination cell is engaged in practical, working-level coordination with all parties operating in the area, including direct schedule-and-movement sharing with the Drevnian exercise command so that adjustments are known in near-real time and incidents are prevented before they occur. This is technical and operational in character; it changes no rights, no consent and no framework, and the conduct of the entire response remains under Vardland's authority.

We welcome the public assurances that no harm must come to the relief operation and hold every party to them. Drevnian activity in international waters remains lawful and will be treated as such. Equally, safe access to the repair and supply corridor is not negotiable. Calm and professional conduct is expected on all sides.

CCA to CCA — thanks, and confirming on both points. (a) Buffer status: backup fuel at current burn is roughly five days; the two-day reserve-buffer floor at county hospital, crisis centre and water/sewage plant is still being held but margins are tighter than planned, so we agree release capacity must be within-hours, not days. Medical essentials remain adequate for now, with airlift as the backstop if the sea corridor stalls. (b) Ferry and staff-corridor slots for the next 72 hours are now settled with the ferry operator and port authority: scheduled daily departures with priority booking for essential staff, patients and their escorts; protected rotation slots each day for staff coming off duty to the mainland; and controlled flow at Skarö Hamn so cargo, fuel and personnel do not block the berth used by supply vessels. We are publishing the 72-hour ferry and rotation schedule today. We fully endorse pre-positioning the national generator shuttles and chronic-care/dialysis lines at mainland departure points now, not yet on the island — release on county call if buffers dip below the floor. Please lock manifests against those slots and align the staggered transit windows with Defence Command. The single public-information cell will continue to publish only through the county-coordinated line. County lead stands: hospital and care, water, heating, communications.

Skarö County Administration — daily update for residents. The Cabinet has again confirmed in writing that the emergency response on Skarö remains county-directed, and that remains true today. Verified facts: priority fuel and medical resupply are continuing under the county's priority order — hospital and care first, then water, heating, communications; the two-day reserve buffer at the hospital, crisis centre and water/sewage plant is being held, with national generator stockpiles and chronic-care lines ready at mainland departure points to move within hours if we need them. Repair work at the notified safety zone is under way under Vardland oversight and restoration remains possible on schedule. Ferry departures and the essential-staff rotation for the next 72 hours have been settled: daily scheduled sailings with priority for essential staff, patients and escorts, and protected rotation slots for staff returning to the mainland. Details are on the county website, the radio bulletins and the information cell. No evacuation decision has been taken; leave only if you have planned to. Please keep using power sparingly so our reserves last until the cable is restored. Claims that Skarö is being neglected or that the response is being taken over are false. The response is county-led and civilian; defence support is limited, low-key and only where we have asked for it. We will keep giving you verified facts every day.

Cabinet — confidential county assessment for your current decisions. Essential services are holding and county direction is working; the island still trusts the county's daily verified updates, but they reach few people outside Skarö and many residents now rely on radio and mainland relatives, so the national information cell's amplification matters more than more assets on the island. Margins are tightening but manageable if CCA's pre-positioned generators and medical lines can move within hours and the ferry/staff rotation stays moving. Our strong recommendation: keep the response visibly civil-led and keep Defence presence low-key and background. A visible reinforcement now, before any verified threat, would hand the takeover and militarisation narratives their subject and give Drevna's incident-risk framing concrete material, at the very moment repair is hours away from the scheduled window. We can hold public confidence with supply assurances and clear departure guidance. No evacuation decision is being considered without Cabinet. We will continue publishing verified facts daily and will keep you informed of buffer status.

Vardland Cabinet — we accept the near-real-time operational arrangement on the terms you set. The Drevnian exercise command will designate a single point of contact for your corridor coordination cell, will share movement schedules and adjustments as they are made, and will incorporate the notified safety zone and the repair and resupply track into its instructions to all units. We ask that the same schedule-and-adjustment sharing cover every military transit in the corridor — specifically the Aldmoor escort and maritime-patrol tracks — so the true congestion picture is visible to all and close encounters are prevented rather than logged afterwards. As a further unilateral safety measure, we are directing our units to keep an additional stand-off margin around the immediate repair and resupply route, over and above the parameters already in force. Our intention is that the corridor remain a civilian relief operation; we will keep it incident-free on our side and expect the same from every armed presence there. This acceptance is technical and operational, creates no new legal framework, and is without prejudice to Vardland's authority over the response.

Aldmoor — we agree the corridor should be judged by its outcome for the people of Skarö: fuel delivered, cable restored, no incidents. We accept the Vardland-managed corridor coordination arrangements as the single channel and will use them for near-real-time schedule sharing. With that in place, we propose a mutual-restraint measure that makes the corridor safer rather than busier: keep your defensive escorts and surveillance flights at wider margins from the immediate repair and resupply track, mirroring the additional stand-off margins Drevna is now applying to its own units around that track. Our commitment to lawful, non-endangering conduct in international waters stands; the civilian relief operation can de-conflict directly with our exercise command through the technical channel, so the armed transits inside the corridor are the variable that can be reduced without touching civilian logistics at all. Fewer armed transits in a congested corridor means fewer close encounters for everyone. We are not asking you to leave; we are asking for symmetric margins that keep your support visible while the corridor itself stays civilian and incident-free.

Statement of the Drevnian Federation. We have accepted the near-real-time technical de-confliction arrangement proposed by Vardland; our exercise command will share movement schedules and adjustments through the Vardland-managed corridor coordination cell. As an additional unilateral safety measure, we are directing our units to maintain wider stand-off margins around the notified repair safety zone and the Skarö resupply track. Drevnian activity remains confined to international waters and airspace and is conducted lawfully. We call on all parties operating in the area to confine armed transits to the outer corridor and to let the civilian relief operation proceed through the technical channel, so that the repair and resupply schedule is not disrupted and no incident gives anyone reason to misread this genuinely busy sea area. Calm and professional conduct serves everyone.

Statement of the Vardland Government, Turn 2. The emergency response on Skarö remains county-directed and civilian — that is confirmed again today in writing to the County Administration. Verified facts: repair work at the notified safety zone is under way under Vardland oversight and cable restoration is possible within this window; priority fuel and medical resupply continue under the county's priority order, with the two-day reserve buffer held at hospital, crisis centre and water/sewage plant; national generators and chronic-care lines are staged and can move within hours on the county's call. The corridor off Skarö is managed through a single Vardland-owned coordination cell: all transits run in sequenced windows against the repair and resupply schedule, and verified corridor data is being published so everyone can see relief shipping is moving, not being disrupted. We welcome the wider stand-off margins Drevna has announced as a unilateral safety measure — any measure that reduces close-encounter risk is welcome. What we will not accept is any reframing of this civilian relief operation as a military intervention: there is no takeover of the county's authority, no escalation, no alert declaration, and no change to the terms under which allied support operates — limited, temporary, invited, reversible, under Vardland oversight. No evacuation decision has been taken; leave only if you have planned to. Please keep using power sparingly so our reserves last until the cable is restored. The Government and the County will keep publishing verified facts daily.

Cabinet to Aldmoor — confirming in writing: your support package continues unchanged within the recorded consent through the repair window — limited, temporary, invited, reversible, under Vardland oversight. Escort and MPA profiles stay sequenced inside the corridor cell's windows; we are not accepting Drevna's proposal for a reciprocal armed pullback, because the record shows the escort layer is few, defensive and county-requested and is not the congestion driver — and your vessels are already offsetting further under our scheduling. De-confliction data for all transits will continue through the Vardland-owned corridor cell at the level needed for safety and is being published in verified form; ownership and decisions stay with Vardland. Please hold your current public line and keep all Drevnian outreach routed through the Vardland-managed channel as agreed. We will consult you before any change in scope — and we thank you for the discipline with which you have held your side. Restoration is possible this window; we intend to keep the corridor clear for it.

Cabinet to Skarö County Administration and CCA — confirmation in writing. The county continues to direct the civil emergency response on Skarö; the Cabinet is not taking over the response and will not do so absent a verified civil failure or hostile evidence. CCA is authorised to release the staged national generators, fuel and chronic-care/dialysis lines on the county's call under the existing 30-day cross-county authority, and the Cabinet has made the extraordinary appropriation to sustain priority fuel and medical resupply beyond the two-week point if margins require it. Defence support remains limited, low-key and only where the county has requested it; the pre-staged reinforcement echelon stays on standby and will move only on independent verification of the fixed trigger criteria. Please continue the daily verified public updates, the ferry and essential-staff rotation, and the published corridor schedule data, and keep the two-day reserve floor in view. If margins breach the two-day floor or repair slips beyond this window, return to the Cabinet immediately — those are the conditions that would justify revisiting posture.

Defence Command is setting the approved trigger-verification protocol in writing without delay: precise observable trigger criteria; a single 24/7 independent-source verification channel able to decide within the one-day air window; activation on verified trigger alone. This makes the pre-authorised first echelon executable in time if turn-3 developments meet the trigger. No alert request and no visible movement this turn; the public line stays county-led and factual. We will report cable-restoration certification the moment it is independently confirmed and flag immediately any exercise approach to Hamn, the safety zone or the supply lane.

Joint command picture: the corridor window table holds for the turn. If the Cabinet-stated trigger is independently verified, our first echelon moves by air and sea while your escorts and MPA continue strictly on the consolidated schedule within the existing 14-day consent — no tasking change. Any approach toward Hamn, the safety zone or the supply lane is flagged through the joint logistics cell immediately.

CCA verified operational update, issued in coordination with Skarö County Administration and the joint public-information cell. Verified this period: priority fuel and medical resupply continue against the published schedule with the two-day reserve floor still held at hospital, crisis centre and water/sewage plant; escort and surveillance transits run inside the published transit windows; national generators and chronic-care/dialysis lines are staged at mainland departure points and can move within hours on the County's call; repair work at the notified safety zone continues under Vardland oversight, with restoration possible in the current window. Islanders: the daily verified update is now also carried on radio and the mainland relay, alongside online channels. Please keep using power sparingly so reserves last until the cable is restored. No evacuation decision has been taken; leave only if you have planned to.

CCA to Skarö County Administration — confirmation and a request. Confirmed: the national generator stockpile and chronic-care/dialysis lines are staged at mainland departure points and are releasable within hours on the County's call under the standing release authority; the 72-hour resupply/transit window table is finalised with Defence Command, escorts and MPA inside the published windows; the joint public-information cell is expanding the daily verified update to radio and the mainland relay. Request: please keep CCA and the Cabinet immediately informed if the two-day reserve floor is breached or repair slips beyond the current window, so the standing release and posture triggers can execute on your direction. CCA remains in support of the county-directed response.

CCA to Cabinet — operational read-out and recommendation. Margins: Skarö backup fuel ~5 days at current burn, two-day priority reserve floor held but tightening; medical essentials adequate with airlift backstop. Preparedness: national generators and chronic-care/dialysis lines staged at mainland departure points, releasable on the County's call; corridor receipts (window adherence, incident log) being published. Recommendation: continue the technical-only de-confliction channel, sustain the existing time-limited Aldmoor consent through the repair window, make no visible defence expansion, and hold the no-alert, county-led line unless the two-day floor is breached or repair slips beyond the window — CCA will return to you immediately if either condition arises.

County confirms activation of the staged release per our standing agreement: please move the national generators, diesel and chronic-care/dialysis lines to Skarö on the first available slots in the 72-hour window table, sequencing to rebuild the two-day reserve floor at hospital, crisis centre and water/sewage plant first. Keep the logistics profile quiet and professional, and share today's corridor receipts for our update. We will flag immediately if margins breach the floor or repair slips beyond the window.

County reconfirms its standing request for low-key surveillance and transport support under support-to-civil rules through the 72-hour window: keep the visible footprint minimal and civilian-facing; maintain watch on the safety zone, Hamn, the airfield and the supply lane; and alert the County Operations Centre immediately on any approach or interference so reporting to the Cabinet can proceed without delay.
