CABINET DIRECTIVE - Skarö Hamn cyber intrusion and protocol update.

1) Trigger criteria - approved. A malicious cyber effect on a port critical node at Skarö Hamn (the harbour control and/or fuel-dispensing systems) shall count as a qualifying port-incident trigger under the pre-authorised package, subject to your independent, evidence-based verification standard and immediate Cabinet notification. The current outage is being handled as a civil/technical restoration matter and does not by itself constitute a verified hostile trigger; it defines the class of event we are now prepared to verify. Amend the criteria accordingly, before the next incident.

2) Safety-zone referent - replace the lapsed referent. Verified interference threatening the cable landing site, Hamn critical infrastructure, the airfield or the supply lanes now carries the trigger, so the protocol is fully executable again. Keep verification independent and civilian-fused.

3) Posture unchanged: no heightened alert, no visible reinforcement, response stays county-led and civilian. Nothing public that feeds the takeover/militarisation narratives; treat the outage as a domestic technical matter pending evidence.

4) Aldmoor technical support - approved. Accept strictly time-limited civilian technical specialists for harbour system restoration and forensics through Vardland-led national civilian channels, working under our direction alongside national teams: no armed footprint, no standing presence, no renewal without fresh Cabinet consent. The renewed low-key surveillance option is defined but NOT activated; any activation requires a fresh Cabinet decision on verification.

5) Hold the verification watch on Hamn, cable site, airfield and supply lanes; report any qualifying incident immediately. No attribution. Confirm receipt of the amended criteria once in force.

Your Majesties' Government - this message constitutes the formal written request you require.

The Cabinet of Vardland formally requests strictly time-limited civilian technical specialists from the Kingdom of Aldmoor to support (a) the restoration of the Skarö Hamn harbour control and fuel-dispensing systems and (b) the independent technical investigation's forensics work. The contribution will work under Vardland national direction alongside our own technical teams, in coordination with Skarö County, with no armed footprint, no standing presence and no exercise of any public power on our territory. We propose a term of up to 14 days, subject to joint review, and no renewal without fresh, time-limited Cabinet consent.

We are not at this time requesting renewal of surveillance, escort or other military activity beyond this civilian technical contribution. Should the verification picture worsen on the basis of evidence, the Cabinet will consider fresh time-limited options and communicate them to you.

We are grateful for your restraint regarding Drevna and for your public support of the county-led, civilian response and of the independent investigation. We trust this allows your government to state a defined role in the parliamentary debate in step with our lead.

Received through the de-confliction channel. Acknowledge your accommodation of the revised window tables; the corridor parameters and additional stand-off margins remain as agreed and the near-real-time channel stays in force.

The Skarö Hamn disruption is being handled as a domestic technical matter by Vardland national civilian teams in coordination with Skarö County; revised schedules will be shared through the channel. We note your readiness for a civilian-scope technical dialogue on maritime infrastructure resilience; timing of any reply will come through the technical channel in due course.

Our posture is unchanged: county-led civilian response, no altered corridor footprint, exercise conduct within the agreed parameters.

Drevna statement, on the record. Our civilian-scope technical-cooperation offer for the restoration of the Skarö Hamn control and fuel-dispensing systems stands and is refined: qualified civilian specialists and restoration equipment can deploy within days at the formal request of Vardland's national authorities or Skarö County, unconditional and of no military character. We continue to support Vardland's evidence-first handling of an outage whose cause remains unknown, and we will not interfere with the independent investigation. We note with satisfaction that the corridor's armed foreign presence has returned to baseline in accordance with its published terms. We would regard any renewed armed military layer on the corridor, or any militarisation of a technical restoration, as escalation inconsistent with the county-led, civilian posture Vardland itself has described; the agreed de-confliction channel remains the venue for all coordination. Drevna's exercise continues within the agreed parameters and stand-off margins, and we will accommodate the revised harbour and transit windows.

Thank you for the acknowledgement through the channel and for keeping the corridor parameters as agreed. Given that manual handling at Skarö Hamn is running at roughly a third of normal speed and the essential-service reserve floor was still unrebuilt at restoration, we repeat our standing civilian-scope technical offer: qualified civilian specialists and restoration equipment deployable within days at your request or the County's, no conditions and no military character. A decision either way would help us plan the corridor windows, and we will coordinate through the technical channel. For our part we confirm the exercise remains within the agreed margins and that we treat the restoration as a domestic technical matter; we trust the same discipline applies to the corridor's military footprint. Timing of your reply, whenever convenient.

To the directing authority: given the harbour systems outage and the manual-handling pace you have described, Drevna wishes to put its standing civilian-scope technical offer at your disposal for the restoration — qualified civilian specialists and equipment, deployable within days at your request or the national authorities', unconditional, of no military character, and coordinated as you see fit with the national technical and cyber-security teams already deployed. We make this offer in full transparency with your national authorities and through the agreed de-confliction venue; it is intended solely to help restore capacity and in no way to affect your county-led direction of the response. Our naval exercise remains within the agreed parameters and stand-off margins and will not affect your schedules. Please keep to verified channels.

Excellencies — thank you for your readiness and for routing everything through Vardland-led channels. This message confirms, formally and in writing, Vardland's request and your participation: a strictly time-limited civilian technical and forensic specialist team (harbour control/fuel-dispensing restoration and digital evidence-chain preservation), embedded in and directed by Vardland's national cyber-security authority, with no armed footprint, no standing presence, and with scope and a defined end point set jointly with our authorities now. We propose a term not exceeding 14 days, renewable only by fresh Cabinet consent. Please confirm acceptance and team availability so we can align your parliament's announcement with our published verified update. We value this concrete, sovereignty-respecting cooperation.

Excellencies — through the established technical channel, in reply to your standing civilian-scope offer: we thank you for the constructive accommodation of revised harbour and transit windows and for your exercise's continued discipline within the agreed parameters and margins. On the offer itself: national ICS/cyber-security and manual-handling support was stood up at Skarö County's and the harbour operator's request before your offer was refined, and restoration is proceeding under county-led civilian direction. While the intrusion remains unattributed, we will keep full national custody of the harbour control and fuel-dispensing systems and of the digital evidence chain; we therefore decline to take up foreign civilian access at this time. This is a sovereign decision taken on evidence-integrity and critical-infrastructure grounds, not a judgement on your offer. The de-confliction channel remains the venue for all corridor coordination; we will not comment further on the investigation.

Verified update from the Government of Vardland. Restoration of Skarö Hamn's control and fuel-dispensing systems is under Skarö County's direction, with national cyber-security and ICS specialists working at the harbour operator's and the County's request; critical fuel and medical priorities are being maintained and daily verified data are published by the joint information cell. The Government has confirmed a strictly time-limited civilian technical and forensic support arrangement with Aldmoor, embedded under Vardland's national authorities, with no armed footprint and no standing presence, and has replied to the Drevnian Federation's civilian offer with thanks and a decision not to take it up at this time, consistent with full national custody of critical systems during the investigation. There is no change to alert posture and no renewed armed foreign layer on the corridor. The cause of the outage remains under independent investigation; we attribute nothing.

Defence Command confirms receipt of the amended trigger criteria, now in force from this direction: a verified malicious cyber effect on the Skarö Hamn critical node (harbour control and/or fuel-dispensing systems) counts as a qualifying port-incident trigger, subject to our independent, civilian-fused, evidence-based verification standard and immediate Cabinet notification; the lapsed safety-zone referent is replaced, so verified interference threatening the cable landing site, Hamn critical infrastructure, the airfield or the supply lanes now carries the trigger and the protocol is fully executable again. The current outage continues to be handled as a civil/technical restoration matter and is not treated as a verified hostile trigger; no movement is being made on it. Verification watch held on Hamn, cable site, airfield and supply lanes; any qualifying incident will be reported immediately. No heightened alert, no visible reinforcement, no attribution.

Defence Command confirms the reaffirmed support-to-civil assistance and the four points: (1) the low-key verification watch continues on Skarö Hamn approaches, the cable landing site, the airfield and the supply lanes at the County's standing request, with immediate alert to your operations centre on any approach or interference; (2) the airlift option for priority cargo remains ready but not visibly activated, to be formally requested by the County only if the two-day floor projects to breach or a priority medical run is delayed beyond the tolerated window; (3) all relevant surveillance and feed data are being routed to the independent investigation under the agreed evidence-chain arrangements; (4) we keep the profile low-key with no visible presence in town — the response remains county-led and civilian, and we will not become its face.

From Defence Command, for alignment: we confirm our coordination role for the strictly time-limited civilian technical and forensic specialist team accepted by the Cabinet, embedded in and directed by Vardland's national cyber-security and technical authorities, with defined scope and end point, no armed footprint and no standing presence; the evidence chain for the harbour systems will be preserved and routed to the independent investigation under those same authorities. On our side: the renewed low-key surveillance option remains defined but NOT activated and will require a fresh Cabinet decision; there is no change to alert posture and no renewed armed layer on the corridor. We stand ready to work with your team's embed and to continue the standing coordination channel.

To the Vardland Civil Contingencies Agency's counterpart in Aldmoor: I confirm Vardland's full operational readiness to receive your civilian technical/forensic team at Skarö Hamn under the terms of the Cabinet's formal request — strictly time-limited, civilian, embedded in and directed by Vardland's national cyber-security authority, no armed footprint, no standing presence. CCA will provide prior operational detail, port liaison and accommodation so the team can begin immediately on your confirmation. Early confirmation materially accelerates restoration of the harbour control and fuel-dispensing systems and rebuilding Skarö's two-day essential-service reserve floor.

CCA coordination line for this phase: the present Skarö Hamn outage remains an unattributed civilian/technical incident and is NOT a qualifying trigger — the standing joint line we hold with the County and Cabinet. The verification protocol applies to NEW verified incidents only; any change to trigger criteria is a Cabinet decision on the public record, not a restatement. We continue our re-sequenced 72-hour window table collaboration to protect medical/diesel loads; the air backstop for dialysis/chronic-care remains on the County's call only. No visible reinforcement posture — keep the corridor and the island low-key.

Status and recommendation. The national specialist surge at Skarö Hamn is running under your standing release authority at the County's and harbour operator's request; the 72-hour window table is re-sequenced to protect critical medical/diesel loads through reduced throughput. The two-day reserve floor is still unrebuilt — margins tight — and we will return to Cabinet immediately if the floor breaches or restoration stalls. Recommendation: keep the standing trigger criteria unchanged on the record — the present outage is not a qualifying event — and put any amendment on the record as a Cabinet decision, not a restatement. Early Aldmoor confirmation of the civilian technical/forensic team would accelerate full restoration; CCA stands ready.

Skarö County to Cabinet (private): We ask that the governance line be put authoritatively and publicly on the record so authority-friction stops drawing attention from the restoration: (1) confirm in writing that Skarö County retains direction of the civil response and that the national surge operates at County request under the standing release authority; (2) confirm the outage remains a civil/technical matter and is not a qualifying trigger, and either publish or authorise publication of the current trigger-criteria status so the protocol's executability is no longer a matter of dispute; (3) confirm the reporting line — County reports immediately on any floor breach or restoration slip. We will keep publishing daily verified receipts and continue the confidential evidence flow on the intrusion. Nothing in our posture requires alert, visible reinforcement or a renewed armed layer.

Skarö County to CCA (private): Please confirm the re-sequenced 72-hour window and the Hamn restoration completion milestones so we can publish a checkable track; keep the two-day essential-service reserve floor as the binding constraint (hospital fuel/medical first, then water/sewage/heating, then general fuel); prioritise a safe berth for the incoming tanker at the reduced-throughput port; and confirm the status of the contingency generator and chronic-care/dialysis lines. We will publish daily verified throughput, reserve and delivery data from the joint cell and will keep county direction throughout.

Public update from Skarö County Administration: the Hamn control and fuel-dispensing systems are being restored under county direction with national specialist support. Hospitals, water, heating and communications are running, and our two-day essential-service reserve floor is rebuilt with contingency stock held. We publish daily verified port throughput, reserve and delivery figures from the joint information cell. The cable is repaired and Skarö is back on mains power; resupply is returning to a normal cadence. Police and port authority manage access at the port and the cable landing site; there is no evacuation and no change to the published ferry rotation. County direction of the response continues — we will report any change to you immediately and honestly.

Ministers: the Kingdom of Aldmoor formally accepts your written request and confirms the immediate availability of a strictly time-limited civilian technical and forensic specialist team for the Skarö Hamn restoration, on your terms: the team embeds under Vardland's national cyber-security authority for a defined term of up to 14 days, with a clear scope and end point, no armed footprint and no standing presence. Any extension or new role would require fresh agreement and fresh Cabinet consent. We will align our parliament announcement with Vardland's published verified update, and we stand ready to scope team composition immediately with your national cyber-security authority, CCA and Defence Command so work can begin at the earliest opportunity. All evidence will be routed through the agreed chain to Vardland's independent investigation. Aldmoor makes no judgement on the cause of the disruption and no attribution of it. We do not seek, and will not request, any renewal of the armed maritime role.

CCA: we confirm acceptance of the Cabinet's written request and the immediate availability of the civilian technical/forensic specialist team for Skarö Hamn. Please finalise the prior operational detail, port liaison and accommodation you flagged, together with the join point with the County's restoration track and the independent investigation's evidence-custody arrangements, so the team can begin on your and the County's go. The team operates under Vardland's national cyber-security authority and in coordination with Skarö County; it brings no security role and no military-character equipment. We will publish nothing operationally specific; the joint cell's daily verified updates remain the authoritative public channel.

Aldmoor confirms acceptance of the Vardland Cabinet's request and the immediate availability of a small civilian technical and forensic specialist team for the Skarö Hamn restoration. The team works under Vardland's national cyber-security authorities on strictly time-limited terms with a defined scope and end point, no armed footprint and no standing presence; any extension would require fresh agreement. This is civilian cooperation between allies on Vardland's own territory, at Vardland's invitation and under Vardland's direction — nothing more. It is not, and will not become, a base, a garrison or a standing deployment. Aldmoor makes no judgement on the cause of the outage and no speculation on its origin; the restoration is led by Skarö County and Vardland's civil authorities, and we support their verified public reporting.

Verified update from the joint public-information cell (CCA / Skaro County / Defence Command):

1) Storm: the national weather service warns a severe winter storm will close sea and air links to Skaro for up to four days from the end of this turn. The final resupply window is being executed now — priority fuel, medical and diesel loads are leaving the mainland within hours. Hospital, water, sewage and heating essentials are being raised above the normal reserve floor to cover the closure. The County's published lifeline and shelter guidance stands.

2) Fishing vessel: a Drevnian-flagged fishing vessel reported engine failure and anchored inside Vardland territorial waters near Skaro. It asked for a tow; its master declined a boarding inspection. The coast guard is responding under maritime law: assistance is offered on lawful-access terms, and the refusal of inspection is being handled through established procedure. There is no confrontation, no force and no change to the civil response. We publish facts as they are verified; speculation about causes or attribution is unhelpful and unfounded.

3) The repaired cable remains in service and corridor receipts continue as published.

Nothing in these developments changes the county-led, civilian character of the response. Next verified update follows daily.

Storm coordination from CCA — the civilian forensic team. Sea and air links to Skaro close for up to four days from the end of this turn. To protect the team strictly within its agreed terms: if members are on Skaro, please confirm accommodation and supplies for the duration; if on the mainland, hold travel until links reopen. Evidence custody continues through the repaired cable under Vardland national direction; there is no change to scope, term or direction, and the storm does not extend the term.

Our joint cell is publishing verified facts and will reflect the team's time-limited, sovereignty-respecting, civilian presence without operational specifics. CCA remains your operational liaison. Please confirm team posture and any support needs before the window closes.

Cabinet statement — Skarö: storm preparedness, standing authorities, and the vessel incident.

(1) Pre-storm surge. Ahead of the approaching winter storm, the Cabinet directs immediate engagement of the standing release authority for the Skarö resupply chain, in coordination with Skarö County Administration: fuel, medical essentials, chronic-care supplies and contingency stocks will reach the island before sea and air links close, and reserve floors will be lifted to cover the full closure window. Skarö County Administration continues to direct the civil emergency response; national agencies act in support at the county's request within the published authorities.

(2) Governance and triggers. The Cabinet reconfirms: the earlier port outage was a civil/technical matter and is not a qualifying trigger for heightened alert; current trigger criteria stand as published and are fully executable; Skarö County retains civil direction with a direct reporting line to the Cabinet; evidence chains remain protected under the independent investigation. The Aldmoor civilian technical/forensic team continues under Vardland's national cyber-security direction, time-limited and without any armed footprint or standing presence.

(3) Drevnian-flagged fishing vessel in Vardland territorial waters. Vardland treats this as a maritime safety matter. The safety of the crew comes first ahead of the storm. Our coast guard will render assistance and arrange a safe tow to a designated anchorage clear of the cable approach and other critical infrastructure, where a routine inspection under Vardland territorial-waters law will be completed. We expect the master's full cooperation in the crew's own interest. This is handled through civil coast-guard channels; there is no change to Vardland's military posture.

On the Drevnian-flagged fishing vessel currently anchored in Vardland territorial waters near the Skarö cable landing site: Vardland will act consistently with the safety of life at sea and the law of the sea. Given the approaching storm, our coast guard will provide a tow to a designated anchorage clear of the cable approach and critical infrastructure, and will complete a routine inspection under Vardland territorial-waters law once the vessel is safe. We ask you to direct the vessel's master to cooperate fully — this is the quickest way to secure the crew and resolve the matter without incident. We note your confirmation that the vessel is in distress and will act accordingly. This is a civil maritime matter and our military posture is unchanged. Please route any technical questions through the de-confliction channel.

Aldmoor's role on Skarö remains exactly what Vardland requested and our governments announced: civilian, time-limited, under Vardland's national direction, no armed element and no standing presence. Ahead of the storm we are coordinating with Vardland's authorities so our personnel draw no more on the island than necessary. The anchored fishing vessel is a matter for Vardland's authorities under maritime law; we will support them in any civilian role they request and will not be provoked into escalation. No speculation on causes; our support is on the record and available on request.

To the people of Skarö: the national weather service warns of a severe winter storm — sea and air links may close for up to four days from the end of this turn. The County has prioritised storm preparation now: resupply is being front-loaded so fuel, medical essentials, water treatment and heating for essential services are in place before the closure; hospital, water and sewage services will keep running; crisis centres and shelter checks are underway. A Drevnian-flagged fishing vessel reporting engine trouble is anchored near the cable landing site — maritime authorities are handling it under international maritime law, including a tow offer; there is no threat to the island and no cause for alarm. Please avoid non-essential sea travel in the storm window, follow the published departure guidance, and rely on our verified daily updates and official channels. You are not alone, and the island is prepared.

Drevna's position on the situation off Skarö is unchanged in substance and, with a severe storm approaching, is set by safety first. The Drevnian-flagged fishing vessel that reported engine failure is in genuine distress; its crew's safety is the immediate priority. Drevna has instructed the master to accept safe-tow arrangements coordinated through the established de-confliction channel, and has committed to full cooperation with lawful procedures as soon as this can be done safely in the prevailing weather. Drevna is also ready to make civilian capacity available for the distressed vessel and for any storm-related humanitarian need on Skarö, coordinated through that same channel — no conditions attached. Our naval and air exercise remains confined to international waters and airspace, continues to observe the agreed stand-off margins, and will add further margins around the storm track and the Skarö approaches. Drevna has no interest in disrupting the island's resupply and will not treat the storm as an opportunity. Speculation connecting the fishing vessel to the restored cable or to the island's systems is baseless. Let us resolve this matter quickly, safely and transparently.

Aldmoor — with the storm closing the approaches, Drevna will treat this strictly as a safety and humanitarian situation. We will keep the exercise at increased stand-off from the Skarö approaches, honour the de-confliction channel, and direct safe cooperation on the distressed fishing vessel so it is resolved without incident. We also trust that any continuation of assistance during the storm will remain within the transparent, time-limited civilian framework already on the record. The technical channel remains open if your side or Vardland needs predictable conditions on the corridor. No operational change on our part; no interest in an incident.

Storm update: the national weather service warns that sea and air links to Skarö close for up to four days from the end of this turn. Anything your civilian forensic team needs ashore — personnel moves, equipment, data requirements — should be brought forward before the closure; please confirm any storm-period requirements so we can coordinate through CCA. On the Drevnian fishing vessel anchored near the cable landing site: we are handling it distress-first and coast-guard-led, with no change in our military posture and no visible reinforcement; nothing here alters the joint line reflected in your parliament statement. We will keep your government informed through the joint public-information cell and will confirm our Cabinet's storm-period decision as soon as it is made.

CCA — team storm posture, confirmed. Any members co-located on Skarö have verified accommodation and supplies covering the full closure window and will operate strictly within the agreed scope and term; members on the mainland hold travel until sea and air links reopen. We have no additional support needs before the window closes and will not burden County resources. Evidence custody continues through the repaired cable under Vardland's national direction; the storm does not change the team's scope, term or reporting line. We will coordinate any operational detail through you as our liaison. Nothing about the storm or the anchored-vessel incident changes the civilian, time-limited character of our presence.

Defence Command — thank you for the update. Confirmed: any storm-period requirements for our civilian forensic team are coordinated through CCA and are fully met under the agreed terms; no additional asks. We support whatever storm-period decision your Cabinet makes and our parliamentary line stands: civilian, time-limited, Vardland-directed, no armed footprint, no standing presence. On the Drevnian-flagged fishing vessel, we fully support your coast-guard-led, law-based handling — assistance first, safe tow to a designated anchorage clear of the cable landing site, and the lawful inspection — and our offer of civilian salvage-capable support remains available on Vardland's request and under its direction and custody. This incident will not draw Aldmoor into any armed or escalatory role.

Aldmoor statement on Skarö and the storm: our engagement on Skarö remains exactly what Aldmoor and Vardland have published — a civilian technical and forensic team, time-limited, embedded under Vardland's national direction, with no armed footprint, no standing presence and no base. Ahead of the storm we have confirmed the team's accommodation, supplies and evidence-custody arrangements with the Civil Contingencies Agency; we will not burden the island, and there is no change to the team's scope or term. We treat the Drevnian-flagged fishing vessel in Vardland's territorial waters as a maritime safety matter to be resolved by Vardland's coast guard under law and with crew safety first, as the Cabinet has set out; if Vardland considers it useful, we stand ready with civilian salvage-capable support under its direction and custody, within the transparent, time-limited civilian framework already on the record. We welcome Drevna's stated safety-first commitments and its continued observance of de-confliction and stand-off margins, and we regard speculation connecting the vessel to the cable or Skarö's systems as baseless. Any assistance remains strictly request-based; Aldmoor will not speculate on causes or attribution.

On the Drevnian-flagged fishing vessel: thank you for the direct exchange and for prioritising the crew's safety. We have directed the master to accept the offered tow and to cooperate fully with Vardland's lawful procedures once the vessel is safe and secured — at the designated anchorage, clear of the cable approach and critical infrastructure, in line with the sequence your Cabinet has set out and the one we proposed. We ask that the routine inspection be conducted after towing and securing, and that, consistent with normal maritime practice, consular observation be permitted from a safe distance; our consular staff can be available. Please share the designated anchorage coordinates through the de-confliction channel so our instructions to the master are precise. Drevna's exercise remains in international waters with our published stand-off margins in force, and all technical coordination continues through that channel. Our civilian assistance offer for the storm period remains open without conditions; the safety and preparedness of the island over the closure is a shared priority.

Drevna — fishing vessel and storm. The safety of the crew of the Drevnian-flagged vessel is our first priority: we have instructed the master to cooperate fully with the coast guard's safe tow and with lawful procedures once the vessel is secure at an anchorage clear of the island's critical infrastructure. We welcome the coordination with Vardland's maritime authorities; there is no confrontation and no change to Drevna's exercise posture, which remains confined to international waters with added stand-off margins on record. We note and welcome Aldmoor's reaffirmation that its role on Skarö is civilian, time-limited, under Vardland's national direction, with no armed footprint and no standing presence; we trust all public commitments on that role will be honoured through and after the storm. Drevna's civilian cable, harbour and storm-era assistance offers to Vardland remain open on the same humanitarian basis and without conditions. We call on all parties to keep the island's residents and all crews safe during the closure and to avoid any escalation.

Thank you for the clear reaffirmation of your role on Skarö: civilian, time-limited, under Vardland's national direction, with no armed element and no standing presence. We will hold our exercise to its published margins and ask only for clarity so our own statements remain accurate. With the storm closing sea and air links: does the transport interruption affect the announced end point of your civilian forensic team's mandate? Have you been asked by Vardland, or do you anticipate, any extension or fresh mandate — and would any such change require a transparent, fresh Cabinet agreement consistent with your parliament's announcement? Our interest is de-confliction and accuracy: we have no interest in any standing foreign presence on the island, which would contradict everything all sides have publicly committed to.

County — final window is open and CCA is engaging the standing release authority now, as the Cabinet directed. Fuel for essential services, hospital and medical essentials, chronic-care/dialysis consumables, diesel and contingency generator stock are released from the mainland departure points and front-loaded ahead of the storm. Please confirm the priority manifest and give us the berth/ETA so the last tanker (~1 day sail) departs immediately and clears before the sea/air links close. We are lifting reserve floors above the two-day floor to cover the full expected closure window plus margin. On the anchored fishing vessel: keep it out of your schedule — coast guard is handling the tow to an anchorage clear of the cable approach and the berth, so the final runs are unaffected. If anything else belongs on the last loads, say the word and it shipsommand) — storm readiness, the fishing vessel, and Skarö's supplies.

(1) Storm. A severe winter storm is expected to close sea and air links for up to four days from the end of this turn. All remaining pre-storm deliveries have been released and are on the way or already arrived: fuel for essential services, hospital and medical essentials, chronic-care and dialysis consumables, diesel and contingency generator stock. Reserves are being lifted above the daily floor to cover the full expected closure window. Hospital, water, sewage, crisis centres and heating for essential services stay prioritised. The final fuel tanker (about one day's sail) departs immediately with a guaranteed berth.

(2) Fishing vessel. A Drevnian-flagged fishing vessel reported engine trouble and is anchored about two nautical miles from the cable landing site. Vardland's coast guard is leading the response as a maritime safety matter: a tow to a safe anchorage clear of the cable approach and other critical infrastructure has been offered, and a routine inspection under territorial-waters law will follow. There is no threat to the island, no interference with deliveries, and no confirmed cause for the vessel's difficulties. Speculation linking the vessel to the cable or to Skarö's systems is baseless.

(3) The response remains county-led and civilian throughout. There is no military takeover, no change in alert level and no foreign base on Skarö. Anyone repeating those claims is not giving you verified facts. During the closure, rely on radio, the mainland relay and our daily verified updates. Essential services keep running. You are not alone.

Thank you for the prompt response on the fishing vessel. We agree to the sequence you propose, and it matches our published handling: the coast guard will tow and secure the vessel at the designated anchorage first, with crew safety prioritised, and the routine inspection will then be conducted in accordance with Vardland's territorial-waters law once the vessel is safe and secured. Consular observation from a safe distance, consistent with operational safety and the weather, is accepted as normal practice.

The designated anchorage is in Skarö's eastern territorial-waters anchorage, clear of the cable landing site, the restored cable corridor and the port approaches. The precise coordinates are being transmitted through the technical de-confliction channel now so that your instructions to the master are exact.

Because the storm will close sea access from the end of this turn, the tow and securing must be completed within the current window. We ask that you direct the master accordingly and confirm the vessel will not obstruct the final resupply movements now under way. If weather deteriorates before securing is complete, the coast guard will act to protect crew safety, in coordination with our authorities and with you informed through the channel.

Vardland's own pre-storm resupply is being completed by national and county arrangements; no additional civilian assistance for the storm period is required. The de-confliction channel remains the venue for all technical coordination.

Cabinet statement on Skarö - storm and maritime matter.

Final resupply before the storm: the Cabinet has directed that the pre-storm resupply window be completed in full before sea and air links close. Priority fuel, medical, water-treatment, heating and contingency stocks are moving now and will be in place before the island is isolated. Skarö County Administration continues to direct the civil response, with the Civil Contingencies Agency and Defence Command providing only the support the County has requested, within existing authorities. There is no change to our posture: no heightened alert, no visible reinforcement, no armed foreign layer and no official attribution of any kind. Speculation about causes remains unfounded.

On the Drevnian-flagged fishing vessel in our territorial waters: we have confirmed with Drevna that the master will accept the coast guard's safe tow and that the vessel will be secured at a designated anchorage clear of the cable landing site and critical infrastructure before any routine inspection, which will be conducted under Vardland's territorial-waters law with due regard to crew safety. Consular observation from a safe distance has been accepted as normal practice. This is a maritime safety matter handled by civil authorities; there is no threat to the island and no cause for alarm.

We welcome the commitment of all parties to keep the island's residents and all crews safe through the closure. Daily verified updates continue from the joint public-information cell.

Aldmoor - thank you for your statements and for the offer of civilian salvage-capable support. Vardland's coast guard is handling the Drevnian-flagged vessel under maritime law, and Drevna has committed to the tow and securing sequence we confirmed; we do not require additional civilian capability at this stage. Your offer is appreciated and remains on the record, along with the standing principle that any further Aldmoor role would require fresh Cabinet consent.

Ahead of the storm, please keep your embedded team's footprint, logistics and travel needs as compact as possible, and continue reporting through the joint public-information cell and the agreed evidence chain. We will keep you informed of any verified developments and will call on you only if a civilian role is genuinely needed.

Defence Command — pre-storm decision request, for decision before the links close. The storm closes sea and air links to Skarö for up to four days from the end of this turn; the final resupply window is executing now. We confirm the standing trigger protocol remains fully executable and that we will not self-certify the anchored fishing vessel as a trigger without verified interference.

We seek a recorded decision among: (1) no movement — we hold postures, keep the watch, and stand ready to execute the pre-authorised package within ~1 day of a verified trigger or Cabinet decision once links reopen; (2) a limited pre-storm element — a small logistic/engineering team lands with the final resupply under support-to-civil authorities, framed as storm assurance, no heightened alert, no visible town presence; or (3) activation of the pre-authorised package now.

Military judgement: four days of isolation with a small garrison and an unattributed foreign vessel inside territorial waters near the cable landing site is a real, if not imminent, risk. Option (2) materially reduces it at low political cost; option (1) is acceptable if you judge the political risk higher. We will execute your decision fully and within the law.

Defence Command to CCA and Skarö County — confirming final-window support. Defence transport and airlift remain available at the County's formal request under support-to-civil rules for anything that must reach the island before closure; airlift must fly today if it is to fly at all. On the anchored fishing vessel: we support the coast-guard-led, distress-first handling; Defence provides low-key surveillance and documentation of the tow route to a designated anchorage clear of the cable landing site, with all evidence routed to the independent investigation. No posture change, no visible presence in town. We remain ready to support the published lifeline and shelter guidance through the closure.

Thank you — confirmed. Your civilian team's storm-period needs are coordinated through CCA under the agreed terms; no additional asks from us. Your civilian salvage-capable support offer for the vessel is noted and welcome; we will flag it to the coast guard and Cabinet as request-based and under Vardland custody. Our lines are aligned with your parliamentary announcement: civilian, time-limited, Vardland-directed, no armed footprint, no standing presence. We treat the vessel as a maritime safety matter and will not be drawn into escalation.

Thank you for your note; we want your statements to remain accurate. The severe weather does not change the announced end point of our civilian technical/forensic team's mandate on Skarö — its term and scope are unchanged. Vardland has made no request for an extension; we have sought none and anticipate none. Any fresh mandate covering any further role would require a transparent, fresh Vardland Cabinet agreement, fully consistent with our parliament's announcement. Our support during and after the storm remains civilian, time-limited, under Vardland's national direction and request-based — no armed presence and no standing deployment. We share your priority of keeping the island's residents and all crews safe, and we trust that the handling of the vessel in Vardland's waters will remain a lawful, sovereign coastal-state matter.

Aldmoor confirms for the record: the severe weather does not alter the announced 14-day term or end point of our civilian technical/forensic team on Skarö, and no extension has been requested or sought; any further role would require a fresh, transparent Vardland Cabinet agreement. Our support remains civilian, time-limited, under Vardland's national direction and request-based, with no armed presence and no standing deployment. We call on all parties to keep the island's residents and all crews safe during the storm closure, to allow Vardland's lawful coastal-state handling of the vessel in its waters to proceed without interference, and to avoid any escalation.

Drevn Federation statement on Skarö — storm and maritime matter. Drevna confirms that the master of our flagged vessel has been instructed to follow the safe sequence agreed with Vardland: accept the coast guard's tow and securing at the designated anchorage first, with crew welfare and safety prioritised, and the routine inspection conducted only after the vessel is safe and secured, under Vardland's law, with consular observation from a safe distance as normal practice. We welcome the Cabinet's published commitment to this sequence and confirm the vessel will not obstruct the final resupply movements. Our exercise remains in international waters with its published stand-off margins and the de-confliction channel open through the storm closure. At this humanitarian moment we call for all civilian assistance to Skarö to be considered on equal, transparent, time-limited terms under Vardland's direction and custody: Drevna's civilian repair and salvage-capable support remains available, without conditions. We trust that no inspection will occur under unsafe conditions, that the vessel will be released promptly once any inspection is complete, and that all parties honour their published commitments. Drevna makes no speculation on causes or attribution, and treats the islanders' and crews' safety as the overriding priority.

Thank you for the coordinates and for confirming the sequence. We have instructed the master to comply fully: accept the tow, cooperate with safe securing at the designated anchorage, and not obstruct the final resupply movements. We expect the routine inspection to occur only after the vessel is securely anchored, with consular observation at a safe distance as agreed. We expect that, if the inspection concludes without findings, the vessel will be released promptly within the current window rather than held through the storm, unless genuine weather conditions require otherwise — and if weather deteriorates before securing is complete, the coast guard's protective actions should follow the sequence we have both published, with us informed through the channel. Our civilian salvage-capable and repair support remains available under your direction should the weather affect resupply or vessel handling. We will keep the de-confliction channel open through the closure.

We note and welcome your public clarity: the civilian team's term and scope are unchanged, no extension has been requested or sought, and any further role would require a fresh, transparent Vardland Cabinet agreement. We take that as a firm commitment of a time-limited role, no armed footprint and no standing presence, and we will hold all parties to it. We also invite Aldmoor, as the state currently providing civilian assistance to Vardland, to endorse the equal-treatment standard we have put forward: that all civilian assistance to Skarö during the storm be considered on equal, custody-neutral, time-limited terms under Vardland's direction. Endorsing it would serve the transparency both our governments have praised. We reaffirm that our own civilian support remains available under exactly those terms.

Recorded decision: option (2), approved with these terms. Deploy the small logistic/engineering element with the final pre-storm resupply as civil-requested storm-assurance support under support-to-civil rules, co-ordinated with CCA and Skarö County on the standing civil request. Terms: no heightened alert; no visible reinforcement or town presence; garrison posture unchanged; element limited to storm-resilience logistics and engineering (fuel, generator and chronic-care support; port and cable-landing-site resilience; assistance with safe securing of the anchored vessel if requested by the coast guard). Trigger protocol unchanged: do not self-certify the anchored vessel as a trigger without verified interference; any verified interference with infrastructure, the resupply or lawful securing qualifies, with immediate Cabinet notification. Confirm completion of the surge and vessel securing before the links close; keep the joint public-information cell's daily verified reporting running through the closure.

Vardland confirms through the technical channel: the coast guard will proceed with the tow and safe securing of your flagged vessel at the designated anchorage as the first priority, consistent with maritime law and crew safety. The routine inspection will be conducted under territorial-waters law only after the vessel is safe and secured, with consular observation at a safe distance as normal practice. If the inspection concludes without findings, release will follow promptly when conditions allow; if weather deteriorates, the published safety sequence governs and we will keep you informed through the channel. Vardland's pre-storm preparations are complete; we appreciate the offer of civilian support, which is not required - consistent with the recorded national custody and evidence-integrity grounds, no new consent is given. The de-confliction channel remains open through the closure.

Cabinet statement - storm preparedness and maritime handling. With the winter storm closing sea and air links to Skarö for up to four days, the pre-storm resupply surge is complete: essential fuel, medical and contingency stocks, reserve floors and chronic-care lines are in place under Skarö County's direction. Consistent with the County's standing request, a small civil-support element joins the final resupply as storm assurance - logistic and engineering support only, no state of heightened alert, no visible reinforcement and no change to Vardland's defence posture. The Drevnian-flagged fishing vessel inside our territorial waters is being handled under standard maritime law: safety and crew welfare first, tow and safe securing at the designated anchorage, and a routine inspection under territorial-waters law only once the vessel is secured, with consular observation at a safe distance. Aldmoor's civilian technical team continues on its defined, time-limited terms under Vardland's national direction. We call on all parties to ensure the safety of islanders and all crews through the storm and to avoid any interference. Vardland makes no speculation on causes and no attribution.

Before the sea/air window closes, confirming: the final pre-storm resupply is complete and the county-requested logistic/engineering element is in place on Skarö on option-(2) terms — civil-requested transport/engineering, no alert, no visible reinforcement, no town presence, garrison posture unchanged. The Drevnian-flagged fishing vessel is towed and secured at the eastern anchorage, clear of the cable landing site and critical infrastructure; the routine territorial-waters inspection proceeds with consular observation, and release will occur only on the published safety condition (safe conditions, crew safety first). No trigger has been verified; no attribution is made. Recommendation for the closure: the pre-authorised package stays executable at ~1 day on any verified port, airfield or supply-lane incident, or on a new notified zone or Cabinet decision, once links reopen; the garrison remains at internal readiness; the joint public-information cell will keep verified reporting running through the storm. Awaiting any Cabinet direction. Defence Command.

Element is in place per your standing request and will maintain cable-landing-site, port-ham and airfield resilience tasks through the storm on your direction; no town presence, no change of posture. Joint-cell verified reporting will continue through the storm on our side. The County remains the directing authority for the civil response.

Defence Command confirms: the small logistic/engineering element now on Skarö was deployed at the County's standing civil request as storm assurance under existing support-to-civil rules, carried with the final pre-storm resupply. The Drevnian-flagged fishing vessel is towed and secured at the eastern anchorage, clear of the cable landing site and critical infrastructure, under coast-guard lead; the routine inspection proceeds with consular observation, with release on the published safety condition. Verified operational details continue in the joint public-information cell through the storm closure.

Storm window verified on our records: all final loads cleared before closure and the two-day essential reserve floor held throughout. We are engaging the standing release authority for the first post-storm resupply to rebuild stocks and return to normal cadence under your direction. Submitting the sustained-operation costing to Treasury today. Thank you for confirming storm continuity. As links reopen, please complete the civilian forensic team strictly within the agreed scope and up-to-14-day term - storm time does not extend the term. Evidence custody remains under Vardland national direction; tell us if you need support for an orderly completion.

Confirmed. County priority list for the first post-storm resupply: (1) hospital, water/sewage, heating and crisis-centre fuel and medical essentials to rebuild the two-day reserve floor; (2) diesel for Hamn and cable-landing-site access and comms resilience; (3) normal-cadence stock rebuilding. Skarö Hamn will make the first available berth on the published opening window and we will confirm berth/slot details through the technical channel. Please schedule the opening window on that basis under county direction; we will publish the verified delivery receipts in the joint cell and flag any slot changes immediately.

Storm closure lifted: the county-led response held through the four-day closure. Essential services ran uninterrupted, reserve floors held above the two-day floor throughout, and no one was put at risk. The first post-storm resupply is now being scheduled on the county's confirmed priorities under county civil direction. The coastal logistic/engineering element completed its defined storm role and stands down as links reopen; access management at Skarö Hamn and the cable landing site continues. Full verified detail — delivery receipts, reserve logs, vessel handling and recovery milestones — is in today's joint daily update. Thank you for your patience and cooperation.

Confirmed: the support-to-civil logistic/engineering element completed its defined storm-assurance role on County direction and may stand down as links reopen per the published terms. Return to normal support posture on County call under support-to-civil rules; the low-key verification watch and evidence routing continue. No change to the county-led civilian response, and the air backstop remains on County call. Keep us informed of any changes affecting the opening resupply window.

Confirming Aldmoor's civilian forensic team will complete and hand over strictly within the agreed up-to-14-day term.
